I received my copy from the publisher through Love Romances.Trent Savage, Sav, is the drummer in Lyric Hound, a very popular band, consisting of Werewolf musicians. For as long as he can remember he’s been attracted to Karlan Rixx, the band’s guitarist. What’s more, for years he has known that Karlan is his preordained mate. Karlan however is as straight as they come and, as far as Sav can tell, completely unaware of or ignoring Sav’s feelings as well as the bond between them.After years of trying to deny his feelings just to hold on to Karlan’s friendship, Sav can’t take it anymore and leaves the band as well as the only life and family he’s ever known.Karlan may be a womanizer, in his heart there is only one person he’s interested in. When Sav disappears Karlan feels lost. The band isn’t the same with Sav to drive the beat and Karlan’s life is incomplete without the man behind him on stage, next to him in life.When he discovers that Sav has contacted Madame Eve to organize a one night stand, Karlan does what he can to be Sav’s date. There was a reason Karlan didn’t know he and Sav were mated. With Karlan’s problem solved both man are in for a few surprises when they meet again. But will it be enough for them to embrace their destiny?Allow me to start with a few qualifiers. I’ve never read a One Night Stand or Lyric Hound story before. I don’t read a lot of supernatural stories, erotic or otherwise and, I very often find myself having issues with novellas. For all intents and purposes requesting this book for review seemed to be an exercise in setting myself up for failure.Imagine how happily surprised I was to discover that being new to the One Night Stand series and Lyric Hound stories didn’t make a difference. I fell into and was captured by this story from the very first word and stayed hooked until I’d finished the last one. What’s not too like? We’re meeting Sav, a sexy and dominant werewolf rock star who, despite his rough exterior is breaking up inside because his mate appears to be rejecting him. And, not only do we get to enjoy this hunk, we’re also treated to Karlan, and equally hot werewolf. The reader is being spoiled.Talking about werewolves; I’ve obviously been missing something while ignoring supernatural (erotic) stories. If this story sets the standard, this is a discrepancy I’ll be fixing in the not too distant future, very likely starting with the other Lyric Hound stories.As far as the fact that this is a novella rather than a full novel is concerned all I can say is that I was very impressed. This was as complete a story as any reader can wish for. The characters are well described and fully fleshed, there’s enough back story to give the reader not only everything they need to know but also a real connection to the character’s feelings and actions. This story may only have counted 35 pages, it provided everything a good story needs: a beginning that puts the reader straight into the story, a middle that provided all the explanations needed without slowing the story down and a beautiful and very satisfying ending.And did I mention this story is hot? Well, it is. But then, that’s exactly what you would expect when you pick up a story about two Alpha werewolves giving in to their feelings for each other after years of having to deny then.This in short was about an hour’s worth of pure reading delight, leaving me with yet another author I have to add to my must-read list.

This is one of several of Chris Nuttall's books I have read, and "Invasion" was better done than others. I tend to judge science fiction story lines differently based on the degree of disbelief I have to suspend. Because this book tells a story that can be said to be a possible future for our planet, there wasn't all that much suspension of disbelief required. That said, I spent the first three quarters of reading time feeling vaguely anxious and generally creeped out. That, I believe, usually suggests to me that I like what I'm reading and the author has done a very good job.There is an obvious parallel between the Takaina's mission and Radical Fundamentalist Islamic Jihad (and the Spanish Inquisition), not specific beliefs per se, but the whole "kill the infidel, burn the witch/heretic" mind-set. At first I thought it was "too easy" a device to use as the reason why one billion reddish-purple, four-hearted jelly legged aliens and their Priests and Inquisitors flew 100 million light years to "convert" us Earthlings, but it actually works, after you get over quibbling at plot devices. (Spoiler Alert) Although I did think that when the Takaina decide to accept the Middle East as one of their "Most Desirable Places to Live" and end up potentially being the new "Oil Barons", it was sort of overkill.Anyhow, a good, creepy alien invasion story, and a good way to illustrate that NASA/ESA really need to get their collective acts together (and taxpayers of the planet need to fund that "act") so that the people of Earth can harvest the riches of space instead of raping the (declining) riches of the planet, a point made often in the story line by alien and human characters alike. I would probably add another half-star, but can't.
summary: Creepy. Which is a Good Thing.,

Angelique's Review"Dragon Mine" takes place in an alternate reality where women are almost extinct. It touches on recovering from past pain and abuse to move forward. Ms. Flynn crafts a unique world of consuming love, searing lust, and a dragon shifter.Gabe is by far my favorite character in this novella. He is strong, brave, and loyal to his men. Watching him fall in love with the guys is heartwarming.The love scenes in this story were uber steamy and the sexual tension was so thick, you could slice it like bread. Illusion was not what I was expecting, it had quite a twist that looking back on it, I should have figured out what said twist was, but I didn't. I am in a state of wow, I loved the entire story, from the prologue all the way to the last page. The writing is beautifully done, I really adored this book.When the story begins Zoey is at the funeral for her fiancé, Kirt. It was heartbreaking and so well written and packed such an emotional punch that I was pulled in, continuing to read until I reached the very end. A year after the death of Kirt, Zoey gets a job in New York City, in hopes of healing and finding a way to move on with her life, she embarks on this new journey. On her first day in the city she meets Harvey, a local tour guide. In a roundabout and slightly serendipitous way, her and Harvey continue to connect which propels them into her first relationship since Kirt's death.Along the way she meets Brice, the IT guy at work and the way she meets him had me laughing hysterically. Through emails to her sister Em, from her work computer, Brice without her knowledge reads her emails and introduces himself, after that it gets very funny as Zoey and Em write to each other and include Brice in their conversations. Sparking a friendship and ultimately a love that left me smiling and crossing my fingers that they would get a happy ending.And that's when everything becomes very intriguing, heartbreaking, stunning and absolutely gorgeous. I do not want to give spoilers so I am not going to say any more about the plot. I will say this, it left me stunned and slightly shaking my head and wanting to email the author and express my awe at how she weaved the entire plot of Illusion.There is humor interlaced with the serious but it definitely deals with some very heavy issues that include depression, death, PTSD, and attempted suicide. Ultimately this is a book with a lot of heart, some very steamy moments, two love stories and the hope that comes with finding love again and choosing to live your life.I loved this book and it is definitely going on my list of best books of 2014. Ashley Beale has written an incredible story. Now go read it :)I received an ARC in exchange for an honest review.Originally posted on Me, Myself & Books Blog

It's not a bad book, per se, though personally I was unable to finish it.  The story concept is not too bad, though not particularly original.  Here are my thoughts overall:=> Writing style.  The book is written at a fairly low level.  At first I assumed that the author was extremely young, or that this was one of his first books, but reading his bio it appears that this isn't the case.  I guess the book is simply targeted at young readers, and I didn't realize that when I bought it.=> Inconsistent Tech.  Sure, I know it's science fiction and some level of suspension of disbelief is required, but it detracts from the experience if the author knows less about basic science than I do.  Putting a cover over a robot's battery prevents EMP damage?  Lots of little stuff like that on almost every page.  Almost every technical aspect is off.  Its more immersive if it makes at least a little sense.  Saves a lot of head scratching.  If you don't care about nonsensical technology, then perhaps this wouldn't bother you as it did me.=> One dimensional characters.  The characters are too simplistic to develop any rapport with.=> Unoriginal story.  The story line wasn't bad, but there was pretty much nothing original about it.  If the story was original or gripping I might have stuck with it, even with the myriad of other flaws in the book.Overall, I'd have to say I wouldn't recommend it - unless you are a boy in the 12-15 age group, in which case you'll probably like it more than I did.
summary: It's not a bad book, per se

Amy Lane brought me a fairy tale for Christmas. Well, a contemporary fairy tale, to be sure, but it embodied the soul of a classic. "Once upon a time, there was a prince who lived in a tower. He had been born to a king and a queen in the kingdom of San Francisco, and he was raised by nannies and boarding schools. He was a good child. He did everything he was told. He never questioned his world, and his rebellions, on the whole, were very, very small." And so began the story of Zach and how he finally got his knight to rescue him from his tower.Zach is sad, but he doesn't even know it, and that probably makes it even more sorrowful. Someone looking in at his life might wonder what he has to be sad about. He was born with a silver spoon in his mouth, was educated at the best schools, is wealthy, owns his own law firm handling union violations, and lives in a gorgeous penthouse. He has no one to share his life with, though. No close friends, and certainly not a boyfriend since he's hidden that part of himself from his parents his whole life. He isn't close with his parents and I don't blame him for that. They are the type of people to care more about society than the happiness of their only child. So it comes as a bit of a shock to his system when he realizes that after running into the same guy in the elevator, twice, that Zach is smiling, of all things.Sean is a teacher, looking for a job and sharing an apartment in Zach's building with five other people. Sean does a lot of substitute work while looking for a full time job and I'd have loved having a teacher like him in the eighth grade! He dresses for his students depending on what he's teaching and that gives him and Zach stuff to talk about while they ride the elevator together. Well, that and the outfits he has to wear doing singing telegrams for money. *snort* Of course, Sean doesn't know that Zach has been timing his leaving just so he can share the elevator with Sean. The part where Zach tells his parents he's gay, at a fundraiser for his father's Republican political campaign, was priceless and I loved it. Nobody should ever have to hide who they are.I love that there are always, and I mean always, phenomenal secondary characters in this author's work. The problem? Then I want books about them, even if they're heterosexual! Leah is Zach's secretary and, in my opinion, she and his infrequent elevator dates with Sean are part of the reason the prince begins to venture away from his frozen tower. She is amazing and becomes Zach's first real friend he's ever had, which gives him the courage to open up a little, to smile more, to break out of his cocoon. Not to mention that Leah and her roommate are giving Zach an education in…ummm…how should I say it? Vulgarity? Women? "Leah moved around him but her arms stayed firmly planted at his ribs. 'God you're short,' he said, wondering how he'd managed to work with her for three years and live without the hugs and the companionship and the crude sense of humor and the best friend who made him laugh.""He couldn't explain it. He couldn't. It was like his entire life, he'd thought he knew what breathing was, what pleasurable meant, what human connection could be. He was wrong. So, so far off the mark, so far short of what the world was about." Zach got his knight in shining armor and Sean got to save his prince from the tower. And, how do all those tales end? Oh yeah. They lived happily ever after.

reviewText: What you’ve got here is a writer at the top of his game, writing about issues he is clearly passionate about. Add to that mix, a story of understated power and the result is what one reviewer described as a masterpiece. I agree completely.The poignant story is told with some truly elegant and clever writing and I was gripped immediately. The story itself deals with issues which sadly will be forever relevant in society. I for one found some relevancies in my own life, perhaps not in the way the author intended but I think this shows how strong a book this actually is.There is an impending sense of doom throughout the story and I found the tension so well handled that although, occasionally, I had to put the book down I knew I had to pick it straight back up to find out what happened next. Again, this is a testament to the writer’s obvious skill.The school and the characters which inhabit it are superbly drawn; even the minor characters are well rounded and add to the bleak outlook for the main character, Grey. You get a real sense of the world closing in around him. Of the frustration and anxiety of his position and of a feeling of desperation and inevitably – hopelessness.I don’t read many books twice but this is one I will be reading again.Superb.

Surrender My Love by Lisa EugeneMy rating: 4 of 5 starsI was given this book by the author in exchange for an honest reviewLisa Eugene is becoming an author who I stalk on Facebook because I want to know when her next book will be released. That's how much I like her writing. She knows how to write characters that a romance-lover wants. And her work flows so well.I love the Washington Memorial Hospital Series! Steal My Heart was great and now we've got Surrender My Love... This story introduces us to Nurse Chloe Bennett. She's a hard worker budgeting her time between taking care of her patients and her mother, who has reverted back to a young child mentally due to an accident many years prior. Chloe cares more for those two aspects in her life than she does for herself, which is so common that I couldn't help but want her to find true love... And in walks the super hot, super sexy, super yummy Brad Markson... okay he more like trampled in. See, Brad is the #1 heart surgeon in the world so he can be a big a**hole almost 95% of the time, but really he's such a softy.Boy oh boy! The romance left me panting. It was done so well. I really detest cheesy romance novels where you can just see the BS from a mile away. Lisa knows what she's doing when it comes to the hotness levels that arise from this book.But there is an actual story to this novel. When patients start dying on both Brad and Chloe, lies become truth and the truth becomes lies.. That sounds so cryptic, but it's the way this story works. The two of them work together to figure out why these patients are dying and who is behind it all. There's so much mystery and suspense and in the end you're going to be like.. "I never saw that coming!!" Lisa always has the bad guys playing the least obvious character, so the whole time you believe it's one character and then POOF it's something you thought you could trust your firstborn child with.Overall, I'm going to give this 4 STARS out of 5 STARS. Lisa has amazing talent. I hope others read this and take a chance on her work because she is one of a kind. Check out her other book Steal My Heart and Strictly Business.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Read by Taryn Lee on December 13, 2013Reviewed by Taryn Lee on December 20, 2013http://facebook.com/tarynleesblog

Sweet, romantic, funny, and very entertaining, Switched was a fantastic New Adult romance. It was lighthearted, sweet, and truly enjoyable to read. I absolutely loved this book!Kayla was a likable heroine. She was very real. By that I mean she felt like a real person, which made her easy to relate to. Her narration was hilarious. She always had an odd view about things, which was fun to read about. I really liked her, for the most part. I thought she was awesome.Wesley was so adorable! He was so sweet and cute and utterly lovable. He always had a sarcastic comment ready, which added even more humor to the book. And, he was always thinking about others' feelings and considering them, which I thought was sweet. I thought he was just perfect and I adored him.The romance was very sweet. I liked how it progressed. It went from Kayla and Wesley wanting other people, to them slowly noticing each other, to falling in love. It was adorable. And, though this book was a clean romance, the steaminess was still there. I liked that, once they both realized their feelings, they gave up on the whole switch thing and it became a matter of waiting for them to be able to admit it to each other. Rather difficult when they had spent weeks talking about how they wanted and would get someone else, but they finally did. I really liked them together. I thought they were a lovely couple.I only had a couple of minor complaints about this book, which is what knocked own the rating. First, I thought it was selfish for Kayla to want to break up her best friend's relationship. Wesley had reservations and wanted to make sure that he didn't hurt his friend but Kayla wanted to just go right ahead. She gave the excuse that she didn't see that Reagan and Talon were truly in love, but I thought that was just her seeing what she wanted to see. I didn't mind the idea, considering it was the basis of the book. I even thought it was well executed in a way the made the situation humorous rather than manipulative, but I just wish she had been more considerate of other people's feelings. The other complaint is something at the end that I can't say without giving away one of the biggest surprises. It involved the workings of the plan and it struck me as unrealistic. A little too convenient. Both of these issues were minor and didn't hinder my enjoyment of the book as a whole. They were just a little annoying. Otherwise, I had no issues with this lovely book.The plot was fast paced and I was hooked the entire way through. The story was a ton of fun and truly enjoyable. I was thoroughly entertained while reading it. And I thought the ending was super sweet.Switched was a lovely New Adult romance. It was fun, sweet, romantic, lighthearted, entertaining, and truly enjoyable. It was the kind of fun read that just makes you smile and laugh and feel all warm inside. I absolutely loved it! Lovers of romance, if you want something fun and light to make you smile, then you have to read this book.*I received a free copy from the publisher in exchange for an honest review

POSSIBLE SPOILER IN THE REVIEW, ALTHOUGH I DO NOT THINK SOI have to admit that I am getting awfully tired of so many characters in mm romances being badly abused - not because it is not an important subject, but because it is often being treated superficially and inconsistently IMO.I did however enjoy this story. I really liked that not pushing somebody who is a survivor of abuse and who was still dealing with a stalker ex into something he was not ready for, meant exactly that for Connor. I liked that the writer did not decide to say "oh to heck with it, lets make them have some gratuitous sex just for the sake of it" and let the relationship proceed at a pace that made sense, to me anyway.I really liked how Kevin was portrayed, I really liked how clear the writer showed that changes in his personality were the result of horrendous abuse and how hard he fought to reclaim his life back.I loved that there was no idiotic break up just to make sure the characters will endure mandatory separation, the story provided enough tension as it was IMO.Now, it is a romance, so we all know that ex had to be dealt with in order for the main characters to be happy, do not worry, I am not going to tell you how it happened, but here is what I do want to say - I was dreading the resolution, because too often in order to deal with the villain one or two main characters has to do something monumentally stupid in order to expose himself to the confrontation with the villain. I did not feel that what happened in this one was stupid, opinions may differ of course, but at least to me it was consistent and made sense.I also liked how protective Kevin's friends were of him - but as much as I enjoyed them all, this is the part which I unfortunately found the least realistic. Just the fact that so many people cared so much and yes, I wish it would have been more realistic.

reviewText: Everyone likes a gladiator, even the king. I suppose my biggest problem with this book was the plot. There was a hefty amount of it, which to me, means the author wants us to take the plot seriously. In that case, she has to make it believable. Did I believe that the gladiator wouldn't turn on the prince? Nooo. Did I really think he would want to keep his sworn enemy safe? Hell, no. So the whole time I was reading it I kept thinking the prince and his advisor were total morons. Maybe it bugged me more than it should have but I guess I think most erotica should be like a long-novella. I read it for the steaminess, not the plot. So if it's being bulked out for plot, I want it to be good. It wasn't. So I give it 3.5 stars.

Stefan Sutherland (what a sexy name!) moved to Maplesville, LA to take care of his five-year-old nephew when the boy’s mom, Stefan’s sister, is called away to Afghanistan since she’s part of the Army Reserves. Stefan is on leave from the Navy because of an accident in the field (or rather air—he’s a pilot) so he agrees to watch over her son. He’s been in the Navy for 14 years but, instead of being rough and callous, he’s soft and sweet. War obviously hadn’t hardened him which is surprising. I wish we could have learned more about his pasts, his missions and all things Navy. The author breezed over his back story which irked me because military men are HOT!His nephew, Jacob, finds an injured stray cat that Stefan dislikes but he takes to the vet anyway. There he meets Calista Webber, a sexy vet that the little town of Maplesville pities because of a childhood trauma she suffered and her public divorce. Their romance starts as nothing more than a fling but soon turns into more. I love the addition of Sandy, the cat, because I’m a huge animal lover. She’s also the glue that holds this broken family together.The only thing that annoyed me was Calista's constant inner dialogue. She kept thinking about leaving town to start over at a new vet practice and it got a little old after a while. It's like she couldn't think of anything else but that except for when Stefan was around to distract her.Set at Christmas time, this heartwarming romance brought tears to my eyes. Stefan, Callie and Jacob are all suffering from pain and find comfort in each other. I love the author’s writing style, it followed beautifully, and I’m interested in reading the other novellas in the series.4 Stars.

reviewText: This is a smart sci-fi tale that jumps right into the story and comes to life with strong characters, vivid descriptions, and a plot that moves along at just the right pace.The dialogue also keeps things moving, and the story itself is crisp and engaging. You'll follow the adventures of an alien and his clone, whose exchanges are quite amusing. There are plenty of human characters, too, and my favorite is Hank, an unassuming Los Alamos National Lab janitor with surprising abilities.When the setting isn't space, it's often New Mexico (although New York and Disneyland are featured, too), and the authors do a fabulous job of conveying all the nuances that make the Land of Enchantment special, including the UFO mystique that permeates the state.As the story unfolds, a shift takes place, revealing something greater happening to humanity through this collection of characters.If you've ever wondered what clones talk about with each other, how a more intelligent alien race would regard humans, what it's like to travel inside an alien space station, and how human beings look when viewed in a whole different light, then get yourself a copy of Encounter and lose yourself in a fun, funny and enlightened tale of space adventures.
summary: Quirky and Imaginative like Hitchhiker's Guide

reviewText: As I was reading the Unrequited Dom the lyrics to "If I Can't Have You" by Yvonne Elliman and Gordon Lightfoot's "If You Could Read My Mind" kept playing in my head. Cash has had his eye on Sugar ever since his stepmother married Sugar's father. There is a 10 yr age difference and over time Cash realizes Sugar has the perfect temperament to be his ultimate submissive to his Dom, but all he has to do is wait and plan her initiation into the D/s lifestyle. The training starts after Sugar's father dies.  Cash takes on the responsibility of disciplining Sugar. His method of choice is bare bottom spanking for bad behavior, which he dishes out until her 21st birthday. On her birthday he decides to take their relationship to the next level and go for the total package. Cash has secretly lusted after Sugar for years and feels he has her primed and ready to fall into his bed and keep her there forever. Sugar falls hard but can't come to grips with her sexual need to be dominated  and disciplined by Cash.TUD has all the ingredients for a 5 star read but I gave it 3.5 stars because I got tired of the retelling of incidents and situations. Faulkner will have Sugar reminisce about previous conversations she had with Cash and then have Cash repeat the same conversation. I did not mind suspending my belief that anyone would endure bare bottom spanking into adulthood, but what I did take exception to was how long it took them to get it on and the amount of times they did. When I'm in the mood for smut I want a little less talking and much more action. The characters were likeable and I loved how Sugar was a bit clueless about how Cash truly felt about her which almost made him loose his mind when he thought she would leave him for the second time. I also loved how he zeroed his sights  on Sugar and no other woman would do. He truly wanted the best for her and in his own way made sure no matter what she was protected. In spite of my negatives I enjoyed this book.

Spiderwork is the second book in L.K. Rigel's Apocalypto series, and it being the sequel to Space Junque, the comparison arises. I thought as Space Junque was Char's story, Spiderwork would be about Durga, but was pleasantly surprised to see that although she was certainly one of the main characters, there was enough time and space to focus on others as well: we got to revisit some characters we got to know in the first book like Char, Jake and Magda and a whole new set of characters were introduced: emerging leaders of the new empires/settlements, chalices and the inhabitants of the settlement Jake and Char have built.I confess that I didn't like Durga in Space Junque and because of that wasn't really looking forward to Spiderwork, but she grew up to be a quiet and serious young woman who made me forget about the precocious little girl who irritated me with her arrogance and know-it-all attitude. It was good to see she had a more human side behind the mask of mission and that despite being the chosen one feared and respected by all she still had human emotions and needs.The world setting became even more complex and detailed and thanks to L.K. Rigel's writing my biggest concern and fear regarding sci-fi and fantasy (namely that I won't be able to picture the abnormal settings/creatures/things) wasn't realized here. Everything was described in great detail and even though I consider myself not too imaginative when it comes to sci-fi, I saw the extraordinary settings and strange species clearly.Though the Apocalypto series has strong romance storylines and love is interwoven all through the story this series has many other focal points: it explores tyranny, democracy, politicians' unethical behaviour, environmental issues, religious beliefs, love and one of the most important ones: reproduction. (but fear not, despite these serious issues it is most certainly not dull or boring!)I have to confess that I was in turmoil over this specific aspect of the Apocalypto series. In this faraway future women are infertile, so when a goddess resurfaced and assembled a dozen girls giving them fertility and long life (they will live until they are 150 years), they were also given a mission: they have to populate the Earth and provide men with children. Of course through this construction these women become breeding machines, having no say in choosing the fathers or how many children they give birth to. They can't have bonds with their babies as it would make the separation harder. The whole procedure reminded me of mail order purchases: the rulers of the settlements chose their chalice based on what kind of baby they wanted and then got the baby after the pregnancy. This inhuman and cruel, impersonal breeding upset me.As one of the characters said:"Not every woman who bleeds longs to become a glorified prostitute"And that is exactly what I thought of these poor women, I didn't see them as revered and being in enviable positions :-/What makes L.K. Rigel' sci-fi series very enjoyable even to sci-fi newbies like me is that despite the rich extraordinary world she creted she explores in depth her characters and their thoughts and feelings, and it is these emotional layers which make the story whole."Sometimes when I look at her my heart feels like it's been torn out of my chest. It hurts."Jake about his love for CharVerdict: I found Spiderwork even better and more vibrant than Space Junque and am looking forward to Bleeder, to see where L.K. Rigel is taking the characters and the big arch of the storyline in the third book.This section of a song sang in the story describes the series perfectly:"And if the old world has died, then let a new world ariseHe'll live out his days, and hold her so long, hold her so strongHe doesn't even wonder now.And he'll remain a man though the gods are changing"Plot: 8/10Characters: 8/10Writing: 9/10Ending: 8/10Cover: 10/10
summary: Even better and more vibrant than Space Junque!

As Pete's brother, Jonah says to him, (not realizing he's having a near death experience) she's beautiful, has a hot body, and an intelligence that can hold its own. Who would be stupid enough to pass up that? And Pete's no fool. He's not about to let his brother try to make a move on the woman he can't get out of his head.This short story was a treat. reviewText: Brought to you by OBS reviewer AndraSpoilers Abound!!!!rekindled-moments-moments-in-time-dori-lavelleI obtained a copy of Rekindled Moments from the author, Dori Lavelle, a free e-copy of this book in exchange for an honest review.  Thank you VERY much.  After reading the first…I had to read the second!Rekindled Moments from the author, Dori Lavelle is the second book in the Moments in Time series.Wow…..LOVED the continuation of Carlene’s life in this second novella…a much needed continuation I might add since I was not finished with Carlene after the first novella in the series!  And I am happy to say….I will also be waiting with baited breath for the third novella.  This was a quick, easy read which totally enveloped me in the world of Carlene…so much so that I read the book straight through on one snowy Sunday afternoon.The book begins with the introduction of Chris and the blossoming relationship with Carlene.  As we are taken through this journey, one can see how Carlene loved this man and how his eventual death played a big part in how she views herself as the person responsible for his death.  If only she could see that she wasn’t….but this self-deprecating view of herself and Chris’ death is what is the underlying current in the story and  makes the story powerful.  It made this reader want to shake and hug Carlene at the same time.As the story continues, Carlene and Nick are apart as he discovered that Carlene was “responsible” for his long lost brother’s death.  You feel the anguish washing over Carlene as a result of Nick shunning her and not giving her a chance to explain.  At this point in time….I wanted to shout at Nick….give Carlene a chance to explain.  After all, she had more history with Chris than Nick did.  When you think the scenario cannot get any worse….the press intrudes in their lives (since Nick is a wealthy, powerful man) by doing what the paparazzi does best…spreading untruths and splashing damaging photo’s out of context.As life spirals downwards, Carlene finally takes a stand with the press. As she is talking with the press, a white night appears (Nick) and saves her from the vultures we like to call the press.  A true romantic gesture.  I won’t carry on as I want to leave you with some surprises.If you like romance, hunky guys, and complex back histories you would not guess all in a short novella, this book is for you.See this review and more at openbooksociety dot com

Adrian King, the author of this unique book, describes himself as `I'm a Maverick Gamer. In fact, I'm not just enthusiastic about the science of becoming a successful gamer. I'm more of an addict, obsessed yet determined to dissect the thought provoking tips and tricks of some of the world's awesome games especially Minecraft. I'm keen on transforming the way you play and bring you the latest updates and awesome tips. I'm out here writing this to "Make a Difference" in people's lives, one game guide at a time. And I challenge you to make the leap and become your own work of art. Passionate gaming is what brought me to this stage early on in my life and curiosity will bring me far beyond my wildest imagination...'Now that we know the goals behind this book for those who are not familiar with MINECRAFT, the following will be introductory info: `Minecraft is a game about breaking and placing blocks. At first, people built structures to protect against nocturnal monsters, but as the game grew players worked together to create wonderful, imaginative things. It can also be about adventuring with friends or watching the sun rise over a blocky ocean. It's pretty. Brave players battle terrible things in The Nether, which is more scary than pretty. You can also visit a land of mushrooms if it sounds more like your cup of tea. Minecraft was originally created by Markus Persson, who you might know as Notch. Though Markus' original idea wasn't as fully featured as the Minecraft you'll play today, "Cave Game" was created from the same DNA. This was a game about placing and breaking blocks in a 3D world. The primary motivation was to create an experience where each individual component felt fun. A game that could be both accessible and emergent.'So, what does this interactive fascinating Minecraft 101 tricks hold for you? Adrian explodes the impossible problems you may encounter in the games and helps you discover how to expand your game. `This Kindle Guide aims to do for you just that. Save you weeks and months of boredom. Not only will you be able to keep this information for your own use, I'll be including some of my personal notes to help you in your quest to show off to your friends your new found Facts and Tricks.' It is impossible to review this book without giving away secrets, except to say it is a reliable resource to improve your gaming skills. Grady Harp, October 13
summary: Introduction for some, advanced information for committed players

In the space of a few hours Lexi Carmichael went from her dull job stopping hackers with the National Security Agency to being confronted with two different gun-wIelding thugs. Why? Because everyone seems to be looking for her best friend and some mysterious papers that she might have sent.  Lexi is totally confused since normally her biggest threat is the blind dates her mother keeps setting up for her.  Lexi knows and accepts she is a dull, brainy geek with little interest in fashion but her mother still tries to set her up with men who don't know how to handle her.Trying to find her friend and discover what everyone else is trying to find, Lexi goes to her other best friends, Elvis and Xavier Zimmerman, twins who are genius with computers and have designed extremely sensitive electronic networks.  You would think that would be enough but no, now Lexi is confronted with one sexy Italian government agent co-named Slash, who says he will help her, and a drop-dead handsome Irish man named Finn Shaughnessy who was working with the missing friend when everything went down.  Lexi now has to not only find her friend and keep her safe, figure out who is behind the thugs, and work her way though feelings for two men who normally would never look twice at her but seem to be falling for Lexi.  With a madcap plan, Lexi works her way from Jersey to Sweden with a trail of thugs, thieves, Finn, Slash and friends all to save the day and get to the bottom of what is going on and why.Thugs, Guns and Hot Guys - Oh my.  No One Lives Twice takes a geeky Lexi out of her normal life and puts her in the middle of an international who-dun-it.  I knew I would like Lexi from the first when I discovered she was a junk food junky and slow to get her laundry done.  When I then got thrown Slash, Finn and a mystery that is turning deadly, I knew this was going to be one fun book.  I was not wrong.  Watching as Lexi dealt with two gun-toting thugs, two beyond smart computer geniuses, one hot agent and then a toe-curling lawyer, all while trying to find and help a friend, proved to be a page turning plot.  I loved the humor that was the background for everything. The beginning buds of romance Lexi was feeling with both Slash and Finn at separate times had me wondering if Lexi would be able to choose. I can't wait until the next Lexi book so I can see just how her life has changed and who will get the upper hand in the romance department - Slash or Finn.  No One Lives Twice is a humorous look at the world of secret agents and enemy plots that will become an instant favorite series.JoReviewed for Joyfully Reviewed

reviewText: Ahhh, this book just gave me so many feels, I don’t even know how to express them all. I worry this review is going to be a jumbled mess, but that’s how you feel after you finish the Consequences series.This last book is told through the eyes of all the different guys we’ve met throughout this series. At first I didn’t want to read a book in other view points. I mean really who cares what John or Harry think. I want TONY. But as the story went on I began to see the genius in Romig writing it this way, the story needs all the pieces each man can bring to it. So much went on during those two years that it couldn’t be just told from Tony’s eyes or even Tony and another person. We needed it all so that we could really understand what happened in the missing years.I had so many notes on this book and you know who dominated most of them? No, it wasn’t Claire or even Tony, it was Emily. I HATE Emily. There are so many words I could use to describe her but none of them are nice and would make it through amazon's filters.  I blame the two years of misery that Claire went through on her. Then even at the end she does despicable things to Claire. Even after learning the truth her heart is just steel and unmovable. Emily is control obsessed and blinded by hate. I think there is a deep seeded jealousy at the root of it all, I really do. She may say she’s doing things “for Claire’s good” but she just wants to control the situation as she sees fit, not what is actually best. I didn’t love Emily in the previous books, but I left this one with a pure disdain for her.There is only one part of Convicted: the Missing Years I didn’t love, but it’s probably one of those “it’s not you, it’s me” things. In certain sections of this book we get to read chapters of the book Claire and Meridith published. They just felt like filler to me. I don’t know maybe they just weren’t interesting to me. I just had no desire to relive the events of book one we’ve gone over so many times before. I forgive Tony, so let’s move on from the past and work on how amazing he is now.There isn’t much action in this book at least when it comes to new events, but there is new information. As a reader I finally received answers to all those burning questions I left the last book with. We find out why and who was fired during those two years. Who may be sending those “special” gifts. So many things were finally tied up.Overall, this book was exactly what I needed in a conclusion. It was everything I wanted in order to leave the series in love with Tony. It was the chance he and I needed to connect. I had never quite reached the point of love in any of the previous books, but this one let him into my heart. It was the chance to really fully forgive him and it gave me the hope to believe Tony is actually a better man.I strongly suggest you give this whole series a shot, it’s a crazy ride, but worth every word. Each book takes the reader in one new crazed direction after another and you never know where we are going to end up. It had me on the edge of my pillows on more than one occasion.
summary: Overall, this book was exactly what I needed in a conclusion

A dark, thrilling, and engaging New Adult romance. Ruined was an absolutely brilliant read. I loved this book! It was just amazing. From the wonderful characters, to the action, to the shocking secrets, this book was perfection.Sam was a lovely heroine. She was incredibly strong and determined. Nothing was going to keep her from getting what she wanted and protecting her loved ones. I liked that she wasn't the type of character to needlessly hold a grudge (unlike some), especially once she knew the whole story. I really liked her. She was totally badass.Jax was also amazing. Despite his denials, he was a truly good guy who did his best in a bad situation. He might believe himself to be evil, but the contrary was obvious in how determined he was to protect not only his loved ones, but any innocent. He was really sweet when he wanted to be and I adored him.The romance was great. Sam and Jax were wonderful together. I thought it was so sweet how, despite their years they spent apart, they still had feelings for each other. I loved how both of them were willing to sacrifice for the safety of the other. And there was definitely tons of chemistry between them. I thought they were a lovely couple.One part of this book that I particularly liked was how the author portrayed the relationship between Jax and his demon (Azirak). I thought it would just be parasitic, with Azirak doing everything he could do make Jax miserable. But, Azirak was actually a fully developed character that I actually ended up liking. And, I really liked how Jax and Azirak complemented each other, basically two sides of the same coin. I just loved how it was done.The plot was fast paced and I was utterly hooked the entire way through. There were tons of thrills that kept me on the edge of my seat and quite of few surprising secrets that blew me away. This book definitely wasn't predictable. I really enjoyed the story and the ending has me anxious for book 2.Ruined was a brilliant New Adult paranormal romance. I absolutely loved this book. The romance, the action, the secrets, the unpredictability. It was all perfect. Romance lovers, this book is a must read.*I received a free copy from the publisher in exchange for an honest review
summary: Dark, romantic, thrilling, and full of secrets

ben ben Ben... I think you know you are deserving. So deserving. You can't let a mistake define you. that is what Ben didn't understand when this book began. he wallowed in fear and guilt. guilt for something that was justified and fear that we would become something he wasn't.Because of this he kept trying to push Kate away. so noble. so precious. Fortunately for us readers, he sucked at it. I mean really sucked at it. Thank you Ms. Scott because Ben so deserved to be cared for and see that he had family and loved ones.Kate- upbeat pushy Kate who was too inquisitive sometimes for her own good. But man if she wasn't this book wouldn't have been so wonderful.So Ben rolls into town and is there for a reason. It took alot of courage for him to come and face what he was but he did and yeah for us. He meets Kate and Kate's friend in the diner and Kate is instantly attracted. In order to keep him in town she tricks him but does get him a place to stay. this leads to his secrets being revealed to Miss M and no not what you are thinking. Miss M is a society woman in her 80's that is very rigid in her ways. Miss M makes him keep things from the others but lets him stay on to work on the house. This delights Kate but causing emotional turmoil in Ben. he likes Kate but is afraid of himself. and what he thinks he will be so he pushes her away. Only to succumb to Kate anyways because his feelings are too much for him.this leads to revealing a secret that is bigger than him and him trying to leave. That leads to Miss M doing something silly and almost ruining his future. Which leads to Kate showing him her true self and showing how much she cares and stands by him.A book on how one person's love can help another breakthrough and find their way out of the abyss.

Oh my goodness!  I couldn't put this one down for a second.  Scott mixes action and suspense alongside heartache and love to create a wonderfully complex experience for her audience.  She captures the essence of a working ranch perfectly and wraps it up in a will-they-won't they tale like you've never seen before.  Scott's descriptions are so vivid that she paints the ranch before you, allowing you to walk alongside the characters.  Each and every moment is extremely real and poignant.The conflicts between family duty and what an individual wants stand out starkly in this tale.  It was a very unique and touching contrast.  It is not just part of the story, but also part of who these characters are intrinsically.  The main characters were such vivid and strong individuals, even if they were slightly misguided at times.  It was both heartbreaking and heart-warming seeing them come to terms with who they were versus who they want to be.  Their individual histories and combined present are so completely developed without sacrificing the storyline that you really get to know them.  I also thoroughly enjoyed the minor characters in the novel.  You really get a feel for this entire community.  I really can't wait to get to know them better throughout the series.Scott had me in tears and squealing for joy throughout.  This was the perfect mix of everything.  It may have been my introduction to Scott's work, but it definitely won't be my last foray into the wonderful world that she has created.

'59 is the first installment of a serialized epic adventure.  There is a lot here that got me interested and anxious to learn more.  I love space adventures, and in this one two ships of cutting edge design take off on a planned nineteen month exploratory mission to a nearby star system. The year is 2059.  There are quite a few characters introduced, and at times I had a little trouble keeping all of them straight, but I'm sure that will become less of a problem as the mystery continues to unravel.Janine is the daughter of Donald Lewis, Captain of the Valiant, and the Mission Commander.  She is bright, opinionated, and loyal to her beloved father.  She also is exceedingly angry with her brother, Sean.  This vitriol seems sometimes to overpower her common sense.  So far, I am having difficulty warming up to her.  I hope the rift with her sibling is better explained from her perspective in a future installment because from the information I currently have, Sean performed admirably and with spectacular courage. It sure seems to me, at this point, that Janine's rancor is unjustified.  One thing for sure, I am curious to see how this story plays out. Lucky for me,'59 Part 2 - Valiantis also available, and is a full-length novel with over 5000 kindle locations. I have Prime and was able to borrow it from the Kindle Lending Library.

I love mysteries like this one!It certainly feels like you are reading one of Sherlock Holmes stories, at times. In fact, I think it's a bit too much like those stories. It felt like the author was trying to imitate them, rather than finding his own style. However, I think that I'll enjoy this author's books once he's written a couple more and has found his own rhythm.I felt that the dialogue was a bit stilted in this book - the characters share more of their feelings than is normal, and it seemed like they were trying to be more "proper" than was natural for them.But the storyline was great! This detective did seek out the clues the way Holmes might have, and it was fun to try and identify them. The author drew out the suspense very well, since I was not able to figure out "whodunnit" until he wanted me to.Honestly, I feel like this was a good first try for an author. I'll definitely be checking out Arthur S. Creeks books in the future.I received a free copy of this book in exchange for my honest opinion.

This is a wonderful book of poetry that I hope many people will read and enjoy as much as I did. The variety and quality of the selections is excellent and I'd recommend it to anyone interested in great poetry. In my opinion, this is how poetry should be written. It's totally fresh, deeply felt, and thoughtfully arranged and articulated. This inclusive book of poetry has something for everyone - even those who are not partial to poetry or for those who wish to be gently introduced to it.While every poem had something special to say, I found myself drawn to one in particular: `Ten Thousand Yins and Yangs'. In Chinese philosophy, the universe is made up of these two forces or energies both of which compliment or balance each other. I felt the poet captured scenes, that for a lifetime, I had never even thought about such as the simplicity of opening and closing one's eyes!These short poems present an opportunity to the reader to not simply read the poem, but to go over and over it, and finally memorize it. Then that poem the reader takes with them everywhere. It becomes part of oneself. And those lines are there for whatever time in life one may need them.

Before reading Dean Giles’ extremely helpful ‘Write a Step-by-step Book’, I thought I already had my writing methods down pat. I was astonished when I realized I could still vastly improve my personal writing habits—Giles’ system is, quite simply, a powerful boost to one’s speed, efficiency and creativity in writing books.It’s important to note, however, that Giles’ book is specifically made for those who write “step-by-step books”: books that identify a certain problem or situation, then provide effective methodical solutions. But even then I believe the fundamentals of this book can still be used even by those that write fiction—for example, the helpful instructions on how to efficiently organize your thoughts, gather material, compare your proposed topic to other similar best-selling books, and even in identifying what are called “evergreen topics”—topics that are barely fleshed out and are therefore hugely promising. What’s more, this book also provides explosive ways on how to market the finished product. But really, this book had me by providing a definite deadline: imagine being able to write a best-selling book in 16 days from start to finish? Read this book and find out how.Overall, Dean Giles’ book is an indispensable “secret weapon” by the serious nonfiction writer. And the best part is that it's not just generic "Secret" stuff, he talks about how you use it to help with IBS directly.Finally, he gives you self-hypnosis tools to get you started.  There are links to download six audio files that are meant to be used with headphones because they are subliminal recordings with binaural beats meant to train your subconscious to help cure your IBS.Since I'm a firm believer in the power of binaural beat subliminal recordings and how they can positively affect you, I know that IBS sufferers (such as the family member that I will be sharing this with) will most definitely get value from this book.  I almost gave this book 4 stars because there were some formatting issues, but the value in the information is just too great and I figured it was just the editor in me trying to be too critical, so the five stars I awarded this book I think are well deserved.

Quicksilver Dreams. Danube AdeleReview from Jeannie Zelos Book reviews.When I started this I was quickly hooked, and I thought it was going to be one I’d vote a five star for. Taylor is a great lead, feels so real and I felt I understood her – she'd struggled, and yet still retained her kindness in her fight for a better life than the one she'd had. That makes so many people hard and yet Taylor had a genuine kindness to her – I felt she's someone that could easily be a friend. I need to like my lead characters and Taylor was perfect. Then in came Ryder – wow- I could see just how she felt as she did about him, though he had some strange, almost throwback ideas, about women and clothes etc. Danube style of writing was easy to follow and led smoothly from one part to the next, keeping me clear about what was happening. I hate being left “in the dark” when things happen that haven't been explained, and reader has to pick up as story continues. That doesn't mean reader is spoon fed here, just that what's happening fits with expected plots.When she finds the metal I was “oh, where's this going to lead ?” and for a while it was fine. There was action and danger, all as I expected and then...Ryder takes her to his home planet. That's where it began to fall down for me. There was so much information, and descriptions of everything that I just failed to take much in. I was just wondering why she didn't have more questions, especially when someone she knows well enters the scene. She seemed the sort who'd be more curious, and TBH this part felt to me very YA, but with erotic sex thrown in to spice things up – strange planet, battles and heroes, mental voices and of course the dream-walking, it was all a kind of overload. The dream-walking part was fine in itself, and proved a good vehicle to explain things without overloading the reader with other info, but coupled with the rest I just lost the thread for a bit. It seemed Taylor was on a switchback ride, enemy to saviour to enemy, lover to traitor to lover, just too much in a short space with little other action to moderate that influence.Coming back to Earth I felt it regained some of that speciality I felt on first beginning the book. Ryder was still the control freak but sensuous lover hottie, but he and Taylor needed some serious time to work things out – the action though didn't give them that. I'm assuming this is part of a series as there's certainly scope for lots more from them, and the battle over mylunate, Taylor and Ryders relationship and Taylor's heritage. I hope so anyway – I think this is a good start, even though I lost in a bit in the middle.Stars: three and a half.ARC supplied by Netgalley

He just needs to get her back in Vegas. When Addison gets to Vegas though she not only finds Rush, but his ex as well. Can this couple put aside all their fears and doubts to find that happy ending they dreamed about years ago?Shattered Ink was a wonderful, satisfying story. The only downfall was that I wanted more, more, more! I love Addison and Rush together. They are believable characters in realistic circumstances. Who wouldn't feel a little bit of insecurity in a long distance relationship? Add in their pasts and their fear of being hurt, and the walls that they resurrected because of that fear was credible. The plot flowed perfectly for the story and the first person perspective gave more insight into what the characters were thinking and feeling then the normal third person would have, which I enjoyed. I am dying now for Vincent and Lisa's story and can't wait until next year! reviewText: This series is just an emotional roller coaster. But I will say it's one roller coaster you don't want to get off of. I love the way T.K. Leigh pulls you into Alexander and Olivia's world and their intense relationship. Below are my reviews for each of the books in the story. You definitely want to pick up this amazing emotional box setBeautiful Mess:"A Beautiful Mess", the perfect title for this book. Indeed, this story is a beautiful mess full of angst, love, betrayal, secrets and lies. T.K. Leigh takes us on a crazy roller coaster with both of the main characters emotions. I have never read a romance book like this one. This romance book is full of action and suspense as well, it keeps the story very interesting and keeps the reader in the story. These two characters have lived a roller coaster life, and struggle through things from their past, a past that they don't know connect with one another. I kept reading to see if the truth would ever be revealed and they would realize how connected they really are with one another. But NOOO T.K. Leigh leaves us with a cliffhanger! We do get a sneak peak into the next book at the end of this one, but not enough to know what is going to happen. I cannot wait for the next book in this series, I am in love with Alexander and Olivia.A Tragic Wreck:I LOVED LOVED LOVED 'A Beautiful Mess' and am hooked on T.K. Leigh. After reading her first book I was a fan of her and COULD NOT wait for the next book. T.K. writing is phenomenal and captivating, it always leaves me wanting more, I just can't get enough. I am so happy that I was able to read an ARC copy of this book as I was just anxious for its released. This book surpassed my expectations and left me with one major book hangover! This book is so emotional and captivating that I just had to read it in one sitting.We begin this book right where the first book left off, with Olivia out in hiding in a small town in Florida. She is trying to push away these intense feelings that she is having for Alex by doing what she does best: running. Alex on the other hand is relentless and will NOT let her simply disappear, hunting her down until finally finding her. He fights with all he has to give trying to get her back and convince her to go back to Boston, to stop running from everything. Their story is one filled with angst, drama, danger, romance as Alex and Olivia continue to fight for their love of one another, against all odds.I LOVE Alex and Olivia, they have quickly turned into one of my favorite couples. When they are together. But when they are apart, they drive me crazy! They do so many things to try and hurt the other one, dumb, little, unnecessary things that keep them away from one another longer than they really should. Sometimes I want to scream at them, they are perfect for one another but they JUST DON'T REALIZE IT! T.K.'s style of writing pulls you into the story, not knowing what is going to be happening. She takes us on a major roller coaster filled with Love, Angst and so many moments of suspense. The way that T.K. writes makes you feel as if these two characters are real people and not just fictional characters.After reading this book, I just CANNOT wait for the third book. I think I may go a little crazy while waiting for it! This book is filled with suspense, and that suspense lasts until the very end. There are questions that we have been asking ourselves from the very first book, some that we are answered in the book, others we are still left without answers to and new questions. T.K. is quickly moving up on those best seller/ best author lists and I can see why! This series is a MUST read. One of those that you will stay up late into the night and early morning reading, unable to put down!Gorgeous Chaos:Wow!! What an ending to this series! We've met and fallen in love with Alex and Olivia starting off in Beautiful Mess and in A Tragic Wreck... We know their history, and everything that they've had to go through. My heart broke for these two throughout the first two books and even more in this one. One one hand you have Alex, who has found the love of his life and is determined to keep her safe even if it means keeping her past from her. Then we have Olivia, haunted by her past and trying to keep herself from getting hurt. But the connection and attraction between these two is just too intense to ignore and to keep them apart.I will say that throughout part of this book I wanted to scream at Olivia for being so stubborn and not listening to Alex when he tried to protect her. She hurt him and herself in the process many times. We are taken through this huge roller coaster of a ride as Olivia's past is presented to her and other secrets are uncovers. T.K. also throws these big bombshells and twists to the story that had me gasping and shocked.This is a great ending to this emotion filled series, filled with emotion and drama. The way that T.K. is able to make us FEEL the pain, the hurt, that these characters feel is amazing. I loved the ending and feel as if their story is finally complete. Now I can't wait to see what Cam's story brings us!!
summary: A roller coaster of a series! MUST READ!!

What said hot young Doctor boyfriend does to her in this wonderful story was not only drop dead sexy, but it was for me so very romantic.One thing that I am not shy about, it is my sexuality. I believe that if more women simply trusted in their own bodies and explored all their options they would so liberated and happy, to be blunt. I love women that explore this in erotica. I believe that erotica is a literary gateway for a lot of women. For me personally stories like this make me lift a brow and toss it at my better half and go read that and turn fiction into fact. I don't read and write erotica to be perverted or dirty. I write it for women, for myself, and because I'm totally comfortable with that style of writing.This story, the way it was written, and how totally fulfilled I was with a simple short story instilled in me that I was totally doing the right thing in exploring my options as an erotica author. It was written perfectly, to the point where I could void the characters out and put myself in that story. Books are so much better than porno movies. Because your mind tells the story, not some fake bimbo on a TV screen that just makes you feel like you need to lose twenty pounds before you get naked for your husband or boyfriend. This story gave me a real woman, with real insecurities. It turned into one of the sexiest shorts I have read to date. I will defiantly be looking up more of this authors work!

The Winter Fairy is a gentle, sweet, warm romance about the choice one has to make between career and love and whether both can work together. Keira is a young woman afraid of the world, of people, of her own shadow. She has reasons to be after the horrific events of a year before that she has not healed from and does not believe she ever will for it is not just what happened to her but what she unknowingly caused that is her burden. She is not alone though for she has her cousin Scotty. He's the only one who knows and understands her pains for he has suffered his own. They are all each other has and Scotty will always be there for Keira but he will help her to move on and push her occasionally to step outside her boundaries for it is time for her self-imposed solitude to end. It will take someone very patient to get through to Keira.Liam is a handsome hulk of a man, a UFC fighter, with a tender heart hiding behind a brash exterior. He has suffered his own losses and combats them with sex and violence, letting his rage against the world out in the ring. Upon meeting Keira through association with Scotty he is intrigued by the skittish woman and is very much drawn to her. He recognizes in her a kindred suffering spirit, someone who understands emotional pain and he wants to get to know her but his presence frightens her.This was a sweet tender romance that captured my attention from the beginning told in multiple POV's. In this story two broken people find in each other what they need to heal and learn how to forgive. Liam is a wonderful hero, very empathic, able to step above his own pains to make Keira comfortable without knowing the why's of her reticence. Keira is stronger than she thinks, the mind has a way of figuring out how to cope with bad things that have happened to us by putting protective defenses in place and when it's time it slowly releases its hold, allowing us to step forward, to make progress against the pains that torment us. With Scotty's support and Liam's patience Keira grows into the woman she was meant to be but it is not easy and there are occasional steps backwards as she learns to cope with the world again and learns to trust in those in it.This is the first time I have read this author. The story was enjoyable and the writing shows a lot of potential. The pacing was a little slow at times and then rushed near the ending. The writing could have been more fluid. There were numerous grammatical errors and typos that an editor should have caught. It would be nice to read Scotty's story if this author writes one for him.
I would like to recommend this book to anyone who wants to read a great story. I will be looking forward to reading the next book from this author.

The plot kept me wondering, how will they do this? Why is he/she acting like this? Can we really trust this guy? Or why doesn't she trust him? It just keeps you guessing. Really? Has never made one friend in her whole life? Has no family except one horrid cousin? Really? No godparents? No local clergy? No solicitor or man of business for her father's estate overseeing her inheritance or her dowry?  She also has no spirit and no brain. Really. If she had gone and told her vicar or estate manager or neighbor or anyone else about her troubles, she might have still been disbelieved and abused, but she didn't even attempt to stand up for herself or seek help in any way.Really.

The book description says this book is 180 pages long, but it felt twice as long to me. The high drama, just one thing after another, really dragged the story out. I didn't so much mind the push-pull between the h/H, but then it got to where it was fight, be mean, then have a misunderstanding, then kiss-make up, then back to I hate you, then I love you, then push him/her away, etc. I really felt worn out by the time I got to the last page. Besides the main couple's drama, there was also personal family drama, friend drama, grandparent drama. It was almost smothering. But if you like a lot of drama and emotional angst in your romances, this might suit you. It felt a bit melodramatic to me, over-drawn, and I didn't like the constant back and forth.Also, this needs a good re-edit. Missing commas, misspellings, missing words from a sentence, the wrong word used sometimes. Just things that caught my attention or caused me to read a sentence again.I do think the author had something interesting going in the beginning. And I did like some elements of this story: the high school setting, the Cinderella theme, the surly, brooding hero. Certain aspects of the story were entertaining, especially if you don't mind teenage angst and drama. And I do happen to like that, but I have to say that here it was just a little too much for me. The book does end with a complete story for the main couple, they finally get there in the end!, and it sets up the next book, Break Me, about Royal, the hero's best friend.
summary: I would have liked this more if the drama had been cut in half.

Author Raymond Le Blanc has written an in-depth book on Autism and what every parent needs to know about symptoms, diagnosis, and treatments.This book covers the history of myths, symptoms to look for in your child and the different levels of testing for autism. Also covered is what to expect after the diagnosis, suggestions on where to turn to for help and support group and the on-going research to learn more about this disease.The author includes information on medications, treatments, therapy and how autism affects adults and the elderly.This book is highly recommended for anyone interested in learning more about autism.  Parents, family members, caretakers and anyone dealing and coping with the effects of autism will appreciate the knowledge and information found in this book.

reviewText: Criminal lawyer Andy Cole is not a stereotypical hero.  In fact, he's hard to like at times.  When he's hired to represent Danny Fairgreen on a murder charge Andy doesn't realize his own life is going to be turned on its ear.  He knows there is some corruption in his small town but what he thinks is going on turns out to be just the tip of the iceberg.Andy is forced to examine his relationships with personal and professional individuals in his life and find out who is trustworthy, as well as deciding if he, himself, can be trusted.  He's put in life and death situatons, and ethical dilemmas, when he decides to seek the truth.  The action really heats up when he's forced to protect evidence that will clear his client, and also himself in the many wrong doings going on.The action is fast paced and life changing for many, and the town is forever changed because Andy declined to accept a plea bargain.

Ronin's family has been cursed, and since they no longer recognized their mates they no longer issue 'the Call' and instead bed enumerable 'faceless' women to keep their magical powers charged.  But Ronin has fixated on one woman, Kari. Kari has watched Ronin and his twin pickup scores of women - and with each conquest her has heart broken just a little more.  And even though Ronin is now sure that just any woman will no longer 'do' and that he only wants Kari, Kari is not willing to be just another notch in Ronin's bedpost and rebuffs his advances.I just finished reading Ronin's brother Raden's story, "Mated", in the anthologyHaunted by Your Touch- "Fated" actually comes first. It was fun to get Ronin's story too after having seen him in the background of his brother's story.  "Fated" was a short sexy read, with a fair amount of angst for Ronin in having to find out if Kari could be the one, and wanting to take the chance to break with tradition and trade the endless string of women in his past for one woman in his future - but being afraid that loving Kari could mean her doom because of the curse.I am not quite sure were this falls in the Doomsday Brethren timeline ("Mated" has events that set up for Black's next book), but this is a nice companion to "Fated" and a nice little fill-in for Black's series (several of the Brethren have cameos).

"Threads" is an intricate story that weaves (no pun intended) together many sub-plots to a conclusion that affects future humanity and their fundamental understanding of the universe.The telling of the complex nature of this future universe comes with strengths and weaknesses. The massive amount of information provided at the beginning of the story does well to establish a very real and believable future, but – for me – it takes on the feeling of reading an essay rather than a story. However, it's broken up with character and actions scenes, so it never failed to lose me. There were times amongst this information where I had to just grab the important points and let the rest slide, but that did not affect my understanding of the story. If you enjoy navigating a complex world, then I'm sure you will enjoy the set up.Once the universe is established, as well as the characters and plots, the story picks up and is very enjoyable to read. It's a multifaceted story: part detective, part political, part science, part humanitarian (and I use the word "humanitarian" most generally because, well – spoilers!) It's well written and all comes together in a satisfying conclusion.I found the concept of the "threading" to be most innovative, and put a very unique and fun spin into the story as a whole. So, even if the first half may require some patience to get through, it is worth the effort, and I would recommend this story for its well-executed depth.
summary: An intricate SF story with a unique element.

Travel narratives are never about just the travel. If a reader desires information about travel destinations, guidebooks and their internet equivalents do a better and much more comprehensive job. What a narrative gives that a guidebook can't is the personal touch. What did this specific traveler experience and get out of their trip? What were they looking for? What did they actually find? It might be adventure, a better understanding of other cultures, escape (even if temporary), or a better understanding of themselves. Travel, Sex, and Train Wrecks has all of these.Morey's writing voice is informal, helping the reader feel like they're a friend tagging along on her adventures. However, this sometimes went a bit too far. One example being her overuse of the word ever, as in "... the absolute best breakfast joint --Ever." Still, a fun read that should appeal to fans of travel narratives, especially women who have a thing for guys with accents.**Originally written for "Books and Pals" book blog. May have received a free review copy. **

reviewText: Kirk Alex never disappoints!  This author really delves deep into the core of sadistic evil and courageously brings to life some of the most disturbing subject matters that most authors of horror can't even begin to envision. Have no doubt about it; he will have you begging to get out of the `Rabbit Hole' he has conjured.I have studied abnormal psychology and I have long been fascinated by what makes certain people monsters and others saints. I have a deep curiosity of the inner workings of the minds of serial killers.  I follow true crime stories and have studied many psychopaths.  With that said, I must admit that I have never gotten a closer, more intimate look into the mind of a depraved, sadistic tormentor with an insatiable appetite for all that is `unspeakable' taboo in today's society.  I have no doubt that people such as these exist within our communities and that is disturbing on so many levels.Lustmord: the Anatomy of a Serial Butcher is a series like no other. It is not your typical and predictable slasher book; it digs down to much deeper levels than that.  It's the psychological depravity that will haunt you.  It is not for everyone.  It is delivered with brutal honesty, with realistic and often, Mature Dialogue and laced with shockingly graphic torture scenes.  It takes Rare talent to bring to life a madman filled with such intricate, twisted pleasures, brimming with sadistic and depraved needs; a man that looks upon humanity with such a warped sense of perception that it invades the mind of the reader.  I give this ENTIRE Series a 10 for the `Realism' Factor alone.I am reading this Entire series...I am hooked, It pulls you into the `rabbit hole' of madness and even though at times you want to stop reading...you just can't .  It has been very thought provoking and it will make you question your own perceptions in life.  What kind of person does it make me that I am fascinated with this type of writing? ...I'll tell you one thing...I am human and it is the humans' basic need for survival that makes one try and understand those around them...and ....trust me, they are around.  Hats off to you Mr. Alex, you have taken this genre and turned it upside down...now, onto Volume 5!
summary: The Ultimate `Rabbit Hole' of Madness that will have you Begging for Release with Each Turn of the Page!

Witnessing the gruesome death of her uncle and his lawyer in a werewolf attack, and being told at the same time she herself was such a beast, a young Cassie flees her sheltered upbringing and ends up in rather difficult circumstances in Las Vegas.  The story chronicles her struggle with a semi-platonic, troubled boyfriend, a wolf who is out to find, protect, and claim her, as well as significant threats to her and those she loves. This "paranormal romance" novel weaves a wide range of interesting themes into the story, including difficult relationships between troubled individuals, crime and violence, a werewolf's need to find and protect his mate, and an intriguing/evolving plot with some rather interesting, suspenseful twists.Readers new to Nicky Charles will not only find some traditional elements of paranormal romance but also find some action and danger as well as flawed characters of mixed motivation and sympathy.Readers who enjoyed the preceding Law of the Lycans books should find this entertaining as well.  This story follows themes somewhat similar to those in previous novels series, although these protagonists (Cassie, Kellen, and Bryan) travel through a rather grittier and darker environment.  This novel focused on two characters introduced in the preceding story, the Keeping, inserting them to a rather difficult and dangerous environment, while also eventually drawing back in the heroes from two earlier novels in the series.
