Lisa Kessler has already impressed me with her “Moon” shifter series, even earning my top spot for 2013 in paranormal romance for Hunter’s Moon. Of course I have a bit of a shifter obsession so she had a little bit of an advantage writing about hot, sexy werewolves.But her novel Beg Me to Slay had me falling in love with demon slayers.Can we talk about the heroine for a second? Tegan is one badass chick. After a demon attacked her, she refused to sit back and ever be a victim again. She trained herself to fight, opened her own business, and had her life pretty well in order until the demon from her past showed up in her present. I liked her a lot – her confidence, her ability to push through her fear and not be crippled by it. She didn’t necessarily need a man to rescue her, she just needed a little help tracking down her worst nightmare.Now Gabe. Oh my Gabe. He’s hot, charming, sexy, strong… he’s not thrilled about letting our heroine help him on the case she hired him to do but he learns to respect her skills. These two have some serious baggage and continually fight against the attraction they both feel, but when they finally get together, they make the wait worthwhile.Filled with plot twists and bits of history that keep the storyline engaging a unique, Beg Me to Slay is a definite must for fans of paranormal romance. Hot guy trying to save the world? Strong woman refusing to back down from a fight? Intense wall sex because they just can’t wait a second longer? Demons with acidic yellow blood seeping out from under their scales?Okay, could have done without that last part.4.5 stars to this fabulous piece of demony goodness. Lisa Kessler has definitely caught our attention – I can’t wait to start working my way through her backlist as I wait for more of her pretty words to be published.

To say this book messed me over is an understatement. Mia played with every single one of my emotions. I didn't know whether to cry, dance, punch the wall, cheer, or throw my damn kindle across the room. She knew just how to bring me to my knees, rip out my heart, and chew it up for breakfast.Arsen is a raw, emotional, angsty, heartbreaking, real, story. It is everything that I love in a story.Mia created a world that went beyond fantasy. It's a world filled with real life problems. Real life situations and real life temptations. Mia gave us Cathy, Ben and Arsen.Cathy is broken. She's a lost soul. She is someone you may never understand but she is someone that you can sympathize with. I never hated Cathy. I didn't agree with all of her choices, but I understood why she did them, even when she may not have.Ben is a man you want to spend the rest of your life with. He's amazing, caring, loving, and overall the perfect man any woman could want or dream of. So what's the problem? One word. Arsen."It's funny that his name reminded me of fire because he certainly looked like someone who could burn you to the ground."Arsen. He is a man that may be just as broken and misunderstood as Cathy. He is the one person that understands the meaning of pain and the one person who can teach someone to deal with it. He is the one man that can break you. But, most importantly, he is the one man that can set you on fire.Arsen is a story that will leave you questioning everything you just read. It may shatter you. It may tear you down. But, most importantly, it will make you FEEL.Mia Asher wrote something that is unlike anything you'll ever read. She knows how to bring her characters to life and give her readers something that will leave you wanting to join a support group!

I read GUT INSTINCT in one sitting and really enjoyed it. If you read Brad Taylor's earlier novel ALL NECESSARY FORCE then you might recall that it ends with Jennifer in a confrontation with her ex-husband. Her character had been wrestling with moral questions regarding the use of violence -- additionally, she'd been a victim in the past but now was coming to terms with her role as a defender and protector.GUT INSTINCT begins with the confrontation between Jennifer and her ex-husband. She's no longer a victim, for sure, and when her and Pike later travel to the Philippines to assist in an ongoing operation we get to see her character grow even more as she works to earn the respect of other Task Force members. In the earlier books and in the opening scene here that corresponds with ALL NECESSARY FORCE we witnessed Jennifer prove herself physically and in some respects emotionally -- here she gets to prove her mettle analytically and in an operational sense. She's willing to go against the prevailing opinion among other Task Force members because she believes her gut instinct is right -- and with a terrorist attack imminent, none of them can afford to make a mistake.This Task Force story is obviously a promotional tool for the author's soon-to-be-released new novel in this series -- it comes with an excerpt from THE WIDOW'S STRIKE -- however, it shouldn't be dismissed because of that. It's a great story in its own right and I highly recommend it to anyone who has previously read and enjoyed the Pike Logan / Task Force series.If you're new to Brad Taylor and this series then I'd probably temper my expectations a bit -- not because you need to have read the earlier work to understand or enjoy this story, but simply put I think people who are already immersed into the world of these characters will be more likely to jump right in and appreciate this short but action-packed mission.
summary: Gut Instinct -- if you want people to bet on you, then you gotta be willing to bet on yourself

It’s a harsh reality but the modern day diet is simply not healthy enough. There is too much trans-fat, salt and omega 6 and not enough nutrients. The result is an almost worldwide obesity epidemic as well as bodies being full of excess waste. This plaque like substance is the result of eating too much processed food and it creates a breeding ground for bacteria. Clearly a big change is needed to improve the health of most people and this book offers an insightful treatment option.Essentially the master cleanse is like a fast, by following it your body is able to detoxify and flush out all of the congestion in your body. This offers many benefits with weight loss and increased energy levels being the most common two occurrences. For people new to this method I feel that this guide is a fantastic resource. As well as outlining all the ingredients you will need to proceed with it a detailed summary is also given of the pros and cons to help you evaluate whether you are suited to this cleanse. I was impressed by the section on common mistakes to avoid, doing any sort of cleanse or fast is tough so you need all the help and tips you can get to keep on track and ensure you get the full health benefits.For anyone looking to lose weight or improve their health in general I highly recommend this book. It presents a really beneficial cleanse in a clear and concise manner that will allow any participants to get started straight away.

2.5 starsAlthea is a gallery owner who always wanted to be an artist but never measured up. One day Steel, a handsome, dark stranger, enters her gallery and asks to rent her basement to work on his sculptures. Little does she know that Steel is about to change her life by revealing another side of her.I thought the concept behind the book was interesting with a unique take on your usual opposites attract story. However, I feel that the concept failed in its execution, focusing mainly on their sexual relationship and not enough on their romantic one. I loved Steel, but I didn't really connect to him because the glimpses I got of him were superficial at best. I wanted to know what really drove him and what his story was all about. Although Althea was developed throughout the story I truly did not feel that her development was real mainly because all these changes in her happened too fast.There are stories you start reading and immediately capture your attention. Although this was the case with Platinum in the beginning as the story progressed I lost my interest. I'm sorry to say that there was too much sex. Yes, I said it. Too much sex and only a couple of them really added to the story at all. Don't get me wrong, they were hot and on the kinky side and I loved them, but apparently I like a little story with my sex and Platinum did not deliver.Although the writing was very good and the characters were interesting together, I felt that their story was rushed. From what I gathered Althea and Steel had major issues with how to make a relationship work and I could not believe that their relationship would come by so smoothly. Especially since it was based mainly on sex.I really wanted to love this book, especially since I thought Steel was such a great character and the concept was so different, but it didn't reach its potential.I received this title from Carina Press through NetGalley in exchange of my honest opinion.

I’ve always been a horse lover so what could be better than a story about a horse wrangler and a park ranger.When a poacher starts killing animals in the park, Ranger Joel Morgan is brought in to track him down. His first brush with trouble isn’t the poacher, it’s sassy horse wrangler, Brittany Lucas.Brittany is camping in the park, enjoying some alone time when she awakens to a strange man snooping around her camp. Recalling the warnings of a poacher,  her guard goes up. When the dust settles, she ends up sharing her tent with Ranger Joel. He won’t leave her alone in the park, and with heavy snows coming, they have to wait til morning to head out.The sparks from the camp fire are nothing compared to the ones that occur between Brittany and Joel. The attraction is strong but both have assumed things about the each that have them battling wits.I enjoy character driven novels and the author has many in this book. Brittany is kind and gentle, but also independent and strong-willed.Joel is hard-headed, determined, and not easy to brush off.The other characters lend support to the main ones, filling out friendships and giving us some suspects.Right away I had two characters pegged as possible bad guys. The poacher wasn’t just into making money. His lust for blood was becoming a need and I didn’t think animals would satisfy him for long.As the attraction between Joel and Britt built, so did the suspense and danger from the poacher. Brittany is now his target and while most of the time, the author doesn’t kill off a main character, you just never know.It’s always fun to read how the characters meet, how their assumptions screw things up, and they fight the growing attraction.  I grinned a lot, laughed too, and shook my head as Britt and Joel made a mess of things.I especially enjoyed reading about Britt and Gypsy. The ranch owner purchased Gypsy because no one else wanted her. She was out of control and dangerous. When he asked Britt to try to gentle the wild mare, she rose to the challenge and that’s where she really showed her stuff as did the author. You could feel the excitement, but you had to be patient, just like Britt. Whatever turned Gypsy into a raging inferno didn’t happen overnight.Beautiful scenery of Colorado, a blistering romance, and danger came together in a really good mystery/romance that kept me turning the pages, enjoying the ride.I received this book for my honest review.
summary: A fun  beginning to this series.

reviewText: I am glad I found this book, and once I started, it was hard to put down.  I agree with the positive reviews given so far, and there is only one reason I did not give it five stars: the book needed some editing before being released.  However, in one area it had been over-edited.  There is a tangible absence of the use of past perfect tense ("He had seen this before," "It had happened in the past").  I fear that the author had been coached by someone who does not share his talent or ability to turn a good story.  Many amateur "wannabe" writers concentrate too much on a silly list of mechanics that despises adjectives and adverbs, and thinks it's a cardinal sin to include the passive voice.  I will agree that too much passive voice will damage a story, but it is part of the English language.  Some less-than-professional writers include past perfect tense with the passive voice because they sound alike.  The omission jarred me somewhat.  It was as if the author had used a "search and replace" to get rid of every usage of the word "had" in the book, because sometimes the omission leaves an incomplete sentence.My advice to Mr. Kasselman is to trust his own writing talent, and to avoid the well-meaning literary coach that butchered the narrative in this book.  He is an excellent author:  the characters are likable, believable, and well-developed.  I never lost interest in this book, and even knowing about this one flaw in editing, I would highly recommend the book.  You will not be disappointed.  I look forward to reading more by Harold Kasselman.

When she refuses to leave, he opts for option two staying in the little village she's volunteering in and being her bodyguard. However, despite his protection trouble finds her and she's abducted and it's up to Palmer to rescue her before it's too late.I really enjoyed this story. It had some action along with the romance. The heroine is a sweet character, caring for the children of the village. While Palmer is the ultimate alpha male, standing over her, protecting her every moment of each day, but in the process finding himself falling for the woman he'd paid to protect. When they finally connect, the scene is explosive.

Complimentary copy provided by the author in exchange for an honest review.Freed, the second book in the Unlovable series, picks up immediately where the first book, Used, leaves off. Denver is left to explore her new relationship with Ransom while dealing with the fallout of the revelation by Greer and the activities of one drunken night between best friends. Denver must put herself back together and come to terms with her past before she can continue to pursue any relationship going forward.Ransom has his own demons to face, and when a surprise shows up on his doorstep he is forced to confront the relationships of his own family’s past. With Denver by his side, they learn that together they can move beyond their parents’ mistakes and limit the affect their past has on their futures.Once again, Ms. Halat has taken a collection of very broken characters from a background of dysfunction and woven them into a family of love and support that works together to defy the odds facing them. Based on their pasts, Denver and Ransom’s relationship should be doomed from the start, but with the help of Austin, Pete, and Maggie, there is hope that they’ll make it.Don’t get me wrong, the book isn’t just a heavy look at the complexities of their relationship, it is also hot as Denver and Ransom begin to explore his dominant tendencies, and her natural submissiveness. It’s a different look at BDSM culture, because it is seen through the eyes of college students, not through the eyes of those in their 30s or 40s looking to spice up stale relationships. It’s awkward, yet equally exciting. I definitely look forward to how this will continue to play out in the next book and hope that the level of heat will only continue to rise.An air of anticipation hangs heavy throughout the entire book. Used ended with a bombshell ending and Freed does as well, one that came so far out of leftfield it leaves you blindsided. Strangely, the book feels like it lacks “action”, for lack of a better term. For pretty much three quarters of the book there is no real angst or action, the chapters are spent building and solidifying the relationship between Denver and Ransom, and repairing the relationship between Denver and Greer.From the moment I finished Used I was eagerly anticipating the release of Freed and it did not disappoint in any way shape or form. If anything, it exceeded my anticipation not only in plot and character development, but in the intensity of the heat between Denver and Ransom. To say that Ms. Halat is a master of sexual tension would be an understatement. The attraction between Denver and Ransom is undeniable and what begins as a slow burn builds to an explosive end by the end of the book.Used had already found its way onto my “best of 2014” list of books and Freed has joined it as well. This was a five star read from cover to cover and has earned Ms. Halat a place on my “must buy” list.

I received this book not as an ARC, but got it free from the author in exchange for a review.****DOES CONTAIN SPOILERS*****It's taken me much longer than I anticipated to read this book. It's not a bad book, it's jut not in the usual category of things that I read and it just didn't leave me running off to read it.That being said, here's what the book is about.Rylan, the main female character, is an ex-cop. She lost her husband and her daughter in an accident and is looking for a change. She's hired to work at Paint River Ranch and goes there. She meets a man named Cole Haywood. He's the owner of the ranch. She's hired to clean and help around the ranch. The last thing that she ever expected was for Cole to have a young child, Birdie. Birdie is a lot for Rylan to handle. She's jealous of her, to an extent. She's reminded of the daughter she no longer has and she really wants nothing to do with her.However, Rylan is falling for Cole and she knows that means she has to accept everything about him, including his daughter. The book focuses on Rylan and her feelings and recovery from all she's experienced up to this point. Despite knowing he shouldn't, Cole fights his feelings and eventually he and Rylan start to have a romantic relationship. Birdie slowly wraps her fingers around Rylan's heart and Rylan learns that she can love Birdie and hold on to her daughter's memories, too.Near the end of the book, Rylan learns just how much Birdie means to her when an accident happens and she saves her. Cole gets upset, but upon learning exactly what happens, realizes he's wrong and goes after Rylan to say he's sorry and he loves her.The only reason I gave this book 4 stars is that it's just not the usual thing that I'd read. While I'm sure the rest of the series is awesome, I don't think that I'd read it. Cowboys and ranch life just don't really keep me interested. Sorry. Don't pass this book up if that's your thing, though. If you like Cowboy romance stories, you'll really like this.

reviewText: By The Bros on June 18, 2013TweetPin ItnamelessdwarfWhen Momma came downstairs brandishing The Nameless Dwarf I knew I HAD to have it. I was sucked in so fast. The companions, all being complete opposites really play well off of each other and the authors depiction and development of their relationships is very rewarding as a reader.  I loved all of them in their own right Ilesa was one of my favorites and I definitely found myself able to relate to Silas in a sort of unsettling way, but hey I am a teenager. If I can learn his lessons now, then I'm doing ok.I have and totally will recommend this book to my friends so I recommend it to you! It's summer break for Laney, Dane and the rest of the Crew.  This a novella (though a good length for one!) and is written only from Laney and Dane's POV.  I am assuming since this takes place over the summer, Sawyer's story will begin where this leaves off.I am team Evan but I really finally started to like Dane in this novella.  He grew on me and I'll be excited to see where all the members of the Crew end up when Ms. Hall is done with their stories.This novella mainly focuses on Laney's new duplex and getting it ready for her to live in.  She and Dane make a bet-- they each decorate a room (because they can't agree) and the Crew will vote to see who wins.I actually feel bad for poor Dane during part of this but I don't want to spoil anything so I'll keep quiet (has to do with what he wins if his room is chosen).  We get little glimpses of Evan, Whitley, Zach, Bennett and Tate as well.  The characters are so loveable and I have actually fallen more in love with the side characters than the two main ones.  So please, Ms. Hall... keep them coming!BTW, there is no cliffhanger to set up Sawyer's story so don't worry about that. He's in the book and you can tell his story is being set up but it doesn't leave you hanging about any storyline.

reviewText: Our hero takes advantage of a young woman's situation and makes her his mistress because she rejected his marriage proposal. He later has the audacity to tell her that he loves her, so she kicks him out of their love nest. Obviously, if he loved her, he wouldn't have ruined her reputation by making her his mistress. The novella centers around him being bewildered by what he did wrong and his efforts to get her back. Meanwhile, the heroine has set out to make a point.This is one of those novels/novellas where the reader is supposed to be dumb like the heroine and overlook the fact that the hero is a jerk and love him anyway. The stories pack a meaty punch and keep you wanting more.  If you're a fan of Scotts previous works, you will definitely not be disappointed. I Received An ARC Of This Book In Exchange For My Honest Review!This book picks up right where Angel's Hero left off and I absolutely loved it.  You do have to read Angel's Hero before reading this book.  You will understand what's happening and the events that have led up to our current situation.Aaron (Angel) and Jordan are reunited at the beginning of the story after Jordan's escape from Afghanistan.  What makes this so emotional is that Angel was told and showed evidence that he had died in a prison over there after being captured.  Things aren't easy for them when Jordan returns home.  Besides being a POW and suffering from PTSD due to what happened to him in the Iraqi prison.  Jordan knows who's responsible for what happened to him but if he can't prove it he can be court martialed and possibly sent to prison.  Jordan can't go back to prison not after what he's been through.  Angel believes his husband and will do anything he can to help Jordan out and prevent that from happening.  He just got his husband back and he's not letting him go without a fight.I know I said it before but I'm gonna say it again...I loved this book.  Liz Borino managed to keep me on my toes throughout the book.  There were a couple times she even managed to surprise me.  This story is full of action and drama.  Jordan and Angel make the story and love each other so much.  You see them grow closer as events unfold in the story.  Everything will finally come full circle in this book.  A definite must read.
summary: A wonderful series. Love Jordan and Angel.

reviewText: This book was gloriously heartbreaking.  Oh the lies, the lies.  So twisted and sad.  Heaps of misunderstandings, pride, and sacrifices.  This is a long book.  Perfect to settle in and get to know the characters.  They felt a part of my life for the past two weeks, and I was embedded in their story - exactly how a well-written book should be.  Plus, I consider Owen to be a true word artist.  I enjoyed the challenge of less commonly used vocabulary words, and I’ll admit I used the Kindle dictionary a few times.  The plot was perfect and captivating. At some points I was so heart broke, I was afraid to read what would happen next.

Not Pretty Enough was an entertaining and sweet novel I think most of us can relate to. It's clean and appropriate for young teens, focusing on embarrassing moments as the main character tries her hardest to get the boy she likes to notice her.Chessie was a hilarious character. She was self conscious, but didn't realize just how brave she was by trying new and imaginative ways to get her crush to see her and note her existence. Except her crazy antics get her noticed in ways she would rather not be. She succeeded in embarrassing herself numerous times! I think most readers will be able to relate to some her embarrassing moments and be thoroughly entertained.Not Pretty Enough was a quick read, but it was full of comedy and important lessons in the end. I highly recommend it, especially for young teens who are looking for an entertaining and funny book. Parents will love Not Pretty Enough because it's hilarious, but also full of healthy and necessary lessons about learning to be yourself and self worth. Maelstrom continues the Sacred Breath series in fine style... The character development plays out crisply and most entertainingly. This writer has an amazing talent for bringing a character's personality to vivid life through internal and spoken dialog.  There is dialog in this book that elicited out loud guffaws at 3am!  (I ended up reading the next few chapters on the couch...) And the plot timing is exquisite.  The story has one going from breath stopping immersion in pitched battles to outrageous comic relief that doesn't feel forced at all.  Some of the lines that come out of N.S.'s head through her character's mouths are little treasures that will have you smiling, shaking your head and thinking WTH?!?!  If you've ever had a lovably outrageous person in your life... You'll relate to Visola, Vachlan and Taranis with pleasure.  This is book 6 of a really fine series whose writer gets better and better at her craft.  Even better... The price point is in the sweet spot to make buying or giving this entire series easy.

Mix that in with the fact her husband has taken on a whole new personality and you have emotion overload.  Gavin has went into hiding, popping up here and there to threaten Rachel's life and succeeding in ending others.  Deep down Rachel knows her husband would never act this way, but given his history she has to question the integrity of the man she married.  Has he really changed or is he reliving his past?  Whatever the case, his life is threatened and the truth will eventually prevail.With questions unanswered, Rachel goes to extremes to bring Gavin home to her and uncover a truth that defies even the greatest of lies.  The only comfort she finds is in Gavin's brother Ian.Who can she trust?  Who has the answers?I can't say enough of how I loved this book. By the end I was scratching my head and saying 'yeah, that just happened.'I cannot WAIT for book 3 to come out and hopefully will not have to wait too long. Annemarie Nikolaus hat die klassische Autorenregel "Show, don't tell" perfekt umgesetzt: Weit entfernt davon, ein Geschichtsbuch zu sein, vermittelt "Königliche Republik" dem Leser eine selten erreichte Nähe zur Protagonistin Mirella und ihren inneren und äußeren Konflikten, und führt den Leser zugleich durch die unterschiedlichen Lebensverhältnisse, in denen sich die Menschen jener Zeit wiederfanden. Geschichte kann spannend sein - wenn sie so erzählt wird.
summary: Ein großes Werk in jeder Hinsicht

this story fell flat for me. By page 2 you are already dealing with grammar issues that continue throughout the book. This story needs an editor, badly. That alone took this book from a 5star to a 3.  I was initially intrigued by the story line, because it is not the norm. A very popular author tackled this subject matter in another book and it was executed so well, that I was excited for this. My excitement ended around chapter 3.***SPOILERS AHEAD***First, I understand that Bobby Jack grew up in the life, but his continued disrespect of black people even while out with Whit was just too much for me to take. I don't know any self respecting black woman who would date a man that still refers to blacks as 'n*ggers' and such. It was understandable and even expected in the beginning, but once the relationship progressed, you would have thought his views would have changed. They didn't. The only black person he respected and didn't call names was Whit. The fact that Whit's neighbors encouraged the relationship was even more troubling.Second, there was no chemistry whatsoever between these two characters. I'm still trying to figure out why they are together besides the fact that he thought she was cute. Their dialogue was stilted and I felt no connection between them. Even the love scenes were mediocre.Third, being from Mobile, AL, I expected to read more about the place they lived in and the culture that would breed these two people. I didn't get any of that. The author says that she did research on hate groups, but I couldn't tell. If you're going to write a story about a white supremacist, then I need to believe it.Fourth, there didn't seem to be any conclusion to this story. I'm not sure if you were leaving the door open for a sequel or what, but the end felt completely rushed and incomplete. So does she keep the kid? Do they get married? Are they moving? Is Jessi dead from OD in prison? Does Whit do ANYTHING with her life? There were way too many questions.The saving grace of this story were the drag queens and even they were underused. This story had so much potential, but after reading it felt like a waste of time. Maybe my standards are high, but frankly for someone who has been in the game this long, there should be a little more attention to detail and character development.

According to William Faulkner, a major part of writing is being willing to "kill your darlings" - in other words, being willing to cut the pieces of writing you might love in service of the greater good of the book. It's a lesson that Reed Sprague could do with learning, because it's clear that Eddy's Current is just full of pieces of writing and character work that Sprague loves, but end up turning the book into a cluttered mess. There are intriguing bits here and there, and the overall story - a look at a religious talk show host who eventually rises to become a global demagogue and the people who struggle against him - isn't bad. But Eddy's Current is a book in deep need of an editor. Do we really need the entire text of the graduation speech that a rising intelligence agent hears as he graduates from his training? No, not really. Do we need meeting minutes for a bank that's helping to launder the demagogue's money (well, sort of)? No. And we don't need the backstory of characters who only come in for a chapter or two. And you could probably jettison the entire storyline about the freshman congressman and lose nothing from the book. Instead, Eddy's Current is meandering and overstuffed, and it ends up making little to no sense at big points simply because the reader loses track of the threads as much as Sprague does. (Sprague's tendency to switch perspectives without notice or warning doesn't help here, either.) There's lots of great bits in Eddy's Current, and I like how dedicated Sprague is to the backstories of his characters and their personalities. But he needs to learn what's necessary and what's not, and Eddy's Current is a book that's full of unnecessary details to the point where the actual plot of the book is almost impossible to find at times.
summary: A collection of enjoyable darlings that need to be killed

reviewText: The story begins right off with the main female character, Erica, trying to get home from shopping before her husband gets home. By the end of the first page, Shawn Harper is giving his wife a brutal beating. What makes the abuse even worse is his strength is magnified by also being a vampire. His abuse doesn't stop there as Erica is his source of blood. Her arms are badly scarred from his years of forcing her to provide for him.Erica is a typical abused woman who has reached the point where she knows she needs to get out before her husband kills her. She wants to leave, yet doesn't because for a couple of good reasons. Who would believe she's married to a vampire? Not knowing there are good vampires out there, She fears for the safety of everyone involved in her escape once Shawn learns she has left. Erica believes that Shawn was drawn to her because he knew she grew up in the state's foster care system. She had no family. Therefore, there was no one to care what happened to her.Kevin is a classmate who has become a good friend, offers to help her if and when she decides she's ready to leave her husband. Unknown to her, is that he's also a vampire. From here the story is fairly predictable, the differences between this and similar stories are in the details. This is the first time I've read one in the abused wife genre where the husband is a vampire.I wasn't riveted to this story. I can't say I read it through unable to set the book down and do something else. The conversations are somewhat stilted in a mix of formal and informal dialog. There is a lack of consistency in the use of contractions when characters are speaking. This makes for a somewhat less than easy read. My mind kept wanting to correct this problem which interfered with having a chance to enjoy the story. There are some issues with grammar, mainly in the tense of the words used. While there are no egregious errors, I do feel this book would benefit from additional beta reading and/or editing. I was gifted a copy of this book by the author in exchange for an honest review.

My rating: 5 of 5 starsI got this book from the author for an honest review. The 7th Day written by Nika Lubitsch was published originally in Germany. This book is the number one bestselling kindle book in Germany. I just finished the English translation and I now know why this book is so popular in Germany. In part one of the book, we find a 38 year old Sybelle Thalheim  on trial for the murder of her husband , Michael. As Sybelle sits in front of the judges ,while witness after witness testifies about Sybelle, most of them eager to paint her in a bad light, she thinks back to when she first met her husband, the close friendship they had with her defense lawyer, Ulli and his wife, Gabi. She recalls the courtship, the marriage, the life they built together.  Sybelle's life was going very well. Both she and Michael had good careers, they were financially comfortable, they had a good marriage. The only thing they still wanted was a child. When Sybelle finally conceives, her life seems complete. But five days after announcing her pregnancy, her husband disappears into thin air. In part two- the author shifts into another gear. We now get to hear the story from Sybelle. We learn of the absolute destitution Sybelle comes to after her husband disappears, and is then told he is suspected of stealing money- millions of dollars. Sybelle loses everything, and I do mean EVERYTHING. It would only be natural to feel anger toward her husband. She has moments of rage, depression, and then just finds herself going through the motions of life, not really caring about anything anymore. Then out of the blue, a clue! Was Michael still alive? Has he been seen? If so, she plans to find him , and yes, she intended to do him bodily harm. But, did she murder her husband? Sybelle doesn't know herself.In the  last portion of the book, all the shocking revelations come to light. When all is explained and all the ends tied, keep on reading! The last few pages of the book reveals a final shocking twist. This book is stunning. I was amazed. I read a great deal, so I've become a little stingy with five star ratings. I had no idea what to think about his book when I was first approached by the author's representatives. I knew it was an independent author, and that the book was a mystery and had been translated from German to English, but not much else.  So, I have to say I was riveted from the very beginning. The author's writing style is like nothing I've read before. She switches from third to first person, but I never found it confusing or annoying. In fact, it was the style and the layers of the story and the way it was presented that kept me turning pages. I just had to find out what happened the night Michael was murdered. I had to know if Sybelle was guilty or not. I had to know if Michael was guilty and why he would do something like that. The ultimate justice is finally served in the end. You will find yourself  mulling over the events and thinking maybe you would like to read the book again. You all know that only really special books get a re-read from me. This book would appeal to those who like legal thrillers, psychological thrillers, and mysteries.I researched the author a little after I finished the book and found her bio very interesting. Check this book out! The English version is  available in the kindle store. Overall an A+
summary: Riveting! Legal drama, psycologica thriller and mystery! Don't miss this one!

I really enjoyed this book, I couldn't put it down! This was well written with very good character development. The main character is battling some demons that carry over into subsequent books. Having not read the first in the series I was able to easily follow the storyline and character development with no problem. The author does a great job of filling the reader in with enough information so as not to be lost. This book can easily be read as a stand alone. I look forward to reading the other books in the series.

Paleo Breakfast Reciepes: For Busy Moms and Dads - Tyler DanielsThe Paleo Breakfast Recipe book is absolutely fantastic if you need nutritious breakfast ideas. I was thinking about going on the Paleo diet but wasn't sure what it would be like; this book taught me that limiting my diet doesn't mean I can't still have a variety of food. From crepes to smoothies and muffins, this book has provided me with interesting recipes that fit perfectly into my lifestyle.The recipes themselves are very creative and taste delicious.  One of the best things I have found is that they are also relatively easy to make and don't take very long. I don't actually have any children, but I still find this recipe book incredibly helpful. Whether it's a rushed morning, or a lazy Saturday, I can try my hand at different recipes that are sure to keep my fiancé and me healthy.I think the book is set out very well and the instructions are very easy to follow, which I think is very important. I've had too many recipe books in the past that have simply been too complicated for me to follow! Daniels presents the recipes in a clear and simple way that is very effective.I've found that since I have spent time making and having breakfast every day I have been a lot more energized right from the start of the day. I have heard many people say that breakfast is the most important meal of the day, and I can finally see why, as there has been an obvious difference in my life.Overall, this book is very well written and easy to follow. This book is definitely not just for those who have children either. I would definitely recommend it to anyone seeking healthy breakfast recipes, especially if you are on the paleo diet.

reviewText: Purchased earlier today and decided to start it as I was laying down for a nap. This is a cute shorter read following the trials one teen faces when her school decides to host a Sadie Hopkins dance. Everything seems fine until her friends start getting dates for the dance and then she starts a downhill spiral that leaves her with not only no date but setting up the dance completely by herself.Does she get her man in the end? This Time Next Year was a really sweet story.  Not at all how I anticipated describing a story about a young woman falling in love with a vampire after having her mother killed by one right in front of her when she was six, but its true nonetheless.To me it was sweet because it is a well told and convincing story of how two souls traumatized by the same event, and who have suffered alone for the past twenty years, find healing and love with each other. They share a bond formed by the tragedy to make them each two halves of a whole.  It's also very romantic in that Kiernan protected Moira after that night and did all that was necessary to insure her safety. When he lost track of her he searched twenty years to find her again knowing she might hate him just for being what he was, a vampire. Yet he needed to explain and tell her how sorry he was for his part in her mother's death. Hoping to give her some closure and peace from her nightly torments. Not daring to believe she'd offer or want more or could ever return his love.This sweet, beautiful, sensual, love story is a short, quick read but leaves you with a warm fuzzy impression.~Complimentary copy received as a contest prize.

reviewText: Wow...i'm sitting here, just having finished reading "Arsen" and i'm seriously at a loss as to what to write in my review.NEVER, have I ever had such a hard time figuring out what I wanted to write for a review. It wasn't that the book was bad, actually it was VERY GOOD. It's the emotions that it has stirred within me, are so conflicting. I loved it for it's story of true love because that is what Cathy and Ben had. I hated it for it's story of betrayl and deceit. I loved it for it's steamy scenes and hated it for the selfishness that Cathy showed throughout the book.In the beginning of the book you are presented with a whirlwind romance. You get to witness true love in all its glory. Then, in once brief moment, you get to sit by and watch that love crash and burn. One minute you're feeling euphoric and the next you want to throw yourself on the floor and cry. I can't say that I hate Cathy. Don't get me wrong, she is horrible for what she did, to both Ben and Arsen, as well as herself, but I feel sorry and sad for her. She just wanted to be a mother. She pinned all her hopes and dreams on each pregnancy. Then when the pregnancies ended...she was left trying to pick up the pieces of her heart, which everytime it broke, they got smaller and smaller. Harder and harder to put back together. Why didn't Ben or her doctor INSIST that she speak with a therapist? Maybe this whole mess could have been avoided.  She KNEW what she was doing when she started hanging out with Arsen....deep down she KNEW it was wrong.. yet she continued to do it anyway. Shame on her.Ben....I had a love/hate relationship with him as well. He had a possessive streak in him that didn't sit well with me. He was so loving, caring and attentive but also it felt like something was brewing just below the surface. It also made me so mad, that he didn't fight for Cathy. He just let Arsen swoop in and he didn't even really do anything. He KNEW Cathy was cheating and he just sat there and took it. I wanted him to fight. Fight for their love, their future. It broke my heart when Cathy came clean with Ben. I wanted to take him in my arms and soothe him, but at the same time I wanted to smack him upside his head.Arsen..I think I felt the most for him. Even though he was the "other man," he was still a person...a person who was hurting too after loosing someone he loved. He found Cathy and their souls seemed to recognize the sadness within them and that was it. That sealed their fate. I think he wanted Cathy to say "No" and stick to it. To truly be his friend (even though the sexual tension was there), to help him heal too and somehow he got pulled into the abyss of despair right along with Cathy.The story was well written and flowed nicely. I loved how we got to see everyone's perspectives. I loved the switch from "past" to "present." The author writes in a way that makes you feel you are right there watching it all happen. Her characters are developed in such a way that you literally feel the emotions they are going through. The plot twist toward the end was surprising....I didn't expect that. The ending left me feeling fulfilled but also bereft at the same time. I don't want to spoil it so I won't go into details. Overall I would recommend this book. It does had difficult subject matter that not everyone will be comfortable reading but it's still an amazing book!
This delivers more than you first think. I appreciate that it was not overly formulaic, was full of humour and engaging characters. Good fun.

I had a weird yet recurring thought while I was reading this book: I sure miss Harry Potter. That parallel universe sort of world where certain parts were everyday and familiar, but even better, many parts were not. People dress differently, there are otherworldly creatures, they have their own school and there is magic. Lots of magic. The thing is, you could really see that world from JK Rowling's descriptions and immerse yourself until you felt like you could live there. On occasion, I got glimpses of an similarly interesting world while reading The Doorknob Society. Now, don't get your wands in a twist - this book is a far cry from the tales of our beloved Mr. Potter. I will say this, though: having read over 100 books in the past year, the vast majority of them in the young adult genre, I just realized that I miss a good made-up story where the unusual is the norm.Chloe Masters is the daughter of a magician. She and her parents have been traveling around the world her whole life while her parents perform their magic show. Unfortunately, Chloe's Mom leaves with no explanation when Chloe is six. Now 16, Chloe is about to have her world turned upside down when she finds out that her father, Elijah, is no amateur magician. Chloe decides to help when she and her dad are forbidden to leave France and their passports are confiscated. Trying to retrieve them, she accidentally activates an unknown power, which propels her through a portal and back into her hotel room. Promising to explain everything when they get home, that promise gets put on hold  when a evil-looking man emerges into their hotel room...from another portal. Elijah escapes with Chloe to their family home in Cape May, New Jersey.Though Chloe has innumerable questions, her father remains tight-lipped for the most part. What he does say, however, stuns Chloe: they are staying in Cape May, there is something called the Doorknob Society and she is to attend Paladin Academy. In addition, there are more groups like the Society: The Skeleton Key Guild, the Mapmakers Union, the Impossible Engineers, and the Honorable and Venerable Order of Detective Inspectors who are known collectively as the Old Kind. Not all factions get along, but they are required to at the Academy. Chloe soon meets Michael Slade, a cute boy who seems to already like her. Her group of friends grows to include Edgar Manus, a student who has declared for the Mapmaker's Union. Their adventures begin immediately, when Chloe begins to hear rumors about her parents and her father's banishment from the Doorknob Society. She is determined to find out the truth, which also could possibly lead to figuring out why her mother left.She soon meets her match in James Nightshade, a member of the Skeleton Key Guild and fellow student. He's a snarky and irritating person, with whom, against her wishes, she feels a connection. The last member of their group is James' friend, Jessica. After a rough beginning, she and Chloe discover that they are more than enemies - they are cousins. United when their grandmother is attacked, they swear to get whomever is behind it.This story is a whirlwind; as Chloe knows nothing of her family history, the Old Kind or her powers, she gets dumped, completely clueless, in the center of a fight that started well before she was born. Despite her inexperience, and due to her stubbornness, she is immediately catapulted into an unfamiliar word with real-world consequences. To top it off, Michael is pursuing her affections. Is there time for that? Does she want it? For now, her father is missing, his nemesis is demanding her full cooperation, and a detective inspector is on her tail. Who can she trust?My main issue with this book is my pettest of peeves: bad grammar! The most perplexing, of all things, was the author's use (misuse, to be precise) of the question mark. I thought most people had that one down? (See how I used it in that previous sentence.) For some reason, Mr. Fletcher put question marks at the end of sentences that weren't questions at all. It was seriously annoying, as they were quite plentiful. I started reading the sentences like questions in my head. In addition, the sentence structure was poor. There were many run-on sentences that were begging for some form of punctuation, as well as a few spelling mishaps (to/too; past/passed). Lastly, word usage. I don't know what a "mouthy smile" is, for example. A good editor can help with these issues.The story itself is interesting and I do like the world that was created. I think Chloe's repetitive chant of "I'm broken" is a little heavy-handed, mainly because it seems to only be a device to keep her from being with Michael. When she does kiss Michael, she seems to wholeheartedly like him. In addition, her relationship with James is a little confusing. I get it that she doesn't know why she has a connection with him; it just makes her "submissions" to Michael ring false. As a reader, it could eventually alienate me since Michael has done nothing except, well, everything Chloe has asked him to do. It seems like drama is being inserted in the wrong place. Obviously, I don't know where either relationship is headed, but there is going to have to be some kind of resolution before Chloe starts to have feelings for her own cousin to boot.The animosity between the groups of the Old Kind isn't sufficiently explained, either. I think that would make the relationships and the drama more understandable and believable. And where are Jessica's parents? Yes, you should save some of the information/drama for future volumes, but you have to answer the obvious ones, even if only obtusely. Give the reader something.In spite of the grammatical issues, I am giving the story 3 stars. I am very intrigued. I would love for the next book to be a little bit more leisurely in its pacing so the characters can take a breath every now and then and so I, as the reader, can immerse myself more fully into their world. I hope that makes sense? Sorry. Had to.3 of 5 StarsThe Doorknob Society by MJ Fletcher was published February 9, 2012 by Smashwords. A free copy of this book was given to Ink and Page in return for an honest review.

What a great read!  In this story, Chapel gives the reader first person narrative from both two protagonists.  I love this device - you see both sides of the story while also getting a great feel for the personalities of each character.  The "inside" look of both protagonists was rich and unique - I loved, LOVED Whit, and Tucker was a beautiful mess - so my only complaint about the book is that it was TOO SHORT.  I wanted more!  I felt this about Chapel's Marine stories too, though at least we got two of those.  Janey Chapel - please write longer books.Chapel's spare style is wonderful and more than so many women authors in this genre, she seems to capture what men would actually do and say (I am tired of women authors who portray gay men like sterotypical "girls" - and I'm a woman, so don't mean for this comment to impugn my own sex, but still...)  I like reading stories where men are men and love each other.  This was one such story, I just wish it were longer!

These serialized erotic romances are taking the Romance World by storm! Every time I log in to Facebook or other social media, I see more and more coming out! Ever since then, I have been devouring these like crazy! I LOVE them! If you want a sexy, suspenseful, quick read, a serial series is the way to go. The WHITE COLLARED Series by Shelly Bell had me gagged, bound, and held hostage from Part One and on. I was lucky to receive all four parts all at once, and let me tell you, THANK GOD! I’m not sure if I could have waited a single day in between parts. Luckily for fans, you do not have to wait too long to have the next part available to you.❝We all carry scars. Some are just more visible than others.❞Ms. Bell had me hooked by the end of Chapter One. Holy ****! My heart was racing and I immediately wanted to know who, what, when, where, and why?! We get a great sense of each character and what their background is. Kate, Nicholas, and Jaxon are AMAZING characters, and they each bring such complexity and raw emotion to the table. You instantly crave more and more of their story. With each part of this series unfolding, the more intense it gets. Erotic isn’t enough to cover what this series was for me. Don’t get me wrong, White Collared is a SCORCHING read, but along with that came the thrilling suspense, and the emotional downfall of certain events. With every page and every chapter came new ideas, new questions, and new plot twists. I couldn’t turn away from these words that left me speechless at the conclusion of each part. This was a VERY WELL DONE serial, and it has created another Super Fan for this incredibly talented author. I’m keeping this series close to me, because when I’m feeling in a funk, and I need a pick me up, I believe re-reading the White Collared Series will be my DRUG OF CHOICE!*Gifted copy provided by the publisher in exchange for an honest review*
summary: Sexy and intense conclusion to an amazing series!

reviewText: I get so bored and exasperated with "template" romance stories, so this story was very refreshing!!  This book was entirely engaging from cover to cover.  I felt the characters were presented with great depth and completeness.  Other reviewers criticized what they felt was harshness of some of the interaction between the main characters, but I felt the story, interactions and dialog were *extremely realistic*.  Actually, I thought the characters exercised a great deal of restraint (more than I would have!), which I chalked up to their having been in the relationship for years. I was never sure how the story would evolve, which also kept me rather enthralled and totally engaged.  I will absolutely look for more from this author.

The Doormen proves that Zack is one remarkable writer and I can't wait to read more from him. The Doorman is Brilliant. For Full Review go here:[...]Central Park Song *5 Stars*Let me say that this was one of the most creative and beautiful stories I have ever read. I loved that Zack wasn't afraid to write something completely different than most authors.  He did an amazing job with this screenplay and I am so honored I got to read it because I really enjoyed it and fell in love with the story. It's absolutely delightful. For Full Review go here: [...]So if you love reading new books that will have you questioning things, crying, ranting, and laughing you need to give this one a read. Because each of these books will have your emotions crazy, but in a good way.

I heard by way of the grapevine that Maggie Carpenter was working on a book involving a cowboy and a show jumper, and I couldn't wait! I was not disappointed. Full disclosure: I’m an “old” person, a 30-something business owner and your average go-getter trying to create a future for myself and my family, while not losing my identity. I read this book because I wanted to understand my own reaction of abhorrence to the millennials I see doing nothing, producing nothing, going nowhere. They’re the ones that sack my groceries, that smell like weed, that never seem to be contributing. This is the opposite of me entirely, but I’m an honest enough and curious enough person not to judge, but to learn what the source of the millennial generation is. This book provided me with the answers I was seeking and the understanding I was hoping for. I get it now.The voice of the author is as authentic and joltingly honest as I’ve ever read. At first, I was shocked by it and the wide array of topics the author covers, from religion, to drugs, to virginity, to how to break and enter, to flatulence. This book is like walking into an art gallery expecting to see the works of Van Gogh and instead seeing a gallery of Salvador Dali paintings and an entire wall of risqué nudes. And then, just when you think you’re offended enough, you see the beauty in the Dali’s and the nudes and realize it was your own worldview that was short, that was cramping you and making you uncomfortable, not the honesty of Dali and nudes.The author’s writing style is engaging and raw, completely non-traditional and not at all cliché. The author wrote this book his way, which is a work of art in itself and consistent with the types of topics covered.My only advice to you when you read this book is this: finish it. Wait until the end, until you’ve read all, and then spend a few days letting the author’s wisdom sink in before deciding how you feel about this book. And by all means, if you’ve ever wanted to understand teenagers, young adults, why society is what it is, read this book. The truth will blow your mind.

reviewText: “Stxeamtown” by John Reinhold Dizon is the story of Trip and Lyrica. They are Abovegrounders; living on different rooftops in a subculture that survives on the rooftops unknown to the Grounders below due to the constant steam that obscures visibility. Steam is their primary power source.Abovegrounders are held to strict rules. Those who don’t follow those rules are “crossed-out,” by given a lobotomy, and sent to the ground below. Those who don’t cause trouble upon reaching the age of 30, too, are banished.I especially loved the way the two lovers communicate before they finally meet: through mirrors and Morse code messages.What follows is an exciting entertaining read with Trip and Lyrica as young hero's that want to bring change and improvement to their world but meet complications and several culture clashes that need to be resolved in unique ways.It's set in a original futuristic world with interesting concepts and social structure, vivid characters and a surprisingly intricate plot,where one can easily find one self lost in and one that resembles our own world.A highly recommended read if you enjoy Dystopian/steampunk and SciFi, you won't be disappointed! It was well written with a good combination of action and narrating. I'm looking forward to read more of Trip and Lyrica!(I received a free copy for review purposes)

I seriously want to gush over the cover for a minute before I go into my review.The cover alone had me sold on reading this book.  I love the colors chosen  for the cover and how the cover models are placed....and the dress of course is GORGEOUS!!!Sera Miller had a very rough life when she was younger and when her mother passed away, she went off to Waywroth Academy where she learned how to become a very proper woman and to keep herself from being disgraced from society.  She never knew who took care of the expense of going to the Academy and when she finds who the person is that helped her...she is more in shock than ever.Digger, otherwise known as Fletcher Thomas now has always felt compelled to protect and look after Sera.  He has known for awhile and all he wants is for her to be happy and be loved.  He knows he did bad things when he was younger, but he's trying to make up for it.He wants to help Sera further than giving money for her to attend school and now he wants her to help him be accepted into society as well.When Sera decides to help she is thrown into a world where she's not used to and a world where she wanted to avoid at all cost.  Fletcher keeps being a very difficult man to be with and she cannot help, but start to really have feelings for him.She's even being threaten in Fletcher's home to leave, but she has no idea who the culprit is.It's going to be very difficult for Sera to keep herself proper around the handsome Fletcher, especially when he tends to be there for her whenever she needs him the most.Lorelei Brown gives you a historical romance that has a lot of angst, romance, and sweetness.She gives you two characters that you will rooting to get together because they are made for each other.  They have known each other for awhile and it also helps when you have the sexy Fletcher trying everything to let Sera know he loves her and then Sera trying to fight her feelings, but she just cannot after so long.  It's inevitable.  =)Fletcher is definitely a character who I adore a lot of in the story.  He had his bad ways, but when he was around Sera, he was different.  He stole my heart and when the steaminess happen between him and Sera....yeah...he kind of stole my heart more.Sera got on my nerves during certain parts of the book, especially towards the ending.  She kind of overreacted over something and I felt bad for poor Fletcher.  Although, Sera did have qualities I loved about her.  She could be difficult at times because she was all about not being snubbed by society...but she did put Fletcher in his place several times in the book when he truly needed someone to.Overall this book definitely was a very enjoyable and sexy book from the very talented Lorelei Brown, who readers know her as Katie Porter.  I had a hard time in certain parts, but other times I had to keep turning the page on my iPad.  I am a sucker for a historical romance book though because I love when a author can make me feel like I am back in time and that is what Lorelei Brown did.I look forward to reading more of Lorelei Brown's books in the very near future.I give "Wayward One" 4 full moons and highly recommend it to historical romance readers out there.I received a complimentary copy of the book from the author in exchange for an honest review.

Ms. Bitch by David Weaver ♥♥♥♥ (SEMI-SPOILER REVIEW)I am very aware of Author David Weaver, but in all honestly; this is my first reading of his written work. Prior to the subject mention book been released, Mr. Weaver posted via his Facebook page for about a week, a sample per day of this book `Ms. B****.' From the very first posting of this book excerpt, I decided this would be the first novel of his I will read. By, the last posting, I uncomplainingly waited for the release date and purchased without hesitation.In this tale, you will met Veronica Lakes, cousin of Kyla Powers - - "Wife of Bankroll Squad Boss - Malcolm Powers." The story is giving mainly from Veronica's point of view. With many tribulations in her past, it truly prevailed her from been the woman she should have been. In results, caused her mental condition to intensify. Despite this, when in her healthy stable mind, she is not `Ms. B****.' However, with revenge on the mind, as an adult, she wants to give a gift to the person who caused her the utmost agony. In return, a jail term for Ten (10) years was her gift. Once released from prison, Veronica does her best to occupy herself with positive thoughts. A new woman. Yet, when reality slaps her in the face, she crumbles. Her life changes, from 0 mph to 80 mph in a matter of hours.The storyline, going to be straightforward I thought would have been foreseeable, yet just when I thought I figured it out, the author twisted the plot. However, the character expansion lacks a bit of depth. The character development seemed rushed. I am always looking for more in-depth thoughts, but still in all, pleasingly done base on the page length. In regards to editing it was near perfect, with just an error of consistency in information about 52-53% within the story, personally it did not bother me; just wanted to make note in case this is an issue for another.I wonder if a Part 2 of `Ms. B****,' will be published or is this the end. Love on the run, will they get help or captured by the law? I would like to see if Veronica and Memra love survives each other's madness. In spite of their deranged mind at times, Memra and Veronica are what both of them need in each other lives. Memra is what Veronica needs to stay in a stable mind, and for once genuine love from a man; Veronica is what Memra needs, real friendship, loyalty and love.Overall, a worthy Urban/Romance/Street short story.

Year of the Monkey was a thoroughly engrossing read. Russell Payne is an army journalist who never has the Vietnam bush experience firsthand.  Willingham comes into the picture and changes everything.  Coming from very different experiences in Vietnam, these two characters really need to decide who they can trust.  This book offers a unique perspective as to the dangers not only in the jungles during the war but also the political and personal dramas that are not often the focus of war stories.  Year of the Monkey also explores the relationship between the American troops and the Vietnamese who have been affected by war for years.  It begs the question of who is the good guy and who is the bad guy and can that distinction even be made.  This book makes it apparent that the only threat for GIs is not necessarily from the VC, but potentially from the CIA and their own personal demons from the past.  Highly recommended read.*I received a complimentary copy of this book in exchange for my review*

The Art of TouchJared Hamilton has an aversion to meddlesome people. Nevertheless, this does not stop his secretary or his uncle from interfering with Jared's health and well-being, since Jared's life consist of work only. Bullied into visiting massage therapist Kyle Washburn, Jared is prepared to find fault with wasting his time for a massage. However, the experience opens up a whole new relaxed world Jared did not believe possible.The Art of Touch is an amusing romantic short story. Jared and Kyle have contradictory personalities but somehow manage to fall in love. Jared is a rich workaholic lawyer, who enjoys wielding power over everyone. Buried beneath the granite exterior, Jared is a lonely man who fears rejections. Kyle is a man who is afraid of making the wrong choices. Kyle is able to break through Jared's tough shell and find Jared's compassionate side. Jared and Kyle's personality conflicts soon bonds into a promising relationship.Dominique Frost has created an engaging, as well as an especially enjoyable saga.

This is really more of a 2 and a half star book for me, but because it wasn't made clear that it was a novella, I'm not in the mood to give the extra half star for benefit of the doubt.  I really wanted to like this story.  The premise was enchanting, the characters were very likeable and believable, but the middle of the story just wasn't there.  They literally went from her hating him and him being indifferent to her to them quite suddenly thinking about each other all of the time and wanting to be together.  It was almost as if the author had written this perfectly good novel and then right before it was sent out, some editor decided that it needed to be a novella (yeah, it's not full length and they don't tell you that either or I wouldn't have even bought this) and just chopped out the middle without giving the author time to go back and rework it.I also felt that there was never any reason given for why the male lead (I've forgotten his name already) didn't have any clue as to why everyone thought he was a jerk for giving the female lead's (forgot her name too) dogs away less than a week after her step-father died.  There's also no real progression from his inexplicably wanting the dogs gone to him deciding to get most of them back for her and suddenly deciding that he loves them all and does want them all around.  There's also some ridiculous bit about her deciding to marry some male friend of hers that she suddenly realized is kind of revolting, as if that hadn't been pretty clear before.I was very disappointed that this was a novella, they don't call it that, don't give an amount of pages, just a file size, which is meaningless to someone whose not familiar with what that means as far as book length.  I only paid a dollar, but since I don't usually buy novellas, I feel cheated for even having spent that.  I would be willing to try a full length novel by this author on the strength of her ability to come up with a good premise and likeable characters, also the strength of the first part of the book, it was pretty good and went at a nice pace, hence my confusion when the story suddenly skipped to the end.

Unfortunately for her, one of the group is her ex-boyfriend Ben. She didn't really want Ben to be an Ex but he broke up with her for reasons that weren't really her fault so she can't do anything to fix it. She's cool, strong but yet there's sweet and softness in there too.Ben is kind of an idiot at times but I still really liked him. He broke up with Lindsey for complicated reasons that he eventually realizes wasn't even truly the case. He misses Lindsey and while on the trip to the convention, Ben finds himself considering where things went wrong between them. One thing he realizes is that Lindsey is interested in a BDSM relationship and had actually been trying to tell him that before the breakup. Ben realizes this is something he needs but has been rejecting in himself. When he realizes this is what Lindsey needs he knows he can't reject it any more and decides to explore it.Ben actually goes to Ivan and Cami (the couple from the first book) to talk and gets some advice to get him started down the path. When Ben first starts using the "Dom vibe" on Lindsey I think they're both surprised at how much it works for them both. They start exploring BDSM with each other but there isn't a lot of discussion so neither knows exactly where this is going. Lindsey loves being back with Ben but afraid that the BDSM is something Ben's just doing to get back with her and wont want to keep it up long term. reviewText: Find Yourself: A Poet’s Journey is a beautiful book of poems that incite mindfulness, introspection, and appreciation of the world around us.Author Feng Zhou brings us this charming collection of his poetry. I always start reading an indie published novel with a bit of trepidation. An independently published book can either be very good or very bad. There's rarely a happy middle. I'm pleased to report that Between the Land and the Sea falls into the it-kicked-ass category! The story is overflowing with intrigue, budding romance and paranormal goodies. Also, the characters are well-developed and engaging. And finally, who doesn't love a good mermaid story!?My favorite part of this book would have to be the story line. The pace is great. Derrolyn Anderson reveals just enough to keep the plot interesting without giving up too much and as a result, readers are left guessing until the end. There's also a few nice side stories that run parallel to the main one and they compliment each other well. Among them are the blooming romance between the two main characters, Cruz's growing fashion career and Marina's cryptic origins. Needless to say, there's never a dull moment! Having multiple plots can sometimes be dangerous because you run the risk of the story becoming too weighed down and confusing. Rest assured that that's not the case here. Derrolyn maintains a nice balance throughout this book.Ethan is a mega hunk! I'm ashamed to admit that I was crushing pretty hardcore on him because he's only 18. Darn these Young Adult novels for making me feel like a perv! He has that sexy, doesn't-try-too-hard, surfer look going on. Ethan's hot but doesn't really seem to know it or at least he doesn't flaunt it. Plus he's a hard worker and is taking planning for his future quite seriously which is a rare trait to find in someone so young. Okay, I need to stop swooning over this guy! Moving on... Marina's story is quite fascinating as well. I enjoyed how she slowly discovers the truth of her past by bits and pieces. I couldn't help from speculating on the possibilities. It turns out that I was right but I still appreciated the journey. The only thing about Marina's personality that irked me a bit is that she's fiercely independent. She keeps everything to herself thinking that no one will understand but when she finally reveals all her friends are super sympathetic. Surprise, surprise!As the book drew to a close I started to get a little worried that Derrolyn was going to leave me stuck with a killer cliff hanger. I was immensely relieved when I got to the last page and that wasn't the case. There's still some questions that are left unanswered which made me crave the next installment but overall I was satisfied. Between the Land and the Sea is one of the better mermaid books on the market and if book one is anything to go by, The Moon and the Tide is looking like a sweet read!
summary: One of the better mermaid books on the market

This novella is part of the Don’t Tell series, but it can be read as a standalone, which is what I’ve done without any problems.This is a different world, taking place sometime in the year 2070, where there are basically two sides of a conflict with the MC’s fighting for opposite sides. They meet on the battlefield, where their attraction and initial encounter lead to future secret trysts that contain some extremely hot sex scenes. But, there is a lot more to these guys than just amazing sex. With their relationship seemingly doomed from the start, and while they don’t have it easy, they are able to overcome and fall in love.In Mayce’s world, men must breed with the opposite sex to further their agenda. Homosexuality is expressly forbidden. And, truthfully, Mayce hasn’t had any trouble with that, until he meets Hawke, who just seems to bring him to life. He wakes up desires and feelings in Mayce that change his whole outlook on what he’s been taught and conditioned to believe.Hawke is a freelander, or Nomad, fighting for freedom to live as they wish. They fight “For freedom. For truth. For all people.” “Live in freedom, love at will.” He falls just as hard for Mayce, and even though they fight for different sides, they continue to allow their feelings to grow.This was such a hot, fast read! I flew through it and didn’t want it to end. I will definitely be going back to read the full stories in this series. This was my first book by Ms. Warren, and it for sure won’t be my last. It had just the right amount of everything for me. Not too much futuristic detail, didn’t take too long to get to the good stuff, had enough action and grit to be exciting, and had a bit of romance with a happy ending to boot. FINDING MY PRINCE CHARMING (FINDING MY PRINCE CHARMING 1) by J.S. COOPERI really think that J.S. Cooper is one of the best authors out there who writes beautiful, engaging and simply irresistible short romance stories out there. I have been a fan ever since I have read The Private Club serial but even before that, I have other of her previous books in my TBR list. I love the blurb in most if not all of her books and I will honestly say that she does not disappoint. And this book sure will not disappoint you.Finding My Prince Charming will make you giddy, laugh, feel good, hot & bothered and will make you embrace the world of art and I really like it because she incorporated art in her story that somehow it teaches you or introduces you to the world of wonderful artists in history. I feel like I am in college again and it truly fascinates me. It was one of my minor subjects in college and it's nice to experience it again. You will also have this love-hate relationship with the characters she created.Lola is an american exchange student studying in London with her BFF. I like her, she is not timid but she is not wild either. When she met Xavier, there was instant attraction and one thing lead to another that they ended up sleeping together. But it didn't occur to Lola that Xavier would be her professor so imagine her shock when she entered the classroom and there he is as her teacher.I like professor-student love stories but this one is different, it has a twist. A good one but I hate Xavier. He is such an arrogant a-hole that I wanna slap his face. I didn't like the fact that keeps insulting Lola even if it's a joke or a way to piss her off. They say guys are sometimes stupid especially if they feel something different or new because of a girl and that's why they keep on teasing that girl. That is exactly what Xavier is doing. Like I said, stupid a-hole. But I still think a person should never ever make a joke like what he did. I also didn't like that Lola is not aggressive enough to correct Xavier. I mean, she did but it's like she's holding back. Like she'd rather let him insult her than correct or argue with him. Well, she likes him so maybe that's why. But still... UGH! I feel it's so unfair on her part and the fact that she is a good person and she's a sweet girl, she deserves more and how Xavier treated her pisses me off.Don't get me wrong. I like the story. It is good and I can't wait for more but like I said, love-hate relationship, most especially to Xavier. I hope in book 2 we get to see a stronger Lola and someone who will make Xavier make up for it. Or like for once, she'll say not to him. Or maybe grand gesture kind of way. I mean, cmon! Lola deserves someone who will treat her good and make her feel loved. And in this book, Xavier is not that guy.IDK how book 2 will play out. There are things that will be revealed and I don't have any idea how Xavier and Lola will handle it. IDK what to expect but I will sure wait to find out. If you're a fan of J.S. Cooper or if you have read one or two of her books then you will definitely love this new addition to her lovely creations. :)4 1/2
summary: Another lovely creation from JS Cooper and sure you will want more.

I love Christine Nolfi's writing style. So pure. A pleasure to read! I have read several of her books, but The Dream You Make is my favorite so far. I totally fell in love with Annie. She has what my Mom would call "personality-plus"! I could hear her voice and picture her through this book like a movie. (Speaking of movies, this book would make a great one!) I laughed when she showed her spunky side at work and with co-workers, empathized with her having to live on a shoestring, grieved her family history, was moved to tears by her growing relationship with and custody fight for her orphaned nephew Dillon, loved her best friendship with Miriam and, of course, rooted and wooted for Michael. Michael, Michael, Michael. Exceptionally generous, executive boss extraordinaire. Broken by his first marriage. Bowled over by Annie, but didn't know how complicated her life was and Annie wasn't good at divulging secrets. There were so many wonderful secondary characters in this story. They each played an important role. I particularly loved the employees of Michael's firm, Rowe Industries, a colorful crew whose antics caused me to cry with laughter. And, finally, the couple fighting Annie for custody of Dillon, the Englands. This book is a romance, but at its core it illustrates the adoption process. While the main story revolves around one side's POV, we do get brief glimpses into the other - enough to form our own opinion of which side should win. The author pulls no punches, but handles the issue with grace and aplomb. I highly recommend this book to everyone. I've made a goal for 2014 to read all of the books Christine Nolfi has written. Anyone with me?
