Emma Turner lives in a tiny house with her two small children, Sarah and Ben. Their father, Larry, was killed in action three years earlier in Iraq. Life has never been the same for Emma...and that includes Christmas. Her Christmas spirit isn't there, and no amount of Christmas decorations or presents is ever going to bring back her dead husband.Jake Nicklaus is a fireman who once served with Larry in Iraq. But when a broken leg side-lines Jake, Larry takes his place. When Larry doesn't make it home, Jake vows to keep Emma and the kids safe.Larry visits with Emma every Christmas eve. It's the one time of year that she looks forward to because she can see him, talk to him, feel him. This year, though, she misses her chance to talk with him. With every passing year, she loses more and more of the Christmas spirit. However, she doesn't know, nor want to bring the Christmas spirit into her house. To her, that would mean moving on, and she's not ready to "let go" of Larry yet.Even the children feel their dead father's presence around them. Sarah even talks to the "soldier", doing what he asks. In his wake, he always leaves something behind...a few feathers. Whenever he likes/dislikes something, he leaves feathers behind as a symbol that he was there.Larry also visits Jake, but this year is different. This year, Larry isn't too happy with Jake and his "idea" of keeping Emma and the kids happy, healthy and safe.Can Jake bring back the spirit of Christmas into Emma's heart, into the children's lives again? Can Emma ever let go of Larry long enough to see what is in front of her?This book was a feel-good romance for the Christmas season. It had the elements of sexual tension, but there really wasn't any. He would brush up against her and that area would "warm" to his touch. Maybe a blush would come to her cheeks. But no real sexual tension involved. I was a little disappointed in this area.All in all, I liked how the author incorporated the ghost into the story, even making him "real" for a short time so that he could speak to his family. His leaving little feathers behind was the author's way of showing that the ghost was there. However, the ghost left behind the feathers regardless of whether he was angry or happy. That got a little confusing. The ghost at one point pushed Jake down, showing his anger by making it look as if Jake had slipped in the snow/ice, but there were always these little feathers around.Also, the author never goes into the significance of the feathers. Is this supposed to mean Larry's an angel? Or that when he died, there was a dead bird beside him? Maybe he killed the bird? No one knows. The story never mentioned the reason behind the feather's as the ghost's calling card.As for the story, it was a little weak. It was a light read, easy for this time of year when everyone is so busy, but it would have been better as a full length novel. This book gave me a few tears at the end, a wonderful visual of Larry, and I felt myself falling in love with Jake throughout the book. He was strong, sexy and attentive to the children and Emma. He was the reason that I continued to keep reading. For a sweet holiday romance, I give this book 3 stars.
summary: Bringing back the spirit of Christmas.

Best Man With Benefits brings us to the end of what has been an absolutely spectacular series. I have enjoyed each and every book for different reasons, and I know without doubt I will revisit the characters and their stories again and again in the future.Logan ‘Pantyripper’ McCade and Sophie Brooks, have been a part of the previous 3 books, but not to any massive extent, and you know what they always say about the quiet ones....”Why are you punishing me?”“For making me want you.”“If it’s any consolation, I want, you too.”Another thing I have liked about the books in this series is that each and every character has been different; they have all had their own unique qualities, back-story and issues. Some have been a little deeper than others, but all have been well developed and easy to empathise with.”Different doesn’t always mean incompatible.”I felt a massive connection to Sophie; this is a woman who likes to blend into the background, stay out of the limelight and is happier in her own company, rather than that of her peers. She has made a few changes in her life recently, and as a part of that is making more of an effort to come out of her shell and ‘get involved’ more.Logan as the Best Man is her Brothers best friend and as such has seen Sophie develop from the goofy little-sister into the woman she now is. As such, although he has been tasked in ensuring that she attends and enjoys the planned events for the wedding, Logan has very much put a Sophie-is-off-limits rule in place after discovering she isn’t quite the cute, shy girl he remembered.”The only chest you’re going to be pressed up against is mine.””You can, you know.”“Can what?”“Hold on to me.”I loved the first few chapters of this book, the amount of imaginary ****ing and eye ****ing that goes on between this couple is drool worthy, and when they do finally get down to it you are not left disappointed.”It’s like someone kicked my ass and left me for dead.””Come on, Soph. I dare you.”For me, there is nothing more of a turn on in a book boyfriend as one who knows exactly what his woman needs, and gives it too her. Logan does this in spades, and pretty creatively at points, his recognition and acceptance of her lack in confidence, I think is one of the main reasons she then manages to take the big step of actually putting herself ‘out-there’ emotionally after spending so long avoiding any entanglements whatsoever. Sophie struggles massively with body-confidence and due to past hurts struggles with self-esteem as well, Logan uses actions as well as words (filthy-dirty ones at times) to prove to Sophie that he doesn’t see her as anything less than the beautiful, intelligent, worthy woman she is.”You make me stand up and take notice. And not just because of all these mind-boggling curves wrapped in silk and lace – though I’m certainly not complaining. Your honesty, your sense of adventure, the way you can’t turn down a dare… those things grabbed my attention, and I’ve been captivated ever since.””I feel like I can be myself when we’re together,” … “And I’m trying to tell you, you can be yourself, too.”I am quite sad to be writing this review, not because it hasn’t enjoyed it, but it means that I have reached the end of the series. The Wedding has passed, the champagne drunk, the toasts made and the guests have gone home, and all that is left is the clearing up…The clearing up for each of these books has been pretty special and the epilogue for Best Man With Benefits closes out the series perfectly. It is my hope that the Entangled team in the future manage to pull together another group of their highly talented authors to provide us with more series like this as each book has been an absolute pleasure to read.

Well, one more failure.  The recipes in this book were updated, only one (that I noticed)  had margarine in the ingredients list, although in the instructions "butter" was used. Unfortunately transfats aren't the only poisons to be on a lookout. Fruits from cans aren't too hot, but not poisonous. Just deprived of most of their value. Besides, you can use what you canned yourself, completely "green". But those handy, work - free cake mixes can be very bad for you. Years ago there was a lot of fuss about them being linked to cancer. I bet the big business cleaned their act some, but still all my family has some bad side effects after ready - mix pancakes. I won't be able to use any of those recipes. "Caveat" mentioned by the other reviewer isn't enough. It is a complete no-no for me. Maybe someone WILL discover what were those quick-fix goodies that Laura Ingall's mom use to throw together in their little house. Maybe...
summary: sadly, this deliciousness is bad for you.

The plot and characters are very different from other Regency romances that I have read in the past. The H and h do not hide their feelings like most books. Neither of them is coy about the feelings or mutual attraction they have towards each other so there isn't a lot of pretense. I love that the H starts his pursuit of the h from the very beginning because he wants to "court" her, not just bed her. I, too, found the H's comment "But also know this.There will never be another woman for me. I have already taken you to wife in every way that matters. When you leave me, there will be no other. You are the wife of my heart" total swoon material.  The H did not play any games when he tries to win the h by making her jealous or appearing disinterested like most books. There is a part in the book where the H asks the h if she is jealous of the attention he was receiving from another woman.  She responds that she has no right and that she would leave the premises so that he can freely court the other woman if she was not expected to help deliver a baby.  His reponse....he is thinking how he can alleviate his beloved's situation and make her his as soon as possible so she no longer has to suffer.  Sigh....The H was so great. He wore his heart on his sleeve and it was refreshing .Throughout the book he is trying to win her despite her protest of being his ideal wife. The h was also trying to be noble when she rebuffs him for his own good. The h was not a whining, dumb, or helpless female in the book. She was a writer with strong views of the working class.  She was like one of the first " occupy " leaders within the social classes.The number one reason I enjoyed the book so much was I did not come across these over used phrases and adjectives at all or they were very subtle.I hate you.SneeringArrogantWhoreTrollopIt was a nice love story set in the tone of boy meets girl (or hears her sneeze), chases girl and catches girl. A recommend.

In a cave she finds a beautiful gem called istore. She has no idea it's more than a gem...or that there would be such terrible consequences, when people started to buy the items she made with it.I loved the characters in this book, especially another main character, Eva. She is strong, whereas Llandry is shy and easily panicked. I also liked two of the male characters. Brave Tren who tried so hard to look after Eva. And then there's the dishy Devary. Each character in the book is unique and I found myself interested in each one, which is a testament to the author's excellent writing skill, as there are a lot of them.I loved all the different animals as well.The twist with Llandry at the end of the book really took me by surprise, as did the abrupt way the story ended...a real cliff hanger. I hope there's a sequel! I would love to think Llandry and Davary get together.In some ways the story reminded me of one of my favourite TV shows, Primeval. In the book, gates to different worlds begin to open, allowing strange and sometimes dangerous creatures to come through. In primeval there's a similar situation, but they are called anomalies.Once you get into it, Draykon is an exciting read. If like me, you enjoy a good fantasy. Then you'll like this, it's brill!

Ever wonder if you could substitute regular cocoa for Dutch process cocoa? Or do you know what the difference is between bittersweet and semi-sweet chocolate? This book is a good, quick reference that answers these and other questions home bakers might have about the many varieties of chocolates that are available in grocery stores and called for in recipes with everything explained in easy to understand terms.There are plenty of recipes for brownies, cookies, and even a braided chocolate bread included plus a couple of non-chocolate recipes. Tips are provided for baking brownies and cookies to make sure you get the best possible final product. Photographs are included for most of the recipes, but not for the braiding technique that is used for the chocolate bread, but step-by-step instructions are given for that instead.My favorite recipe from the book is the one for Double Chocolate Sandwich Cookies which is certain to send any chocolate lover into a swoon.Formatting of the book is very good and it is well-edited. There is only one noticeable blip where several paragraphs of one section are in a grayed font which makes them difficult to read on an eink Kindle. There are three embedded links to a commercial site for the purchase of ingredients, but they are unobtrusive and can easily be skipped over.Recommended for all chocolate lovers.

“The Hell of Osirak” is a suspense novel that weaves together elements of historical fiction and erotica to create an exciting, entertaining read.The story is told through the alternating perspectives of Dvora and Nikki, both undercover agents—and at one time, they were lovers, although Dvora broke Nikki’s heart. Their turbulent past doesn’t mean they stop thinking about each other, though, and as Nikki embarks on a mission to recover an important microfilm and a foil a plot involving Iraqi nukes, they’re destined to cross paths once again.What I liked best about this novel is that the author does an excellent job of maintaining almost constant suspense—from a tense “layover” in Zaire to Nikki’s mission to become a powerful man’s mistress to gather intelligence about a nuclear bomb, each situation escalates breathlessly into the next. Behind the action, though, lies a romance—the story of two women who still long for each other despite years having passed and despite other loves in their lives. Dvora’s and Nikki’s personalities are also strong and come off the page to make them real people—Dvora is a bit more calculating and driven, and while Nikki may seem fragile she’s actually incredibly tough and tenacious. I also liked how they were both strong, competent women who were trusted with dangerous jobs—that’s a nice change in suspense/spy novels, which usually focus on men.I think this book would appeal to a wide audience—to historical fiction fans for the 1980s setting and the exploration of politics, corruption, and nukes; to erotica and romance fans for the frequent sensual scenes; and to suspense fans for the action and espionage elements. I would recommend it to readers of all three, and I’m interested to see where the trilogy goes.

This took me by surprise—very pleasantly so.When I read the ‘blurb’, I was expecting a gentle, ambling story about a wife struggling to decide whether or not to continue being a trophy wife to her wealthy husband and stay-at-home mum to her two young boys or to feed her artistic talent and need to express her creativity by going back to work for her former employer.But it had an awful lot more meat on the bones. The anguish she experienced went further than just her: it was shared by her husband who feared her proximity to her former boss (was he her ex-lover?) would rock the increasingly unstable marriage. His paranoia wasn’t helped by his own work problems. It was also shared by her sons, who found it hard to cope with a mum who just didn't seem to be around very much. It was even shared by her former boss, who, while determined to win her back to his growing company, doubted his confidence in being able to keep her with him.The repercussions of her decision echo loudly, resonantly, and dramatically.I thoroughly enjoyed this novel. It was classy, sophisticated, well written, reasonably well edited, and it was easy to put yourself into each of the main characters’ shoes to see their points of view and feel their passion, whatever its focus. You didn’t necessarily have to like the character: there are one or two undesirables and one or two (deliberately) irksome ones. It was easy to feel an emotion (good or bad) for all the characters;  there were none who could be ignored.This book was about decisions and what-ifs. I found it hard to put down and that’s always a good sign, I think!
summary: An enjoyable story with unexpected drama

Towns and forts are attacked, slaves taken leaving the survivors to look to their well-being and plan for their future protection.My problem with this book for me is that whilst the action is nicely portrayed and there is enough to excite most military history fans, the descriptions of life between military engagements drag a little and are written in such a simplistic, sweet, style that it reads to me as if it was intended for the younger reader.More positives than negatives though and I will likely read any sequel.

reviewText: Mad Gods is a repurposing and reimagining of mythology and religion.  As such, there is a lot of information here--back story, legends, reinvented interpretations of famous historical occurrences, and how they all piece together in a big ole Xian conspiracy. The book touches on correlations between myths that have always fascinated me, with the adage that everyone believes/has faith in the same thing, only in different ways--and some of them, not so great.This is a killer book.  At times, very shocking, but in a way that isn't outrageous--just an uncomfortable reminder that life is cruel and too often we see things through rose-colored glasses.  At other times, it is an upbeat view of pop culture 60s amidst the despair and devastation caused by the Darkness.Lyrical writing, poetic in tone, as well as absolutely vivid imagery.  There are dozens of lines that made me pause and re-read because they ring so full of truth.As a girl whose own faith operates by duality--light and dark, black and white--yet she exists in a blessedly gray area in between, this novel resonated with me.  I'm looking forward to spending more time with Adam in the next book!

reviewText: Karen Devane is the daughter of Hollywood elite but a misguided incident involving her drug obsessed friend and a homeless woman leaves her in the middle of a complicated and deadly accident.Meanwhile a beautiful Aryan girl named Katya is the daughter of a Nazi commandant, whose entire family are killed as a consequence of their allegiance to Hitler. Yet when she discovers her father is still alive and living as a movie director in Hollywood she takes a trip across the world to have some questions answered.The prologue of Too Little Too Late stands in stark contrast to the following few chapters and it takes a long time before the connection between Katya and Karen apparent; from there a complex and disturbing web of lies and destruction link these two women inexplicably.Though at first the conflicting stories are a little hard to understand, Too Little Too Late quickly becomes an intriguing and captivating thriller. The nature of some of what takes place in throughout the narrative is unpleasantly dark and painful to read, touching on difficult subjects that may put some readers on edge, however more mature readers will see all this as a necessity to compliment the strength of the plot. Interest levels in the plot do have a tendency to wax and wane as the occasional chapter goes by with absolutely nothing happening; yet more often than not Too Little Too Late is almost un-put-down-able.Unfortunately the author relies on one or two obvious stereotypes and clichés for his characters, including the sexually sadistic Nazi and the confused, rebellious teenager, but the mysterious thriller aspect of the story is enough to make these flaws forgivable. The final revelation is fairly obvious to readers about two thirds of the way through the book but that doesn't stop the rest of the book from being an intriguing and worthwhile read.

reviewText: Let me say first that in order to like this book you have to like books about shifters. If this is going to be your first read into this genre you might not like it. But happily for me; I love stories about them. This book was not a disappointment. The hero, Alexander was everything a hero should be. He was confident and very comfortable in his wolf form. He found his mate when he came upon Carole Anne. As a heroine, she was very unsure of herself; coming out of a very bad breakup. Her Ex left her believing she would never be able to attract anyone. She felt unattractive and very unsure of herself. She believed she would only find romance by reading about it in her romance novels.But Alexander wants her and she struggles with that; just believing that his feelings are only a "passing fancy" and he will tire of her. Carole Anne resists everything that Alexander does to try and convince her she is beautiful and very desirable. Will she feel it; feel the pull between them???There are parts of the book where even Alexander worries if there can be a HEA with Carole Anne. But does he succeed?!?!?You will have to read it to find out.It is a very enjoyable read. It's not a deep and meaningful book that will leave you breathless; but as a light read; it hits the mark.

The Abnorm Chronicles: Glimmer (Kindle Worlds Novella)A Sci-Fi and Fantasy Thriller of abnormal proportions. Authors J.R. Rain and Eve Paludan have engaged in intellectual curiosity and developed the scientific fiction fantasy: THE ABNORM CHRONICLES: GLIMMER (Kindle Worlds Novella).In American politics, Senator Richard Lathrup promotes micro-chipping of brilliants (gifted) and is in direct conflict with Senator Blake Crouch. Competition rears its ugly head and we learn how crime can develop and exploitation can rue the day. Blake Crouch happens to be one of a gifted population.A female scientist, Dr. Jude Malcolm works in Phase One of the Genesis Project, which is based in Erik Epstein's New Canaan Holdfast in Gillette, Wyoming. Phase One exploits gifted top echelon male executives and senate leaders. The project identifies `normal' and `brilliant' people. Additional `Phases' are developing. They are light years away from their narcissistic fantasy of a race of brilliants.The heroine, Dana Marlowe, is the featured natural-born `tier-three brilliant' who collects secret sperm samples of brilliant men for the agents of Phase One. Although an immoral activity, the behavior of Dana is without sensation or conscience and is directly related to her war experiences and PTSD. However, she is unaware of the ultimate goals of her superiors. Dr. Malcolm considers her the ideal candidate for her assignments.Dana lives day to day in limbo ready for performance of duty. Dr. Malcolm gives her the names of prospective donors and Dana researches their preference in women through the internet on her computer. Then she lures them into her apartment for a relationship they cannot refuse. Dana is camouflaged in fashionable clothes the men see as former wives and girlfriends, which include hair styles and tinted contact lenses.The next assignment Dana is given is Blake Crouch who is the scheduled speaker supporting a charity ball for autistic children. Crouch has enormous compassion for autistic children. Dana begins to feel emotions returning and becomes engrossed in intellectual conversation with the attractive and compassionate Blake. She is ready to nix her team and assignment. Finding true love after many years jolts her senses and Blake feels the same.A life and death crisis in the hotel hallway overtakes their first romantic escape after leaving the ballroom but the drama is handled by government officials. Dana and Blake are reunited for the evening, at least, but danger lurks. Total chaos escalates when Blake leaves town and Dana tries to quit her job. Thus begins a terrifying experience for both and heroes arise.The authors J.R. Rain and Eve Paludan present an exciting story that is fast-moving science-fiction fantasy: THE ABNORM CHRONICLES: GLIMMER (Kindle Worlds Novella) a Kindle Edition at Amazon.com.*NOTE: The ebook was received as a gift for an honest review.

reviewText: ***I received an ARC in exchange for an honest review.***Gabe Thompson had me from the first page of Camouflaged!!! Gabe can't because it's against regulations. She can't because she has a boyfriend waiting for her back in Texas. So, they agree to be friends since he is assigned to be her personal escort and guard. As the two embark on a journey to deliver goods to Afghani civilians, they come under attack. Will they survive, and if they do, will they finally throw caution to the wind and give into their overwhelming desire for one another?While Camouflaged was a HOT, HOT romance, it was also a story about war. The author did a great job of describing just a bit of what soldiers go through in war. She also touched on the shock that people experience when they go through something traumatic. It gave me a moment to pause and be thankful for the sacrifices our men and women make for our personal freedom and protection.I hope we are going to read more about Gabe and Alexis. Their story isn't quite finished yet. I am anticipating seeing what their future holds. If you haven't read this book, give it a try. When you're done, read Hidden which is about Gabe's friend, Nick. You do get to see a bit of Gabe in this one too. Thanks again, Selena, for another great read!!!!

reviewText: This review can also be found at Beyond the Squee: Book Reviews[...]I loved the beginning of this book. Sophia is in a carriage and needs to be in the Inn. There is a sea of mud between her and the stoop. Blake, who she had hoped to not see right away, strips off his boots, socks, and wades to her. We all know what's going to happen, and indeed, it does.She thinks he did it on purpose and so begins the continuation of their miscommunications.Sophia hasn't ever told anyone why she left at the age of 14. Blake, once he found out where she was, never went to her. She left because her father sold her, basically, to an abusive man. And what takes this down a bookmark rating is the fact that the Old Duke never got what he was due. I like my bad guys to get what's coming to them. I don't think this is a spoiler, as he's gone when the book begins.Sophia keeps her secrets, as does Blake. Blake thinks that her life as a courtesan was all trinkets, new dresses and romping bewteen the sheets with many men. Part of her secret is that it really hasn't been that many men, and if she hadn't taken on this persona, she would have been dead. Somehow he just doesn't get that.Very few books that I've read that have had a main character who was less than pure. And even fewer that followed a courtesan. This was an interesting theme and I think that Ms. Stuart gave us a seldom seen perspective. I have to applaud her for giving Sophia men that appreciated her.There are a few twists and turns, some that I saw coming, and some that caught me by surprise. I sure wanted to smack Blake a couple of times! I actually didn't need to, as Sophia slapped him four, or was it five, times. Why, yes, he did deserve it!This one had me turning the pages, wondering if something else BAD was going to happen, and wondering just how this would all come together. I would have liked to have had just one more chapter, as I like to see my main characters down the road a bit. But the ending was a good one, especially followed by the author's note.Thank you, NetGalley and Carina Press, for the opportunity to read Behind the Courtesan.

From the outset, the premise of Kim White's The White Oak grabbed me but, as I read, I found myself a bit torn over how I felt about the style of the storytelling. The gist of the novel is that the main character, Cora, falls in the Underworld through a sinkhole during her father's funeral. This understandably upsets the order of things for the despotic ruler, Minos, and Cora, aided by the many-faced Minotaur and Sybil, the librarian embarks on a journey to escape.What would have improved the narrative for me vastly would have been additional layering. I needed to have more insight as to Cora's motivations and emotions. Also, it is hinted that her brother, Lucas, a genius computer programmer, takes a more important part but if he's to be more than a secondary character, I'd have liked to have seen him get a bit more of a proactive role from the outset.White certainly has given much thought to her world-building in this tale that offers a nod at the legend of Persephone. And for that alone, for the bizarre and very much surreal landscape, the story kept me turning the pages. White's vision is reminiscent of a Dali-esque landscape with a whiff of Neuromancer thrust in. At first I wasn't quite sure I could suspend disbelief for the cyber theme, but White handles this well, and it added an extra dimension I found quite enjoyable once I got used to it.The pacing lagged a bit once I got past the initial start, and while I can see White intends for this to be part of a series, I myself as a reader wasn't sufficiently motivated to want to invest myself in what follows. I feel she could have written a longer story and concluded with better resolution, even if she wanted a cliff-hanger. Yes, the vision is nightmarish, and will probably stay with me for a long while, I just never truly engaged with the telling. The story flows like one dream sequence into another, and at times it felt like I was reading someone's journal as opposed to really immersing myself in the adventure.There could also be parallels to Alice's journey through Wonderland, and for White's supremely inventive imagination, The White Oak is worth reading. I just felt I needed a bit more oomph from the text to truly make me care about the protagonist, Cora. I give her five out of five for concept, but The White Oak falls down in execution. Still, I enjoyed this story a lot more than some of the YA offerings that are currently trending as bestsellers.
summary: Down a sinkhole and into the Underworld

What an interesting twist!  I won't go into more detail to prevent spoilers.  All the characters in this installment develop with a great deal of color and depth.  The universe Ringel has created also takes on a very interesting shape (both physically and metaphorically).  I am eagerly awaiting the next installment.The writing style displayed here has developed along with the characters; it is clean and well paced.  It also has a good balance between description and action that flow smoothly together. This is a long way from where the series began.  I feel that Ringel still has some issues with physics; especially in regards to inertia.  I both like and hate how Ringel measures distance in light-seconds (ls), light-minutes (lm), and light-hours (lh).  Across a vast stellar space, seeing things minutes or hours after they have already happened can make choices of action very difficult especially in a military scenario.  At closer (more actionable) distances, however, using these unfamiliar units created more confusion then they eliminated.  I think using the metric Giga-meters (Gm) or Terra-meters (Tm) or even the old standby Astronomical Unit (AU) would have kept things more clear.  4lm = ~72Gm = ~1/2AU

This story is about Brigid, a young witch running a New Age shop passed down by her grandmother. First off, the story starts out as if readers are already familiar with everything going on in Brigid's life. She's outside on the ground, with her faithful cat Mari, trying to cast a spell to keep her grandmother from dying (against her granny's wishes of course). While she's out her phone starts ringing, and it's her grandmother calling her to tell her she's dying right that very second. REALLY? Do people do that?Then during the conversation, several words/terms are spoken by Brigid and her grandmother in what I suppose is their native Gaelic language, but none of the terms are translated or explained, even when more terms are used throughout the story. And it's never explained what the grandmother and mother died from.Then there's Christian, Brigid's best friend who's been pining for her for several years with no results. It's later hinted that he has an ulterior motive, but it's never revealed what that motive may be. Also, it seems as if Brigid is kind of leading him on anyway. And I am assuming that Christian is aware that she is a witch, being that he attends the mother's funeral where chanting and magic is performed and he doesn't bat an eye. But again, we don't know for sure. THEN there's the fact that Brigid has never had any idea that she was even attracted to women, but a single kiss from her cat-turned-naked chick and she realizes she's not only attracted but in love? Wow, that was SOME kiss. (<-- Sarcasm. The 2 times they kissed, and that's ALL they did, ranked about a 1.5 on the hotness scale)All in all, the only way for this to have been a good story was to have fleshed it out from beginning to end. There was too much lacking here. It reads like an entry in a high school creative writing contest where there could be no inappropriate language and the limit was 75 pages. Glad I got it for 99 cents, but wish it had been free.

Where do I start with this without giving too much away.I should start with I was given a copy of this book in exchange for an honest review.I loved this book.It made me think.I don't know if it will make you think the way I do, but I do have my reasoning behind spending so much time analyzing my own thoughts regarding the subject.You can see that this book brings in some of the old gods, it also brings in Wicca, and with the Templar Knights, Christianity.  I'm a Christian who has always studied other beliefs.  It's not because I doubt what I believe, but because I want to know why someone else might believe what they believe.  Without going into my testimony during a book review, I know why I have my faith.  What about other spiritual beliefs make people believe in other gods or in nothing at all. Why do people believe in Diana, Pan, Brahman, HaShem, Allah, Jupiter, Zeus, Aphrodite, and the list of gods people have worshipped throughout time goes on and on.I have always wondered about the ancient gods, the Greek gods, the Roman gods, the gods that people believed in before Jesus Christ walked the Earth and Christianity was spread all over the place.  Why did they believe in those gods?  Did they have their proof for their faith? I don't know if I'm going against my own beliefs by saying this, but I've always wondered (since I believe the Christian God created the heavens and the Earth) did he create other powers as well?  I know there are things out there we can't see with our own eyes.  Why not that as well.  There is a scripture (Jeremiah 10:10 and I know there are other scriptures that say it as well) that says that God is the only true LIVING God.  I've always questioned that one word - living.  Did he create other powers and when people started to worship them.....?There is also the scripture (Exodus 20:3) that says thou shalt have no other gods before me.  I've always wondered if that meant that there were other powers out there? He could have just said thou shalt not worship false idols and left it at that, but he specifically said no other gods. Just a thought I have had in my time of studying the Bible.My other question is what if we are all truly serving the same God, we just call him different names?  I'm Pentecostal, my husband is Catholic, we both believe that Jesus Christ is our savior but we follow different rules to get to the final place.It's how my mind works. I am constantly wondering these things.  I really should have been a religions major in college rather than vocal performance.  I might have used it more.See what a novella brings out in me?Anyway, when you read this book, you'll see why my mind went through all of these questions.  I don't know if having all those thoughts while reading Shadow Of Hope is natural for everyone or just for me because of my fascination with religion.Obviously, I loved the book.  I like how Tina and Elizabeth somehow brought everything I have ever wondered together and made it work.  It was a fairly fast read, I had no problem getting through it in a couple of hours.  It was definitely an enjoyable story with bringing the god Aries into our current millennium.  There was scheming, and fighting, and a love story that was the icing on the proverbial cake.I have to admit, even with my desire to be nonjudgmental and open minded towards everyone, there was one part at the end of the book that made me uncomfortable.  It wasn't bad, or evil, or illegal or anything.  There's just one part that gave me a little bit of guilt and made me feel like maybe I shouldn't enjoy that one little section. That's because of my own beliefs and knowing I'm a Christian, I bet Tina can figure out what part I am talking about.  It was that ay, should I really even consider this to be a plausible possibility? moment.It's a good book if it makes me think and squirm a little.Awesome job Tina and Elizabeth! Thank you for letting me read this!

I must admit that the first book in this series left me a little disappointed, mostly just because of the cliff hanger and how much was left to resolve in the characters lives.  However, the second book started bringing things together and now this third book has made me fall in love with Quinton and Nova's story.Nova is one of my favorite female characters out of all the Jessica Sorensen books I have read so far.  She went through a terrible time dealing with the death of her boyfriend but unlike most of the characters in this story she is strong enough to pull herself back up and help others also.  I love how once she had her "breakthrough" and decided to start "living" again that she constantly reminds herself to stay strong and to help who she can.  Her character is a refreshing change from the characters in other books who throw themselves a pity party in every book and the guy characters who have to constantly rescue them.Quinton, was drowning in so much guilt.  What amazes me about him is that Nova is the first person to even notice it really.  I found that incredibly sad.  He really is a great guy, just lost and torn apart by guilt and grief.  I thought it was interesting that even though he tried to convince himself he wanted to die and that he was worthless, he continues to feel bad about whoever he hurts because of his self-destruction, proving he wasn't a horrible person.  He is honest with Nova and doesn't give her the wrong idea.  He knows what he is and isn't prepared to deal with. I loved how the author waited until the time was perfect for Quinton and Nova to finally be a couple.Overall, I loved how the characters finally learned to move forward and that it didn't mean they didn't love those they lost or that they were forgetting who they lost.  I hope there is a 4th book to complete this story, maybe letting Quinton say what he needs to say to Lexi and Ryder's parents and letting Nova continue to move forward.

The Travel Writer by Jeff Soloway is a recommended debut mystery series featuring Jacob Smalls as a smart aleck travel guide writer turned sleuth. When veteran American travel editor Hilary Pearson is missing and presumed kidnapped from the Matamoros, a Bolivian Hotel,  Pilar Rojas, the PR agent and an old friend of Smalls contacts him. Pilar offers Smalls an all-expense paid trip to the Bolivian resort if he will just write a complementary piece about the hotel.Smalls admits, "I’m a travel writer, and corrupt as they come. I’d sell my journalistic principles for two nights at the Four Seasons with a free meal and a massage. I’ve been wheedled and bribed and plied with bottles of wine worth more than my laptop, and I’ve rarely failed to succumb to the temptation of providing a puff review. But I was not entirely without ambition. That afternoon I had for the first time inspired hate, not just disdain, from a hotel employee—if that’s what Gonzales was. I had stumbled onto something, perhaps a crime worth uncovering, or at least a story worth writing about." (Location 142)All Pilar wants is a shill to write the pro-Matamoros propaganda piece, but Smalls decides to investigate Hilary's disappearance with some help from Kenny,  a goofy, naive co-worker of Hilary's who is sure they have a relationship. Smalls is a rather hapless, but clever narrator who displays plenty of self-deprecating humor and some interesting descriptions and outlooks on life. He's hardly anyone's first choice for an investigator. “What makes you think you can find her?” she asked. “The FBI couldn’t. You’re just a guidebook writer.” Guidebook writers are the peasantry of travel writers. Apparently my magazine work hadn’t caught Lisa’s attention, which wasn’t surprising. It hadn’t caught anyone else’s." (Location 323)While the actual plot isn't full of suspense or intrigue, the beauty and fun in Soloway's debut novel is in his laugh aloud descriptions:"I slipped the clerk my passport, and he hammered my name, two-fingered, into his computer keyboard, pausing for one heartbeat between each letter, perhaps to facilitate the computer’s comprehension of the outlandish 'Jacob Smalls.'"Or  "Her placid eyes widened in respect, as if she’d been told he owned a unicorn."The Travel Writer is an entertaining start to a new series. I laughed along with Smarts and liked him. Now let's hope he has a more intriguing, tough mystery/crime to solve in his next outing.Disclosure: My Kindle edition was courtesy of Random House via Netgalley for review purposes.
summary: entertaining start to a new series.

reviewText: * Disclaimer / Disclosure: I received a free sample to facilitate my review. This post reflects my honest, personal opinion and experience with the product which may differ from yours. Product information courtesy of the sponsor. No monetary compensation was provided for this post.My Thoughts-There is a beautiful but worn box full of what looks like random buttons. However these buttons have been passed down through the family for years. Each button shares a story. To some these are just silly stories, but the prayer of the one telling the stories is that the listener will hear a story of how God was involved in the tale. Our heros are off and running to rescue Francine before she falls victim to ruination by Hepplewort, who only wants her as his wife to produce an heir.  I think it is safe to say that Gideon and Perry save the day, and Gideon, Tenth Duke of Roxleigh, one time recluse, sets his mind to ruining Francine for any other man. (And, boy, does he ever!)The date is set.The bride and groomare ready. The onlything missing now isPerry, who returnswith some shockingnews of his own.This is when the evil laughter I imagine as Jenn LeBlanc's plays in my head while we wait for the next installment of The Rake and The Recluse, Book Five: SUBMISSION.Would I recommend this book to you? But, you must remember that this is a six part serial and they should be read in order: FREEDOM, FOUND, TAKEN, RUINATION, and soon to be released, SUBMISSION, and the conclusion,  RETRIBUTION.If you like your hero handsome, tall, strong, and powerful with plenty of -all I can think of to describe Gideon is- "Oh, yes..." to season him a bit more, then this is for you. reviewText: Given a copy of this book from the author in exchange for an honest review***Review From Amy Conley For The Nerd Girl Page***Anela Alborn's life is a lie. reviewText: After 100 chapters into Red Gambit most people have decided whether or not to keep reading and I seriously doubt that anyone is likely to have started reading this series this far in. This review is only for discussion and, as I know the author checks out the comments, to offer one view of the series.I'm guessing most readers, like myself, are history buffs. Alternate history done well is outright fascinating to people like me. Colin Gee has risked using well know, real historical characters to a larger degree than seen most such works. I have to say he's done a masterful job doing so. Sure, we can never know how the Stalin's, Eisenhower's, Beria's, et. all, would really behave given these alternate circumstances, but so far Gee has persuaded me that their actions are very plausible. (We know Beria was an evil man. Skeletons of young women have been discovered on his property. Sure - he could have done what Gee speculates.)As always the strength of the story is the impressive research. I've said before that it can be overwhelming, but adds to the logic of what he writes. And, again, his characterizations of people is impressive, whether good, bad, or mixed, he describes them in a way that makes them real.His previous focus on the European theater may change as he has included action against the Japanese. I'd like to know how the research toward American's bomb was progressing after breaking the spy ring early in the series, but the scale is so huge that may have to wait.In all I'm glad I've got the time and patience to follow the events depicted. And I'm looking forward to the next installment.Again, I'm pretty certain that anyone who has put in this much time into reading Red Gambit has already made up their mind about  continuing reading.Ohh... almost forgot, the graphics on Kindle make a full appreciation of the details Gee includes on maps and charts difficult to appreciate. That he has these maps and charts does reinforce the competence he's shown in his research.

*** Mild Spoilers***I purchased this book after I was reccomended it by a blogger friend. This was my first Lily White book. Although, I am well aware of her dark writing reputation and knew that going into this story.I'm not sure how to rate this book or what to say. It was a train wreck that I couldn't turn away from. Honestly, it registered with me on a different level than most ... because ,like Lucas, I'm an author. However, not a sick and twisted one. But I get his need to delve into a story and find ways to help develope it. His way was just a bit unothodox. Around every corner I was waiting for the sickness he writes to carry into life. In a strange way hoping that it would, as another part of me held out hope that he'd fall head over heels and change the true sadist lurking at his very core, to succumb to some feelings rather than his manicle primal nature....as twisted as that sounds, that's what I was torn between and what kept me reading. You'll just have to read to see what he did or didn't incapsulate.As many will be happy with the ending ... others will not be. For me I was torn. But satisfied with it as a whole... I think because I picked up on the intent for the ending from early in the book. I would reccomend this book for anyone seeking a different perspective of life... something dark and sinster .. yet light in its own way.My final thought is this....I f'ing hated his assistant and deep down I wish I could exsact a kind of tortour on her myself... making her die a slow and agonizing death.

ABSORBED is a short-story thriller about Violet, a woman pushed to the edge by a violent, psychotic boyfriend, and how an elaborate gift she finds on her doorstep one day triggers events in both her life, and that of her boyfriend's, which changes their lives irrevocably.ABSORBED is a vivid, suspenseful adult story of a toxic personality who manages to maintain an air of sympathy for the reader throughout the course of the story. What a fun novella! I usually avoid them because 98% of the time I'm left unsatisfied, but this novella felt like a full novel from beginning to middle to ending. As part of the Sons of Sin series, Days of Rakes and Roses has some familiar faces in the form of Jonas Merrick, Camden Rothermere and Sir Richard Harmsworth, the hero of the upcoming full length novel A Rake's Midnight Kiss.Days of Rakes and Roses is Lady Lydia Rothermere's story and a story about rekindled love.When Lydia was only 17 she was caught in a compromising situation with Simon Metcalf, by her uncompromising father. After that night, Simon fled England and Lydia became the very image of propriety. Ten years later, Lydia is engaged to a man she doesn't love and Simon has come rushing home to try and win her back.I adore rekindled romances and this was no exception. At 27, Lydia is now a distinguished, proper beauty in society but on the inside she's still the same insecure, lonely girl she was when she was caught with Simon. As stubborn as she was about her feelings for Simon, I understood Lydia's dilemma. She had so much pressure placed on her as a child and the one time she tried to take happiness for herself, she was punished severely. I was pleasantly surprised at Simon. I expected an out and out scoundrel and at times he was, but he was more focused on winning Lydia for himself and was honest about his feelings. Lydia was the one in denial and it was a refreshing switch for me. Simon never denied he was in love with Lydia ten years ago and he didn't deny it when her brother asked him point blank. It was refreshing.Naturally since Days of Rakes and Roses is a novella, it unfortunately doesn't take long to finish. As much as I loved Simon and Lydia, I understand why their story was a novella and not a full length novel. However, I enjoyed it nonetheless and recommend that if you've read Seven Nights in a Rogue's Bed and liked it, you should add Days of Rakes and Roses to your collection.
summary: lovely novella while you wait for the next book in the series

A.N. Bond is a new author for me. Right out of the gate, I have to say that Ms. Bond managed to create a character who is exceptionally difficult to like.  And I wanted to like him! Joseph is very much a mercurial personality. He holds a carrot in one hand and a stick in the other. He is hard to read. Not in the words sense, but his moral fiber and motivations are hard to pin down. Just when you think you know Joseph Van Aardt and what his impetus is, Ms. Bond turns your belief on its head and you have to try to figure him out all over again.When newly minted lawyer Ryan Paullson is short-listed for a job at a top New York law firm, it seems like a dream come true. He will get to work at the firm where one of the rock stars of the legal field works. He and his fiancée are thrilled when he is hand picked by said rock star, Joseph Van Aardt.Ryan finds himself strongly sexually attracted to Joseph, whose changeable personality makes it difficult to read his feeling at any given time. Joseph does make clear that he is equally attracted to Ryan and they begin a hot and heavy office romance that must be kept secret at all costs.  My first thought was that here is a lawsuit in the making. A named partner having sex with a junior associate? Not a great idea.The case that Ryan and Joseph are working is a lawsuit brought against controversial billionaire, Jack McNeil.  McNeil is accused of misappropriating funds from his employees’ retirement accounts and insider trading. He has already been found not-guilty in a criminal trial, so Ryan and Joseph have an uphill battle on their hands.As their work together brings them closer, Ryan begins to wonder just how far Joseph will go to win. Joseph is able to charm his way into Ryan’s heart and convince him that the suspicious deaths of witnesses are the doing of Jack McNeil and his people. It seems Joseph is able to pin anything and everything on McNeil.Ryan allows his feelings for Joseph to cloud his judgment and render his intelligence useless. Ryan wants to be with Joseph so badly that he believes whatever Joseph says. Until he doesn’t. The case becomes personal for Ryan in ways that could never have been predicted. Although it seems that perhaps Joseph was able to predict them. And perhaps Ryan was hired not because of his qualifications as an attorney, but because of his hidden ties to the case. Ties of which he was completely unaware.How much Joseph knew when he hired Ryan and his motivation for doing so are questions Ryan inevitably begins to ask himself and eventually Joseph. Ryan wants to win the case.  He wants to be with Joseph. But he doesn’t want to break the law he has sworn to uphold. And he doesn’t want to be in bed with someone who does.It becomes a deep internal dilemma for Ryan. He doesn’t know who to trust or believe any more. Nothing is as it appeared months ago when he was hired for what he thought was his dream job. A.N. Bond adroitly takes us along inside Ryan’s thought process and his disillusionment as he uncovers just how deeply he is personally involved in the case. Not just as a lawyer, but as a man. He is torn up by disappointment in everyone around him and really doesn’t feel like he knows Joseph at all.The Dangerous Seduction is a fast-paced, thrilling read. There are a lot of loose ends left when the book is finished. I can not wait for a sequel to tie them up. I certainly hope there is a sequel in the works or I will be forced to stalk this great new author until I find out what happened after the last page. Picture “Misery” without the hobbling. I’m not cruel, just a little crazed! And I highly recommend this book.

Taken by Surprise introduces us to 5 seemingly ordinary people but in reality they all struggle with abilities unusual to other people. They are all kidnap over a span of time and are all thrusted into a new and pressure filled environment. They are told their abilities will help them become great fighters and that the government needs them.....could it all be a lie? or is the government telling them the truth?All the characters draw us in wonderfully deep into their lives. We form a connection with the POV we are viewing that when the author switches it to the next POV I was a little sad and wanting more of the persons story we just left. After you get delve into the new POV you become enamored with them....and then it switches! Its a never ending cycle but I LOVED it! I really enjoy multiple POV's and that is definitely what you get in Taken by Surprise.There is an amazing cliffhanger at the end which of course leaves you wanting more! It has love, special abilities  time travel, origin history, and secret government agencies...Everything you could want :)  This is the first book in the Paranormal Romance Series and I can not wait to see what becomes of the group next!

reviewText: "After witnessing last year's fifty-metre-high rolling fireballs, she'd wondered if the treetops were truly Satan's home. And God resided in the water. Everything about that fire had smacked of hell." -Dark HorseThis is my second Honey Brown book. And while I enjoyedAfter the Darkness, this has to be my favourite read of the year so far. I literally couldn't put it down.Dark Horsedelivers on all fronts. There is not a moment when something isn't happening. Brown somehow manages to imbue every setting and every exchange with suspense, which is all the more surprising given the small cast of characters - one woman, one man, a horse and the weather. Simply masterful.I also love it when a twist catches you by surprise - especially when all the clues are there.Days after I finished readingDark Horse, I found myself still thinking about the story. It is a rare book that stays with me like that.A must-read.

Okay, I could really like this book if it was not for the hero's vindictive behavior. He was hurt and instead of asking the heroine why she left, he makes bad choices. After first running into the heroine, he gets drunk and takes the town slut back to her place for sex, then he goes to church the next morning to sit beside the heroine so she can smell the sex on him as a payback for leaving him. Married to Madness, by Devin Shane was a very interesting story, to say the least.  I traveled into the world of childhood abuse, convenience marriages, murder, jealousy, prescription drugs,  and true love.  Vigilante justice, sometimes paid and sometimes not, runs through the entire plot along with an ample amount of sex.Zack is a military war veteran, father, and stone cold killer.  He is part of a secret group of men who take out the scum of the earth in an effort to rid their town of the low life molesters, abusers, dopers, and murderers.  Most of these criminals are not reported, and if they are, the criminal justice system just turns them back out on the street.  Leon, Zack’s drill sergeant in the military who just happens to also be his father-in-law, leads the group of men.  Brandon is Zack’s beautiful wife.  Her mother expected her to be a boy; hence, the masculine name.  She is abducted, tortured, and raped but from the lessons that Zack taught her she is able to kill her attacker.  This one act of killing fuels her desire to kill again, making her the newest member of a group of sophisticated women who get paid to eliminate portions of the city’s criminal element.  Lucy, a very wealthy older woman, heads this group which she started after the death of her teenaged daughter years ago.  Other characters include children, sisters, brothers, and an entire host of others who make this story come together.Zack and Brandon have a love story that is written in the stars.  Lately their marriage fluctuates from good to bad with them continuously loving each other.  No one can quite understand their madness when they fight, bodily injure each other, live separately, and then come back together without skipping a beat.  Everyone does understand that they love each other and their children and would die to stay together.  The problem is that neither of them knows about the other’s vigilante extracurricular activities and keeping secrets is hurting their relationship.  Zack begins to suspect that Brandon is a killer and wonders when she will trust him enough to let him know.  Brandon has no idea where Zack disappears to at all hours of the day and night and she has no clue what he is up to either.  Join these two as they help people, kill others, and still manage to raise their children.  It is not an easy task and their love and commitment are strengthened when they finally confess to each other.  Can two killers lead a normal family life?Overall I enjoyed the book.  I had a little trouble understanding the flow at first because some characters were introduced out of the blue and there were fluctuations between the past and the present that threw me for a loop.  Once I got into the flow of Mr. Shane’s writing style I was able to enjoy the story as he got around to developing these characters.  I thought about my own husband as I saw how Zack and Brandon loved each other and their children unconditionally, which is the way families should be.  A sequel would get my vote, especially if Zack and Brandon team up.  I will recommend this book to my friends who enjoy this particular genre.
summary: Married to Madness by Devin Shane

You realize the tight bond/friendship between Tristan, Malek and Micah and even King Bain when it comes to Micah. The overwhelmed and outgunned forces of humanity heroically position themselves for the onslaught, ready to fight to their dying breath.The final volume of the Nexus series, Black Rift provides an amazing series with an even better conclusion. One of my favorite aspects of the series has been Michael G. Thomas’s incredibly detailed universe-building, which is amazingly conceived. Imagination abounds in Black Rift, Thomas’s creativity is staggering.Unlike a lot of science fiction novels that scrimp on characterization, Black Rift is filled with complex and developed characters, whose motivations are believable. The battles are stunning, and the book reads like a non-stop thrill ride, never letting you catch your breath.This is sci-fi at its very best.
summary: An amazing conclusion to one of my favorite series

reviewText: This is a good old fashioned science fiction military adventure for the young at heart. Definitely YA material. Sex is non existent. Complicated human relations are kept to a minimum. There are no bad guys apart from the aliens.You feel you are back in Star Trek where everybody behaves and only the bad guys try to stab others in the back. Nice to know humanity can work together seamlessly!This is not the real world. Technology is developed and implemented in month, sometimes hours. A planet is colonized with 3 million people and a self sustaining infrastructure built in 3 years. Yeah, right.If you can get over the Utopian human relations and the too fast pace of technological development then you are in for an entertaining read. Lots of space battles with just enough detail to keep you going. It never goes on and on as some authors love to do.in fact, the story moves very quickly and you want to know what happens next. As soon as you get the idea of what will happen you are on to the next scene or chapter, where it already has happened. No pussy footing around here. I loved it.Highly recommended for the young from ages 14 to 90. I gave it only 4 stars for stretching my credulity of the goodness of human nature and unrealistic technological pace. Enjoy. It was a fun read and I was sorry to discover that the next book in the series comes out on 29th July 2014 with the third book scheduled for 25th November 2014. Damn, I'll just have to wait!
summary: SciFi Action Adventure - First Contact - Mobilizing humanity to fight for survival

reviewText: A beautifully written story of the life of a child through his eyes.  The child is indeed the initial designer who helps create the man.  How the child copes with the dealings of the adults and world  around him can be carried with him long into his adulthood.  The way he views the events in his life and the walls he creates in order to deal with them can be an obstacle in reaching his true self.  Such is the case with Jamie.  HIDDEN CHILD can be read as a stand alone, but I found it to be a necessary tool in understanding Jamie and why he acts and reacts as he does.  Locking things away is not the answer as they have a habit of getting out of the box in one form or another.  Reality is always the victor no matter how hard you try and hide it from yourself.  It is a compelling book and at times I found it difficult to read from an emotional level.  Grab your kleenex and read this well written story of a young man who had much to deal with at a very young age.

This read like a few "left out chapters" that was laying around on someone's computer.  The story starts off like it would be intense, but reads like it was a series of pasted together paragraphs thrown together to make a short novel, and fails to deliver anything other than really flat characters, lame bad guys and no background or follow up on anything. It starts, it has a few scenes, and then the story is over.
summary: This book was a few chapters from a larger story... because it definitely is not a full novel.

reviewText: Emmie is not your run of the mill lady by any stretch. She is mischievous, clever, underhanded, and fortunately for her husband, also very lucky. I find her charming and really enjoy reading any book that features the Reeses.

A policeman returned from undercover work is just saved from a shot by a man who has walked into a coffee shop. The cop is unsure of what's happening and promptly arrests his saviour. But they sort it out at the station. The newcomer had a serious car accident and is gradually rehabilitating himself to life, having to try to remember simple words and actions. He's not slow however and they find each other attractive....I found this fast-moving with continued tension and the four hungry kittens were a nice touch.  The men's names being Brennan and Keegan were a bit too similar however and there wasn't a great deal more in the tale, there's not much room in a novella and there was a lot of adult romance to fit in. This will principally interest gay readers who might well give it more stars.

It is so sad that so many people have no idea what fasting in - oh, they may have some inkling, but do not know how important it is. We are in spiritual warfare with principalities and powers and spiritual wickedness in high place. If every Christian were to make fasting part of their Christian life, I am convinced our country would be different. Fasting breaks down strongholds. David Miller's book on praying and fasting is an exhaustive study of the Scriptures related to fasting.If you have always wondered about fasting or if you want to review the principles of fasting, get this book and read it. Put it into practice. Your spiritual life will change.

reviewText: This is the third and final part in the Distant Desires series.Just like part two, book three picks up where the previous book ended. We get more Sophie, Tarek, Matt and some new characters. This story had me intrigued from the first book and I'm happy I got all the answers I had from the previous two books in this final installment.We get to see more of the developing relationship between Sophie and Tarek. Not only is Tarek completely new to this relationship stuff, but so is Sophie, she has never had feelings like the ones she has for him, and its lovely to see how much they love each other and how they learn to navigate the problems that come not only from a new relationship, but living together and lets not forget the baby!! The only thing that left me wanting more was Matt, his character grew on me and I would love to see more of him. Maybe a book with him and Teagan?! *wink* *wink*This was the perfect conclusion to the series!! You get more from the swoon worthy Tarek and you get answers to pretty much everything, Cambria did a great job wrapping everything together in this book. If you have not read this series yet, do yourself a favor and pick it up, and be sure to read it. <3

Anna, your not so stereotypical wall flower gets discovered on one of her wild night swims in her oh so mysterious neighbour's pool. She is shocked to discover he has been watching her naked night time dips for weeks now. Strangely aroused and completely confused she vows never to return. Not used to being noticed she finds herself in front of him, again and again.Blaine, the roguish billionaire is one of the most exciting male characters I have come across since the ever famous Mr Grey. Extremely mysterious, and strangely sensitive. Anna on the other hand is like nothing I have ever come across. The supposedly innocent virgin who seems to hide an extremely passionate nature behind frumpy clothes. So insecure and soft spoken that you cannot help but want to shelter her and protect her.This was a very passionate, and thoughtful story that has you so nail bitingly close to the edge that it has you literally begging for more. I myself, am counting down the days until I get my hands on the next installment. My recommendation? Get it. Get it now.book provided by the publisher for the purpose of an honest reviewreviewed by angelique

This series must be read in order. The first book isShe's the One (Counting on Love). The second book isIt Takes Two (Counting on Love). This is the third book.I want to be clear... I adore the Emma character and could not understand why she didn't just douse Nate in alcohol and light a match! That said this is an awesome book about the transformative powers of love and all the crazy things it makes you do in between :)Each book in this series is heartwarming and funny (not to mention steamy). I really enjoy getting to know the hidden alternate sides of the characters you wouldn't normally see. I can say with complete connlfidence that they are NEVER boring. In the case of this book I would say they can be at times annoying and aggravating but that was part of the charm. You see two people together and think ... Ummm no. They WILL kill each other... But they both become the perfect person for the other and you are left sitting there wondering how did that even happen?!This series is truly awesomeness and I will be very sad when it is over. The Dixon family feels like family to me and I really enjoy every new chapter in their lives. Who knows maybe if enough fans beg the author might just be persuaded to write a companion series about some of the minor characters from the town and we will never have to say good bye :) Stranger things have happened! reviewText: Wow!!! What a ride!!! Tessa Bailey has done it again!! Never Let You Go kicks the fantasy in this series into high gear! Where I felt like the first book was a bit lacking in its magical elements, that is not at all the case here - book #2 is fantasy through and through, which I loved!This book picks up right where book #1 left off - Skye has just abandoned Xander to go off to the palace on her own, hoping to find the mysterious necklace that the Elf King Griffin told her about and save "her" (though Skye doesn't actually know who it is she's trying to save). But when she gets to the castle, she finds that the truth isn't as cut-and-dry as she thought and her enemies may not all be enemies after all.The negatives:The love triangle.Maybe it's because it's been a long time since I read book #1, but I just didn't feel all that much of a connection to Xander in this book. Skye spends the entire book with Nickoli, who pretty much captured my heart right from the beginning. I kind of found myself thinking "Xander who?" no matter how often someone in the book mentioned that Xander and Skye were destined for each other. At the same time, it seemed obvious (at least to me) that Nickoli and Skye weren't going to end up together, so my adoration of Nickoli just felt a little fruitless. There were definitely some twists and turns with the romance - and I can't say who she actually ends up with at the end of the book (or if she even chooses), but the journey itself wasn't as interesting as it could have been because I wasn't connected to Xander.What I loved:True fantasy.Unlike the first book in the series, this book felt like a true fantasy novel and I was truly drawn into Tyalbrook and it the lives of its people. There was a much greater sense of magic and mystical danger in this book, which I loved! I thought that Miller did a great job of worldbuilding in this book!The mysteries.Throughout the book, Skye is trying to learn the true story of what happened to her parents and who's side she should really be on. She's gotten one side of the story from The Guardians, but when she gets to the castle, she discovers that there is another version of the story being told. And she comes to realize that some of the people who she has always considered to be her enemies really just believe in that other version of events - and since she's really just going off of what she's been told, she doesn't always know what to believe herself. Then there's the king's obviously evil sidekick - but the question is, what is he up to and is the king in on it all? Meanwhile, Xander is learning some new truths of his own - and those truths may change everything. While I did kind of guess some of the twists in the book, I was still intrigued and excited to unravel the story as it went along.Nickoli.Did I mention that I'm in love with Nickoli? His sometimes overactive ego just made his softer, protective side seem that much sweeter. And I ached for him every time that Skye crushed his heart - why, oh, why Skye? I have a guess about what might happen with Nickoli in the future and I can't wait to read the next book so that I can see if I'm right. Since we got to see parts of this book from Nickoli's perspective, I'm hoping that we'll get even more of him in the next book (and that his heart doesn't get stomped on too badly)!I definitely feel like this series is heading in a great direction and I can't wait to see what Miller has in store for us in book #3. I give Never Let You Go 4/5 stars.***Disclosure: This book was provided to me by the author in exchange for an honest review. No other compensation was given. All opinions are my own***

Physically and emotionally scarred while stationed in the Middle East, 26 year old Christian Derringer has been discharged from the Air Force. After 10 months away, 5 of those recuperating and rehabbing from almost losing his life, Christian returns home to live with his parents while he attempts to understand his new limitations and determine what to do with himself. The changes in Christian are evident in his eyes and his demeanor to those who love him: “She could only hope that while his body was forever scarred, something could heal the man on the inside.”I found Christian’s return home very odd and out of sync with how loving and supportive his family dynamic is. His parents knew he was returning, but not when. The day of his return, no one made an attempt to go out of their way to see him; after a year away, and almost losing him, excitement would be expected. If not ready to throw a party, at least placing all else as secondary, and yet this was not the case, and I don’t understand why this was.In his depression, Christian becomes a bit of a recluse. But Annabelle, being the loving and supportive mother she is, forces him to interact. It’s at a laid back Christmas party where Christian meets Logan Mannette, a 21 year old college student with a friendly and open personality. The two men immediately have a connection full of witty and humorous banter. I loved Logan’s character – he’s funny, gregarious, charming, and compassionate towards Christian and his struggles. Knowing he’s been attracted to men all his life; Logan is outwardly gay, not hiding who he is or what he wants. The self-assuredness Logan has is opposite to Christian who, while admitting he has found men attractive before, has only ever wanted to be with women. Meeting Logan changes many preconceptions for Christian, and places him on a path of self-discovery.The relationship which forms between Christian and Logan is heartwarming and inspiring to follow as it slowly unfolds and develops. As the reader, I appreciate the ability to travel this new path with Christian and experience his growth, with him. Altering one’s personal views and sexual orientation could never be an easy path, but the author has made it a beautiful one. I finished this book with a warm feeling and a light heart, loving Christian and Logan more at the end for the journey they traveled together.
summary: Sweet Story of Love and Staying True to Yourself

reviewText: Series that involve angels and demons tend to fall into one of two categories: They are usually either preachy and pedantic or they completely remove God and faith from the story line. Both feel wrong and this is where Anne Conley gets it right.The Father makes appearances in the story and does give guidance, but he is a compassionate god, who truly loves humans. He is also very quirky and lightens the mood a little in an story that otherwise feels dark and brooding. The only judgmental behavior comes from his angel, Uriel. Uri is jaded and has lost compassion for humanity. He seems to wander the earth in an empty, listless manner that is reminiscent of the German film about fallen angels, Wings of Desire. When he meets his target, a stripper named Heaven, he is judgmental, even as he learns the desperate circumstances she faces.The Deceiver's character is intriguing. There was a moment of the story that I felt compassion for him, as he seemed to be feeling an emptiness similar to Uri's. I am interested to see where his character goes in the sequels.Looking forward to Falling for Grace next. BTW, although this is part of a series, it is cliffhanger-free.
summary: good start to a new paranormal/angel series

Shattered Promises by JR GrantReview by Jen (BestSellers & BestStellars)Shattered Promises was amazing!  This was definitely an emotional book.  There were secrets and lies, betrayal of the worst kind, and a lot of heartbreak.  It really puts you through a roller-coaster ride of emotions, I was all over the place.  JR Grant did an awesome job integrating some heavy issues in the story.  She did a great job with her debut novel.I loved Lani.  She’s strong, beautiful, smart and just an awesome person all around.  She has great, supportive parents, two cute little boys, Justin and Zakrie, Kade, her husband that she loves more than anything, and Parker, the best friend any girl could ask for.  Until tragedy strikes her family and she’s barely hanging on.  She endured a lot when things finally came out, and I think she’s incredibly strong for that.  Kade really shocked Lani, and she blamed herself for it because she wasn’t aware of what was happening.  She also wasn’t sure that she could make it through that.“He wrecked me; Kade Foster ruined me.  And from here on out, I’ll have to live with the sins of my husband’s destruction for the rest of my life ... I should have kept my eyes open over the years with all of his sneakiness.  It’s my own damn fault.  I think I’m more pissed at myself for being naive than anything else.”Once the truth comes out, Lani has convinced herself that Kade didn’t love her, because then he wouldn’t have done what he did.“Kade never loved me.  He never cared for me.  He couldn’t have.  Our vows ... those vows ... they didn’t mean s***.  If they did, my husband would have never thought about hurting me or abusing our love, destroying what he had, what we shared.”I hated Kade.  He had no respect for Lani or his children, even when they were younger.  There was not one thing about him that I liked, and when the truth came out, I was happy with the way things worked out for him because he deserved it after all the trouble and pain he caused his family.Then we have Parker.  I loved him!  He’s sweet, caring, and handsome.  He was always there for Lani and her kids, no matter what.  He’s an amazing best friend and I was really happy that Lani had him.  He has been in love with Lani since they were kids.“I said, ‘One day, you’ll be my queen, and I’ll be your king.  We’ll have lots of babies, and they’ll be our princes and princesses.”Lani means everything to Parker, and he wants nothing more than to be with her forever.“When you’re sad, I’ll be the one to cheer you up.  When the world disappoints you, I’ll make you happy.  I’ll protect you, hold you close to my heart and make you feel wanted.  I refuse to let anyone hurt you or take advantage of you ever again.”Lani’s father was definitely one of my favorite characters.  He supported her through everything and wanted the best for her.  Everyone should have a father like that.“Don’t hide or try and run from your life when the going gets tough.  Grab that son of a b**** by its balls and take control.  You’re a lot stronger than you give yourself credit for, sweetheart.”I loved this book!  I love a story that is told in dual point of view, it’s my favorite.  I also loved all of the characters, except Kade, even though he made the story what it was.  Even though it was such an emotional book that dealt with some heavy issues, it was also a beautiful second chance story and I loved being able to watch two characters come together so beautifully.The quality of writing was great.  The story was well-written and very enjoyable to read.  This was such a emotional story that had me turning the pages quickly to see what was coming.  JR Grant did a fantastic job!5 Diamonds for this wonderful story!!
