reviewText: Right at the very beginning, the Governor could have set our heroine free. That he didn't made it a very good read. Lu Lu's story is an engaging one, told through the eyes of a girl who shouldn't have been a slave. One that could have happened. The story is multi-layered in that there are many different characters whose story is revealed in order to bring the whole novel together. Each story in itself is a peep hole into the history of the American south from both sides of the coloured divide.The issue of slavery is addressed historically through real life people and families at a period of time when the abolitionists were very vocal, so the author brings in arguments for and against the rights and wrongs of slavery. The times they collide either make you angry, or indignant, or incredibly shamed and sad or a combination.  It also details the underground rail road to freedom and the risks many took to save lives, and then culminates in the civil war. Historically, as a non-American, I found it fascinating and it kept me intrigued. I didn't find the ending a problem as did some reviewers. We knew each person's demise or future in a way that led us to cheer or feel satisfied, but not feel robbed. The way he finished saved the novel from becoming the next War & Peace! It is a good read in every sense of the word. Yes there is slave dialect, but it would sound unrealistic for a slave of the time to speak Queen's English. I commend him on his efforts to speak in different Voices - not an easy thing to do when writing a novel. Well done Tom - you've won my vote.

In my opinion this is probably the strongest of the Tales of the Empire installments.  The characters are very well developed with the author doing an exceptional job of showing them evolve from children into adults.  Especially well done is the description of how circumstances shape them.  Secondary characters frame the story giving thorough insight to environment that the main characters negotiate.The story itself covers the beginning of interregnum to the re-establishment of the empire illustrating the circumstances that befall the main characters as the empire is torn by strife and stability crumbles.  The narrative centers on how three children initially adjust to the new circumstances and ultimately strive to influence the environment to suit their own goals.  The author is very effective in describing their efforts and showing that while some of their actions might not be consider "good" they all are logical and directed towards survival and greater goals some of which are laudable.
summary: A solidly crafted and satisfying narrative.

reviewText: Review for Nocturnereads.comEvery now and then you come across a book that within the first page you just know it's good, and then you get to the end and say "Yep, that's it, that is why I read books." I am a sucker for a paranormal romance that has just enough sexy details to make it steamy, but doesn't go overboard and make it smut. Ms. Cherie Nicholls and I must be on the same wave length because this book has become a favorite, and quite possibly one I will compare other books too in the future.Let's start with characters. Heath (fan myself) Oh wait, I mean Alpha. He is the ultimate wolf-boy of my fantasy land. Dominate, sexy as hell, and knows how to flirt and please his woman...need I say more! Laney is who I can aspire to be in my alternate life (hehe). A strong independent woman, often underestimated, but goes after what she wants, whenever she wants it.The one thing I would ever change about this book is the blurb, and maybe the cover art (I know that is two things), but honestly it suggests and depicts more smut content. The sexual scenes have some details, but nothing overboard, and there aren't a whole lot of them. So don't let those details deter you from reading this incredibly addictive book....and by addictive I mean, I skipped watching one of my favorite shows so I didn't have to put this book down!This is book one in this new series, but there was no cliffhanger on Heath and Laney's romance which suggests one (or more) of the secondary characters will step into the spotlight. Hmmm might Clara and Wall be the next installment...I can't wait!This book is definitely going on my reread list and I will be watching for new work from Ms. Cherie Nicholls. LOVE LOVE LOVED IT!

Barely wanting to put it down (although I was dividing my time between reading this, working, and season 4 of Downton Abbey).Kayla is one of those strong girls I mentioned above. Left by a dead mother to live a life running from the inevitable. She has a will to live and I appreciated that she hardly let her vision get cloudy when it came to Shaun.Shaun. She finally tells him, in his language, to leave and he stays.  So the bodyguards grab his camera, toss it in the bay, and then take him out of the area.  She gets  mad because he was handled badly.  Really?  I wonder He was totally in the wrong and was lucky they didn't toss him in the bay. Sound familiar?  all this is taking place around Italy and Germany.Everything always has to be her way, if she doesn't get it then she blows up and gets mad and he gives in to her.  Finally she decides to leave the boat.  She can't take the rich lifestyle, he is not at her beck and call, he won't give up working - I don't suppose she has ever considered that all those companies that he owns have people working for them that depend on that job to live and support their families and the responsibility of all of it falls back on him. Every time things didn't go her way she would lock herself in her room.  What is she?  12!!  She sure didn't act her age and a gal that had the experiences she had had.I was glad when she left the boat and thought good riddance, he deserves better.  Then he comes back and he is willing to give up every thing to be with her, blah, blah blah.  I didn't even read to the ending I was so outdone with this whole scene.  he gives up every thing and she gives up nothing and she is right about everything.  Oh yeah, I can see this one lasting forever.  I ended up not liking it at all.  I thought the heroine was a selfish bitch. Just talk to the Vet; she (he) went to school for the love of animals.Our young cat and old dog sniff noses together every night. Molly was brought home to our daughter's cat and slept with Tigger many years. Our children's friends would pull into the driveway and see a cat rubbing against an 85 pound dog. The way they got along was a preview of Heaven.Our cats Leo and Loni loved dogs, too. Sometimes I think Noah's Ark landed here. The magic Noah wielded to keep peace on the Ark has been engrained in our little piece of land.The author says all of you can have that peace. Our cats were older when they met their dog friends. Leo and Loni were 5 and 7 when Gaston and Pepper were pups. Tigger was about 10 whenen Molly first came home, all 7 weeks old. Initially the cats ignored the dogs, probably because the cats knew they could take them.I agree that our dog is happier with a friend, and it doesn't matter if that friend is canine or feline. Four men, longtime friends, meet every year for a trip. Some of the trips have been wonderful, some have not, but they have all been unique. This year the four decide to go on a hunt to find a bestselling author. Nick Roberts is a ghost, never seen or heard from. They guys are seeking a chance at fame, but for journalist Steve finding Mr. Roberts could be the story of a lifetime.Every now and then a book will touch your heart, and for me this was one of those books. The Celtic Fan is in a way two stories that intersect into one. The first story was Nick Roberts’ star-crossed lovers Bill and Claire. They were a couple very much in love, but faced opposition because of the religions they practiced. Throughout the book there are snippets of the story that was born of love and died in tragedy. The second story brings Steve and Diana. While on his search for Nick Roberts he meets the enchanting woman who changes his life.I am going to take a moment to gush and praise Hall for such a breathtaking romance. It is unlike most of the romances I read which are usually fare that is significantly more spicy. The Celtic Fan has moments, but I prefer to call them passionate and deep. The relationships in this book weren’t something that was fleeting. I can’t describe the book as anything but beautiful.I cannot rightly end this review without commenting on the more technical part of Hall’s writing. Hall’s words were so illustrative, I could see every tree, and hear every sound. Once I was immersed in the novel it took over my senses. The way she brought the personalities to life was stunning. I felt heartbreak for Bill and Claire, as well as elation for Steve and Diana. Her story telling was just eloquent.If you are more into hard core erotica, this may not be for you. If you want a genuine love story that is passionate, tender, and sentimental please don’t let this beautiful story pass you by.*Reviewed by Teresa D. for ThatsErotica.com*

reviewText: Forty-year-old Vince Fierro is at a crossroads.  After three failed marriages, he suddenly begins to wonder if the problem isn't that he chose the wrong women, but that he chose women at all.  For a good Italian boy raised in a huge Catholic family, it's a terrifying question to suddenly be asking himself.  After confessing his confusion to his sister, he decides to take her advice and go to a gay bar.  If he's not attracted to anyone, he's not gay.  The experiment ends in miserable failure, until he runs into Trey Giles.Trey's family and Vinnie's have been friends forever.  When Trey sees Vinnie at the bar, he's astonished.  Seeing Vinnie's discomfort, he takes him to a jazz club, where they share a hot dance Trey can't get out of his mind for days afterward.  Between college, his two jobs, and taking care of his grandmother and mother, Trey really doesn't have time to help a guy who's just discovering he might be gay, but something about Vinnie makes Trey want to make the time.Can the tentative feelings forming between Vinnie and Trey survive Vinnie's fears and Trey's difficult circumstances?I absolutely loved Family Man.  Vinnie and Trey are wonderful characters.  Both men are caretakers who feel a lot of responsibility toward their families.  Vinnie's huge Italian family is a lot of the reason he's afraid to admit he might be gay.  The last thing he wants to do is disappoint them, or cause them to turn from him.  The family has strong Catholic beliefs that make Vinnie's fears a real possibility.  It's during a plumbing job at the home of a married gay couple that Vinnie begins to consider he might be gay, and he freaks out.  After gathering his courage, he tells his sister about what he's been thinking, and thanks to her advice ends up at a gay bar.  It's not his scene at all, until Trey shows up.  Trey's more than a decade younger, and really attractive, and Vinnie is terrified of him--or more accurately, of the attraction he feels for him.  Once he allows himself to go with the flow, however, he begins to enjoy himself.  Unfortunately, no matter how much fun he's having, or how much he's starting to care for Trey, his fears won't go away.Trey has his own problems.  At twenty-five, he's still in school because he spends most of his time working to support his grandmother and alcoholic mother.  He's also still a virgin.  Dating Vinnie, who isn't anywhere near ready for sex, seems like the perfect way to have fun and spend time with someone without the demands another guy might put on him.  Of course nothing is that simple, and pretty soon Trey starts to want the strings he thought he didn't want.  His feelings grow deeper and deeper, but his family and Vinnie's could spell the end of their relationship.Family Man has so many things going for it I couldn't help but love it.  Both heroes are men I'd want to know in real life.  I sympathized with both of them, and shared in their joys and sorrows.  The secondary characters, especially Trey's grandma and Vinnie's large, Italian family, are great.  The conflicts are all realistic, and handled beautifully.  The story is told in alternating styles--third person for Vinnie, and first person for Trey.  That should have been weird, but was so well done that I ended up really liking it.  The partnership of Marie Sexton and Heidi Cullinan brought all the best things about their work together into one delightful book.  I can't recommend Family Man highly enough.Cassie for Joyfully Reviewed

She needed to be thought of as an individual and he gave that piece of heaven to her.DISLIKES:I've said it before and I will say it again, I cannot stand the insta-love stuff!! Lastly, the ending bothered me but most of the time when authors leave an ending open like that it usually means they are going to continue the characters stories so I hope that is the case for this one!!I really want to know more about Abby and Annika and it would be nice to have a second book that worked on their relationship or even give Annika the second book to see why she was such aC U Next Tuesday!Other than the insta-love and the ending, I really enjoyed this book, and I would like to see more from these characters, I feel like I am left hanging and I need to know MORE!!So I recommend this book to anyone who loves a good love story with a crazy plot and a psycho twin sister. reviewText: It's difficult to characterize the myth of St George the dragon-slayer.  He is an important character in the consciousness of English-speaking people and in the history of English literature.  He appears as a protector in Spenser's Faerie Queene as well as John Bunyon's Pilgrim's Progress.  Edward III made him the patron of the Order of the Garter, and his distinctive red cross on the white background, with transverse arms longer than the vertical, has been a symbol of England since about 1270.However, St George appears in the literature of the rest of the western world from India to Portugal.  There are connections to stories as ancient as that of Perseus.  According to the hagiographies, George was born in Lydda, some ten miles from Tel Aviv, where Perseus rescued Andromeda by slaying a sea dragon (according to Strabo, Pausanias, Josephus, etc.).  Eastern Orthodox depictions of St George always include a young woman in the background, who is not specifically said to be Andromeda.So George is not unique to Britain or British mythology, yet Badden-Powell and the Boy Scouts claim him to have been the patron saint of the Knights of the Round Table.The introduction of Morgan Le Fay in the last chapter also leads one to believe that British or Arthurian mythology is going to be important to this series.  When Mr Schubach incorporates elements of myth or legend into his stories, he imparts a sense of background and familiarity that enrich the tales and make them that much more enjoyable.

reviewText: I had a dormant Twitter account for awhile. I just didn't get it. A lot in this book is common sense but I also learned a lot from it too. It is full of great resources and links for Twitter. I have used a lot of them. If you are new to Twitter this is a must have!!!!!!!!Here's something interesting I got out of the book. So when they dump me after following them I dump them back! Ha ha! Take that shallow unethical Twitter Follower seeking Twitter people. Um...okay....Anyway.....I am now a Social Butterfly on Twitter!  Sounds cheesy, but it's true! :0)

I read alot of Amish Romance stories. 1) you can find several FREE books for Kindle and 2) they're CLEAN. Alot of free books for Kindle have raunchy, porn-like sex scenes in them. Without the sex, Amish Romance novels focus more on the relationship between the two people and their devotion to God, above all.This book was short. I read it in about an hour while my son was napping this afternoon.This book wasn't what I was expecting. The relationship between the courting couple wasn't really the focus of this story; the hateful mother who despised her daughter and viciously emotionally abused her was the focus. As stated above, I read alot of Amish Romance, and I haven't really met a character I didn't like that wasn't redeemed or didn't repent and change their ways by the end of the story. SPOILER ALERT-- that doesn't happen for this character. Toward the end, she gets nuttier and nuttier, with crazy thoughts entering her head and spewing out of her mouth. She finally decides to leave and a peace falls over Peace Crossing.. BUT WAIT, then she's back. And in a simple paragraph, she meets her end and the characters move on. It's almost like the storyline got away from the author, or she didn't quite know what to do with this woman once she dove off the deep end... It wasn't a bad story, I just didn't really connect with the characters as much as I wanted to.

Two strangers, because of a deathbed promise, are married.  Husband, Jack, professional military and a colonel in the army, leaves very soon after the wedding for Canada where he's posted for the next 5 years.  Wife, Elizabeth, recent widow of Jack's best friend, is naturally distraught.  She remained at Jack's home recovering from her grief, caring for Jack's mentally confused mother and learning to manage Jack's modest estate.Then comes the gossip and all hell breaks loose.This book was just all over the place for me.5 stars for showing, very well, the extremely tenuous circumstances of unprotected and "poor relation" females of the era.5 stars for the subtle portrayal of the insularity of village life.2.5 stars for excessive development of Elizabeth's character.  (The problem is usually the opposite.)  I would have liked equal  billing for Jack.-1 star for Elizabeth being a sanctimonious twit5 stars for the author's research and adherence to history and to the mores of the period.  I'm willing to give license regarding Elizabeth's having a horse in Brussels, etc.2.5 stars for a rather wooden, unconvincing love story.So, mathematically,this story ends up a 3.2 stars for me.I realize this is a strange review.  Sorry.  Did my best.
Enjoyed this story.  Could relate to the subject and was well written.

Gabriella is a humorous, and exquisite blend of sexuality between the two main characters from different school backgrounds, St Swithins Public School first eleven and the local working class grammar school.The story of the cricket match is well written with bawdy and humorous segments , it is hard to put down once you commence reading.Alan Hardy has the ability to draw you into a story, this being the second book I have read by  him ,  the other being  `Good Queen Beth.' reviewText: I spent a good part of my early life in the mid 1940'-50's in a small town in Ohio. We had gossips just like those in this story. Oh my, don't be a divorced woman or the daughters of one and live in 'their' town. I know those ladies well.I thought it was gone until I went to a church outside of Atlanta. The preacher - a really great one - was divorced and remarried. His wife taught exercise classes - OH MY!! You could tell there was a lot of love between them but the gossips had their say about her. Her hair was not 'normal'; she was not a teacher - an acceptable profession and it goes on.What Paul and Martie faced is alive and well unfortunately but Bob & Beth will endure as Paul and Martie did, facing the gossips and living as God intended man and woman to live.A really sweet story about how to tell the truth of your feelings, how to reconcile them and live life, what you see is not necessarily what you get - and maybe win over the town (church) gossips. Good quick read.

Black Hills Blessing is the second book in the Black Hills series. I recently read the first book in the series and absolutely loved it! Many characters from the first book make appearances in this book, however, this book primarily focuses on Garrett's story. Garrett is Matt Johnson's older brother and a partner in the business the two own in South Dakota.I was captivated by Garrett's story from the very beginning. I loved how the relationship between him and Rayne took longer to develop and establish then most relationships, even though there was obvious chemistry between them from the beginning of the book.The pace and speed at which the book and the storyline developed was an amazing decision and choice made by this author. This allowed for all of the important matters to be addressed properly and in an unrushed fashion.The secondary characters in this series and this book were by far some of my favourite secondary characters I have ever read about. They tied the story together beautifully and created the scenes that ever good book should have.This book is a beautifull extension of the series. A.C Wilson has done a tremendous job with this novel. There are not many authors that are able to keep the slowed down pace and still captivate readers with the story. This is definitely a 5 star read!!

The fourth book in the Until series finds Nico Mayson, the tattooed bad boy bounty hunter brother, meeting Sophie Grates when he returns her cell phone.  Nico knows at first sight that she’s his “boom” and he’s not going to let her get away, no matter what she does to protect herself from life.The GoodI liked Nico and Sophie, even if the story was very similar to earlier entries in the series.  Ms. Reynolds’ writing has progressed with each entry and I think this is much more cohesive and the grammar/punctuation errors aren’t as abundant. The strength of the whole series has been the focus on family and that hasn’t changed here.The BadIt’s a bit of the same issues I’ve had before.  The stream of consciousness writing is difficult to pull off, the info-dump of some big moments instead of writing them can be frustrating, and Nico is a return to the uber alpha-hole template (his desire to impregnate Sophie immediately wasn’t one of my fave moves).The Bottom LineBy the fourth book you know what you’re getting with Ms. Reynolds, and it’s either your cup of tea or it isn’t.  Until Lilly still stands as my favorite book of the series.
summary: The fourth book is more of the same....

Without Doubt is the second novel in C.J. Azevedo’s series Without though it can be read as a stand alone. I’m not at all sure about my overall feelings for Without Doubt, I’m leaning towards saying I liked it, but didn’t love it.Ava Sterling is a very grown up 22 year old, she is a strong character but very stubborn. From start to finish there was something about her that just didn’t sit well with me, I found myself rolling my eyes at her more times than not. She did have a lot going on in her life though so if I had to pick a few words to describe her they would be kind, caring but sometimes annoying.Declan James, though he is definitely a sexy as sin MMA fighter, his borderline obsession with Ava from the get go didn’t really make me warm to him. He is used to getting everything he wants which makes him come across as a bit of a brat but as the story progresses he becomes very sweet and loving and an all round nice guy which gets a huge thumbs up from me.Plot wise, the first few chapters were pretty painful for me to read. I love instant lust between characters, not instant love or instant attraction. Instant love and attraction needs to be built up and played out well, instant lust though can happen from the get go. Instant attraction is what we got between Ava and Declan which just made me shake my head, wanting to go out with someone before you even know them is just…blah!Getting past that and really reading into the story was when it got good. I picked up on how things were going to play out and what would happen early on in the book but it didn’t change that fact that I still enjoyed reading it. The start to the book, near the ending and some characteristics of the characters let me down overall but it was still an enjoyable read.

Eliza Terribury is a heroine who I liked for most of this novel and then she becomes someone I really didn't admire at the end of the novel.  For this reason, Rebel Marquess does not merit above 2.5 stars.Eliza has a mamma who has high ambitions for her daughters.  She wants them to make excellent matches and her mother has always wanted to add Michael Gerard, the Marquess of Rutherford as one of her son-in-laws.  She has been unsuccessful but her machinations are well honed by time youngest daughter Eliza s on the marriage mart.Eliza never wants to marry she only wants to publish her romantic novels.  She has never had any true romance herself but has a pretty active imagination.  She fears a husband will not allow her to write and feels he will stifle her life. Michael knows he will marry one day but he is in no hurry and he certainly does not want to marry into the Terribury family.Unfortunately Eliza and Michael are caught in a compromising position and they agree to a pretend engagement.  They both do not want to marry and they figure they will find a way to escape the betrothal at a more opportune time.Eliza really likes Michael who is witty and charming.  Still she stubbornly keeps her mantra of "I will never marry."  Eliza is at heart a romantic yet does not really believe in romance and the power of love and acceptance.  She writes of love but cannot recognize it in her own life nor can she understand its life altering power.Michael is emotionally smarter that Eliza.  He makes a mistake here and there but of the two, he is much more willing to change his course when love takes hold of his heart.  He is a passionate man and an honorable one too.Eliza is afraid to change her path but even worse she is rash and her actions have devastating effects on the people she loves.  It's hard to believe a smart woman can be so oblivious about her hurtful actions toward her leading man and her family too.  I liked Eliza through most of this novel but by the end, I really stopped caring for her.  Her behavior was hurtful in the extreme to Michael and I never felt she was overly sorry for hurting him so deeply or showed enough remorse.

The cover shows a cute bunny. The book is organized very well. There is a table of contents with a Prologue and five one-page chapters. All of the links to the chapters work. There are no other photos/illustrations in the book. SPOILER ALERT: The little bunny, named Hopsy, was told by his parents he was going to be getting a brother. He hops off into the forest and begins telling everyone that he will be getting a brother. When he told the fox, the fox told him he would get less attention from his parents with the new baby brother. The bear gave him some honey for his little brother. The owl told him he would have to share everything with his brother. The wild boar informed him there was a food shortage, and so there would not be as much food available for his brother. By the time he reached the goldfish and told her the good news, he was feeling a bit sad. The goldfish told the bunny that he should look through the forest for hidden eggs, and then his baby brother would have food. The bunny (Hopsy) searched through the forest, found the eggs, and took them home to his parents. The next day everyone in the forest was talking about the little bunny that was searching for eggs in the forest; the story grew and grew until it became the story of the "Easter bunny and colorful Easter eggs."I liked the story idea, but I had a lot of difficulty reading it. It was almost like the book was originally written in another language and translated into English as the phrasing was different. An example is in the author's book description on Amazon: "They tell him something which makes our little bunny decide to take care for everyone he loves." Examples in the book: "Trees were expanding their vivid green branches higher and the higher into the blue sky." "The next who he met was a wise owl which told him..." "Little goldfish felt sorry for Hopsy and discovered him a secret that somewhere..."I did not notice any misspelling. It was formatted perfectly across all of my devices. I would have given it 3-stars, but since the formatting was correct and the table of contents worked I am giving it 4 stars -- that was worth the extra star!
summary: The story of how the Easter bunny came to be.

When Ashly is dumped by her nervous fiance on her wedding day, she recovers by making a living as a fashion photographer and throws herself into her work to forget about Jake. She also runs a fashion line with her friend, Nadia, but they run into financial problems and can't afford the rent. So when Ashly is offered $25 million dollars if she travels around the world with her ex, she has no choice but to say yes. According to her mother's will, her and Jake have to sleep in the same hotel room and take pictures at a variety of romantic places. And though the will doesn't make sense to them, they are both promised the cash if they follow the guidelines. Ashly decides to go along with it not just for the money, but to also get a video diary from her deceased mother. Her mother always hated Jake and she wonders why she tried to break them up, and yet now wants them to go on the trip together.It's been five years since they split, but being with Jake again stirs up all the old feelings. At first, Ashly is cold towards him, but eventually she starts to warm to him again. He's now a firefighter in Texas and he's matured an realised what a bad mistake he made. It's quite an emotional read, and sad in parts, and you can't help feeling for Ashly. The reader gets to travel the world with the couple and you feel like your actually there.I recommend this story and it was certainly a bargain. Great work for a new author.

"Stand To... A Journey to Manhood" brought back a flood of memories of my time in-country.  Just over 40 years ago, I was a field artillery 1Lt serving as an advisor to the Montagnards in the Central Highlands of South Vietnam.  I could thus relate to Frank's detailed descriptions of the geography and of the local people.  I hold the Montagnards in the highest possible esteem.The book focuses on Frank's time in-country and is not intended to be a history of or political commentary on the Vietnam War.  It would thus be of more interest to a Vietnam veteran rather than a reader wanting to learn about the Vietnam War in general terms.My friends have been pushing me for several years to write my recollections about my 30-year Army career.  Frank's book has given me another nudge in that direction.
summary: Brought Back a Flood of Memories

I received a review copy of this book via the Goodreads Don't Buy My Love program.Geoffrey has just  broken up with his boyfriend Brian after two years of dating. He's upset  and frustrated and humiliated because Brian posted a sex video of Geoffrey bound, gagged and blindfolded on YouTube. It's Valentine's Day and Geoffrey is nursing his anguish at a bar, when Brian's best friend Paul joins him.Paul has had a secret crush on Geoffrey for many years, but they were always committed to others. Paul is outraged over Brian's treatment of Geoffrey, and tries to convince Geoffrey to come home with him.Geoffrey is nervous about Paul's motives but they do go back to Paul's condo. The men begin to work through the issues Geoffrey has concerning Brian and his betrayal. In fact, at a couple points Brian intrudes on Paul and Geoffrey's intimacy. There are nasty words and even blows exchanged. (I kinda felt like the fight scene was a bit over-the -top)It is not long before Paul reveals the extent of his desire for Geoffrey, and while Geoffrey reciprocates, to a degree, he is unwilling to let Paul fight all his battles.I liked Geoffrey; he seemed so grounded, and so open. Paul was a bit of an extremist--and had a few anger issues I wished he'd overcome. They actually seem very good together, however, and I was glad that Geoffrey overcame his humiliation. In the end Brian turned out not to be the source of all evil, so that was nice.The smexytimes were super sexy, and frequent, considering the novella's length.

Bella quit speaking to her father years ago. He may be the vampire king and she his only daughter but she can't forgive him killing her husband years ago. She was a spy during WWII and helped save many children. Falling in love with the wrong man was all she did wrong.  Years later she is sent Brent O'Hara he was a Marine who worked for her father. When he lost his legs and a hand in battle he has about gave up. Cormac the previous vampire king is hoping Bella and Brent can heal each others wounds and reunite Bella with him. They have a lot of issues to get over and they have to keep their lust under control.I really liked Bella as she isn't the typical vampire you read about. She doesn't like to kill unless they deserve it and she loves to help those in need. She has a soft caring side as well as the hard stubborn side. She can be very passionate and she doesn't like being told what to do. Brent thinks no one could ever want him again and he is useless. He opens up around Bella wen he sees she won't give him pity or rejection. He is a very charming sexy man who just doesn't realize it.I enjoyed reading this as you get to see Bella in different time periods. She has done many things to be helpful over the years to many. She may be a vampire and I love that side of her I also love the soft side a whole lot. Seeing her with children will warm your heart as I am sure it did hers. She and Brent butt heads quite often and while they are both still healing that sometimes is the best thing for them. I also appreciate the fact that while Brent is a big strong guy he still lets Bella take the lead and even does what she says when she is in danger. This is a very intriguing read and if I had one bad thing to say about it it would be that I wanted more. I could read a whole series about these two.

Master Prince, the second book in the Master of Tabu Series is another hot, steamy, delicious read from author, Ms Gray Dixon.  This time it follows the exploits of Club Tabu's chief counsel, Mitchell Prince as he spars, both in and out of the playroom, with Giulliana Hathaway, counsel for one of Club Tabu's regular members.In order to nail Club Tabu for promoting violence against women, Giulliana decides to a little more research that pits her against the enigmatic Masked Avenger before she finds out who he really is.  Research becomes a hands-on exploration in so many ways, not only with respect to D/s relationships, but also becomes a cathartic release for Giulliana of wounds deeply buried and best forgotten.And Master Prince is there to help her.Ms Dixon never disappoints. She successfully juxtaposes Giulliana's subconsciously submissive behaviour and deftly differentiates it from the fear that underscores Giulliana's childhood trauma. Mitchell Prince, although a ruthless corporate lawyer,  becomes Giulliana's anchor.  He helps her get past the abuse Giulliana experienced and embrace the pleasure and pain he gives her through their play. Mitchell makes Giulliana realize that exploring her sexuality as a submissive is not the same as being beaten into submission.Another incredibly erotic read with a lot of food for thought, Master Prince is another great offering from Ms Gray Dixon.Kudos!

Office Hours was a much anticipated read for me, as it's set in one of my favourite places, Buxton in Derbyshire. For that reason, I pounced on it when it was released.I had no idea what to expect, as it's Sam Crescent's first release, but I'm happy to say I was not disappointed. I was enthralled by the characters and storyline from the very beginning and kept flipping those virtual pages, desperate to find out what happened next.In brief, the story is about Anya King and her boss, Nathan Banks. He's a somewhat arrogant man and Anya is his super-efficient, super-aloof PA. Their relationship has always been completely professional. Anya does her job, does it well and doesn't take any crap from Nathan. He respects her and thinks she's very good at her job. He also fancies her, and she him, but there's never been so much as a hint of this between them before. That is, until now.The fun begins when Anya discovers that Nathan has booked a team-building weekend for the two of them - without telling her until the last minute. She already had sexy weekend plans and isn't happy about being forced to cancel them, especially when she finds out why. She does as she's ordered, and goes along, but she makes her displeasure very clear.Soon, though, the frosty atmosphere between them is melted away by their attraction to one another. They gradually get to know more about one another on a personal basis, rather than their usual office professionalism. And the more they discover, the more compatible they appear to be.Eventually, they give into temptation and have some seriously hot sex. But is it just physical attraction between them - or does their compatibility spell something longer term? Will they risk having their fragile hearts broken again? And what happens at the office? Read the book to have all these questions and many more answered...I really enjoyed this novella. It was a quick, easy read, but it sure was satisfying. A brilliant debut release and one that I'd recommend if you like a quickie m/f, romantic read.

I think that it could have happened sooner in the book. The heat in this book was worth the wait. I like that Lizzy had realized her greatest strength lie in her ability to being submissive. I would recommend this book but would also suggest to pack your patience; know that it is worth the wait.Playing Rough:This is the second episode in the Billionaires in Disguise series by Blair Bablyon.  In this episode Lizzy begins her BDSM relationship with Mannix Bonfils.  This is Lizzy’s first BDSM relationship.  After her failed attempt at a relationship with Theo Valencia, Mannix’s half-brother, you really wanted to see Lizzy happy.  You quickly see her going down the wrong road fast.  She thinks that Mannix can give her all she needs. Strength and love, the things she was lacking all her life.  At first you think Mannix will provide all those things but you soon see how manipulative he becomes.  The person who seems like the hero becomes the villain.I could not put this book down. I needed to see what happened next.  Would Theo, who is aware of all Mannix ways and who you can see cares about Lizzy, step in and play the white knight? Would Lizzy finally wake up and know that this type of relationship is not for her? I had to know.  Unfortunately, not all questions were answered but enough to give you hope. Especially when Mannix puts Lizzy in Theo’s care for a week while he goes out of town.I look forward to reading the next episode.  I want to see Lizzy get her happily ever after.

I rarely read a book that has this much information in such a small package. Many writers fill their books with fluff to up the page count, but Marg McAlister writes lean and to the point, and actually ends up giving us more of what we need to write a romance novel than wordy writers.One of the tips I appreciated had to do with choosing the name of my characters. She gave a great tip about the choice of names that has actually bugged me in the past. I'm glad she is bringing that problem to the attention of writers.Another point has to do with critique partners, and she gives us a surprising reason why we should have one. There is much more information in this book that is helpful to writers. She then closes with three great checklists and a list of resources that alone are worth the price.This really is a must-have guide to romance writing. I've not read her other books, but will definitely check them out. McAlister's experience and willingness to share puts her at the top of the go-to authors if you want to learn about writing romantic stories.

Star Struck,  follows Heather Wainwright, an A-List Hollywood actress with a diva reputation that precedes her. Though that reputation may not be wholly deserving or accurate, Seth Rafferty comes to think it is when he meets Heather at a charity event for an urban arts program. These two are not sold on one another. There first conversations are highly memorable, and to say there is no love at first sight between these two is the understatement of the century.That doesn’t deter these two from trying to figure out what it is they are seeing and feeling in one another. What ensues between these two as they try to figure out what in the hell they’re feeling for one another makes for a truly engaging story with some laugh out loud moments, a smidge bit of spanking, many instances of wanting to reach in and hug and/or possibly hit the characters, and plenty of events that will just make you smile about these two.Star Struck was a fantastically fun and engaging story that had me hooked in until the very end. Even when I wanted to strangle Heather or slap Seth, I loved it. It kept me entertained throughout, and I couldn’t wait to see how it would all work out.This book did a wonderful job of combining it all. It had some fantastically created characters with some bumpy pasts, it had humor, it had plenty of spice, and it had that connection and spark we all love to read about. It also does a pretty magnificent job of balancing the heavy with the light.

I really wanted to like this novel.  There is a kernel of a good story here, but this story is an example of why a good editor is needed to make a successful novel.The book purportedly is about manipulation by the military of religious perceptions, and this is actually quite an interesting idea.  The military uses high-tech holograms to create religious visions aimed at preparing the population for a feared alien invasion.  And this is where the story should have focused.Instead, the story takes in a huge cast of characters, many contributing absolutely nothing to the plot.  The storyline plods on and on, taking side-trips to who knows where, yet when it is all supposed to be pulled together to a climax, it compresses this into a very short, unsatisfying ending.In addition to the meandering storyline, some of the writing is amateurish and just plain wrong.  For example, there is one character who is almost always identified as "General Nate Williams."  Not  sometimes "General Williams."  Not "the general."  Not "he."  Always "General Nate Williams."  This is even when others are talking about him, as in "Have you checked if General Nate Williams is really in his room?"This "over-specification" pops up time and time again with both people and places.  In the story "North Mexico" is the 51st state of the US, as is described the first time it pops up in the narrative.  However, each and every time after that, is it always referred to as "North Mexico, the 51st state of the United States."  One character even uses the exact phrasing when speaking to a politician from North Mexico, as if she might have forgotten that the state was now part of the US.  Later on, the author seems to forget about North Mexico and writes that El Paso is on the Mexican border, which it is now, of course, but would not be if there was a state of North Mexico.An important locale in the story is in a "space hotel," a hotel which perches on an elevator 35,000 miles long and is secretly used by the military from which to beam their holograms.  This makes absolutely no sense.  A 35,000 mile elevator supporting a hotel in space would be totally unfeasible.  First, why?  The International Space Station is in orbit from 150-250 miles above the surface of the earth.  So what possible advantage could come from making the hotel at 35,000 miles?  The cost alone for the elevator would be more than for the construction of every skyscraper on earth.  And all for a hotel?Then there are the descriptions of the "dangers" of the South American jungles.  In her narrative, the author has an army of  jaguars, maned  wolves, and others creating such a danger that humans cannot be out at night without a severe risk of getting killed.  Pretty much none of that is accurate.  Jaguars need huge swaths of land as their territory, and to see even one is amazing.  Attacks on humans are extremely rare.  Maned wolves do not even live in the jungle, and they are extremely shy animals.  While is it easy to get poked, bitten, stung, and whatever in the Brazilian jungle, and it is possible to catch a deadly disease, getting violently killed is quite hard to do.The holograms also seemed to be able to have physical effects.  A hologram of Anubis was able to shake parts of walls and ceilings down.  They also seemed to be able to kill.These are just a few examples of inconsistencies and downright errors.  Some are fleeting and barely register, others are more jarring and interrupt the reading.Despite the above comments, there really is a story here.  All the author needs is a good editor to help her form and shape the book, to help her with the inaccuracies.  The author's descriptive skills are quite good.  She can paint a precise and clear picture of what she is describing.  And the core premise of the book is fascinating and can be given an interesting treatment.I am just reviewing the novel.  I am not an established editor or a famous author.  But in my opinion, the author would do well to take this story and have a good editor go over it with her, then re-release it to the public.

reviewText: My Review: 4.5 Stars our of 5 *****By the Everlast, I really enjoyed this Novella. The Budget Cooking 30 Recipes for Under $5 by author Delynda Middelton is a good basic cookbook for frugal living. Her cookbook has a few flaws. Some of those flaws are editorial while one major flaw concerns food safety. To wit: Her cookbook would have been so much better if there was an interactive table of contents included making navigation easy.As to food safety:  At location 91 she writes "Benefits of the Slow Cooker: You can put meals in there in the morning...even frozen meat!..." The USDA does not recommend cooking frozen meat in the slow cooker as it is considered unsafe.I do agree with most of her suggestions for for purchasing a waffle maker, bread machine, food chopper or food processor, and slow cooker. If you have the right kitchen tools you will be more likely to cook at home rather than buying processed foods or eating out. I do somewhat disagree with her suggestion to make waffles as waffles can be expensive to make. Her waffle recipe is rather inexpensive as her recipe uses 2 eggs and 1/2 cup vegetable oil. Some waffle recipes use far more eggs and other expensive ingredients. An even cheaper alternative would have been a pancake recipe. Pancakes can be made with a minimum amount of ingredients such as eggs, fat and milk. You can also make pancakes ahead and flash freeze them for later reheating and eating.It would have been helpful if the author had included recipes for some basic food mixes such as the USDA baking mix (you can use this for making pancakes, waffles or biscuits) and the USDA baking mix is in the public domain when last checked. Homemade food mixes tend to save money and use basic kitchen staples.I did like her list of pantry ingredients and things you can store in the freezer to help ease meal prep. I've done a lot of the things she has suggested. Granted I've been cooking for close to 50 years.Some of the recipes you will find in her cookbook include:Abby's Favorite WafflesChicken & Vegetable Stir-Fry (a truly unique stir-fry recipe)Chicken Noodle SoupBaked Pork ChopsThis is a good basic frugal living cookbook.Recommend with caveats given.Penmouse
summary: Good basic cookbook for frugal living

A homeless man dies at Lalla's feet in an alley after he's been warned to stop leaving cut out snowflakes/love letters attached to her car.The man's mother points her finger at Lalla as the murderess. The dead man's aunt wants to talk to Lalla but goes missing. And a newsman whose body is found in Lalla's Cadillac is linked to all of them. Is anything what it seems?I like this series and the author has a wonderful story telling ability. This novel was fast moving and although lots of suspicion was cast over the supporting players I had guessed whodunit quite early on, but I was never 100% sure until the end.This novel has some editing problems. Looks like an editor was changing sentences around and forgot to go back and delete extra words. Punctuation shows up in odd places and punctuation is missing at the end of sentences and quotation marks are missing. I was confused at one point over who was talking. Mostly because the respondent's sentence was tagged into another person's paragraph. A lot of little things that distract a reader from an otherwise good story and slows down the reading trying to figure out what just happened here.For me the most annoying thing about this story was the random use of French words. These people are in California not Quebec and one of them is occasionally speaking in French when neither of the woman are known to have grown up in a bilingual family, studied French together, or have a French connection. I grew up in a bilingual household and studied French in school and university and I never use French unless everyone in the room speaks it or myself or someone else is providing a translation, otherwise its just rude. That's how I was brought up and how I felt when I read those passages minus a translation for those who might not understand this foreign language. There didn't seem to be any point to the one character who was speaking French and didn't add anything to the storyline. Typos in French too. Caught me by surprise but the author got it right a little later in the book. Just one of these things that kept me questioning why, why, why and disrupted an otherwise good read.Well written, not well edited, interesting characters, good dialogue, and a fast moving story that made me want to keep turning the pages. A good, fun read.

I guess the most amazing thing about Mishka Shubaly's drug and alcohol soaked memoir is how much he is able to remember.In some circles used to be that when a baby started teething, parents would massage the infant's gums with bourbon or more often vodka, which didn't taste as bad. The alcohol soothed the hurt and quieted the kid down.Shubaly was likely one of those infants. For him the alcohol started while he was still in diapers, before conscious memory, and didn't stop for the next three decades.  When he grew up, got older, and after alcohol no longer made him feel good - just not bad - he started with opiates and heavy duty non-opiate helpers such as Opana, and he'd snort it and after just a line or two he felt as if his body was" bursting with love."At 32, he was used to his face scraping the floor. "I got a job, got fired, got another job, got dumped, moved onto a friend's busted futon, joined a band, got fired, bottomed out, got sober, got a job and started drinking again. I'll give you a nickel if you can detect a pattern."Then he got sober and stayed that way, for two days straight, then two months, now it's been two years.A friend hired him to manage a place called the Beauty Bar on 14th Street in NYC. One night a buddy working in the bar was sucker-punched by a drunken Aussie and he landed on the floor unconscious with a big knob on the back of his head.Shubaly hung around until the friend got transported to the hospital. By then he was too bummed out to think about pedaling his bike home across the bridge into Brooklyn. He cabbed it. The point is, the next morning he decided to run back across the bridge to get his bike. To run. This is just after he got sober and it hurt but it really felt good, too. He kept at it. Running. He ran marathons and he stayed sober and his outlook changed.Running became the new possible. Instead of only bad, running became proof that he could do good things, too. And that's pretty much the story.It's a lot of people's story and the job for Shubaly is to tell it in a way that keeps things interesting. I think that deep down this guy wrote about himself so that we'd come to like him and to appreciate his rehab and resilience. I think he's the type of guy who just wants to be liked. So it's a good thing he comes across as a really likeable guy.I think you should read his story. I've given you a couple details. He has a raft of anecdotes and encounters that will amaze and amuse. But most of all, my guess is he'll win you over the way he did me.When he hit bottom, he says, he "lived on foot in the gutter and the other in the grave, face down on the bar with both middle fingers in the air." It's not that way anymore. And the turnabout is a rich story told well. Hey, dude, keep on running.

Like the previous reviewer, I could only get partway into this book. I have read in the M/M genre for over 4 years, with many being BDSM novels (think along the lines of Chris Owens's excellent Deviations series). Based on my overall impression of BDSM, I found this book to be a pretty poor representation of what it means to be in a true Dom/sub interaction. The main characters, two boys in a band, are portrayed more as a leader and a follower, a pursuer and the pursuee, the latter not even sure he is gay, but thinks he is a submissive.  The author does not explore any complex thought process here. The dialogue feels artificial, just "saying the right lines" if you will. It feels like a bad intro into this aspect of sexual interaction and seems that it could lead a reader looking for accurate depictions of BDSM with the wrong impressions and/or directions. The title is also a bit harsh. The proper Dom/sub relationship is not about breaking someone. To do that is evil. A new book that might better satisfy reading about BDSM is SJD Peterson's Pup (Guards of Folsom), and no, that is not a book about prison guards.

This story starts violently and pretty much stays that way for the majority of this novel.  It is a story of injustice, betrayal, revenge with the slight chance for justice at the end of a long painful road. There is too much story to allow a reviewer the latitude to give a reader the scope of this novel, it has a bit of everything, love, betrayal, dark forces, divine intervention, old prophecy, and in some future novel an epic ending.  So many things hang on events that you need to discover for yourself that would be spoilers if I tell too much.The vast majority of Marek's family was slain in a surprise attack by Mircea.  Now Marek's whole world not revolves around keeping the remainder of his family safe and obtaining the justified revenge for his family.  Mircea must die a most painful if possible for our hero to have peace.  This novel is the first installment in Marek's story of his journey for his revenge which will cover the world and possibly even worlds beyond this one.  The problem is that there are unseen forces working against him and the possibilities of an ancient prophesy yet to be fulfilled.There is at least one situation that many (most?) readers will find repugnant as did I but it does add to the desire for retribution and revenge that is the heart of this story.  Again, to tell more gives away too much.I guess without writing a book, the short version is this, it is a dark and violent story of retribution denied.  Some of the most ultimate evils and corruption are described in this novel so this is not for the weak or timid.  I believe there is going to be a good day for Marek but it is going to be a dark path that takes him there before there is justice.I cannot say much more since all I really want is to get the other books when they are released and get this whole story, this seems to be an epic undertaking and I cannot wait to see it through to the end, hopefully without any cliffhangers.I gave this novel 4 Stars because it left me wanting much more of this addicting story but I am a revenge junkie as always and nothing reads better for me..  It should be noted that this is NOT a novel for everyone, it is dark, violent and disturbing in its depiction of torture, buyer beware.Reviewed by:  Douglas C. MeeksMember of the Paranormal Romance Guild Review Team

reviewText: "Pawn" by Sophie Davis is the first in a new series and having read and liked her amazing Talented Series I downloaded this book on the day of its release, eager to see what idea she had come up this time.In "Pawn" the protagonist Endora, or "Eel" turns 18 and at her surprise party (nearly?) drowns and gets rescued by the mysterious Kannon. Her feelings towards her attractive saviour however turn ambiguous when he seems to know things about her she has not told him herself. Unsure whether she can trust him she ceases contact with him.In the meantime however she sees or 'meets' him in dreams, all of which seem to have special meaning or a clairvoyant or omniscient character. She finally meets with him and finds out that Kannon and her are not so different and share the same gift or powers.Her exchange with Kannon is romantically charged but also leads her to the investigation of some myths, the nature of which I do not want to reveal here so you can find out yourself without a spoiler.I thoroughly enjoyed this book, it is written in parts for young adults and briefly crosses over into chick lit territory with scenes between Endora's circle of girlfriends but not in a way that would limit Davis' story or audience to that market.The central idea behind the story and probably the rest of series to follow very clever, well thought through and engaging and I found myself drawn into the journey of discovery that Endora and Kannon embark upon more than I would have thought. There are additional interests woven into the plot, like some mystery regarding Endora's father, making this a more dimensional and enjoyable.The writing is tight and smooth and the plot moves along perfectly, never letting me out of its grip. Davis is a talented writer, story teller and entertainer and leaves us with a great set up for the next instalment of this series.Highly recommended.

I am still in awe of Alicia's capacity to love and forgive.  Her forgiveness of Agnes endears me to her and I am happy she is no longer a pushover.There is no question about it; Dennis is the man.  I absolutely LOVE him.  This book continues the love affair that he and Alicia have, it's like you can "see" the love they have for each other as it casts a glow.  He is so protective of Alicia that it makes you giddy.  Dennis' character represents that knight in shining armor that many young girls only dream about.Jay and Jeremy are cut from the same cloth; just evil and only thinking of themselves.  I have my fingers crossed that Jeremy comes into his own and becomes a real man in spite of the lessons from his father.  The fourth book will surely tell.This author continues to be consistent in her storytelling and leaves me wanting more every time.  I wish more people were aware of her work as I believe her work deserves a bigger stage!

You must be careful that you don't become one yourself.I downloaded this book when Ms. Taylor offered it for free on Kindle. I read the entire story, from start to finish, in one day. ONE DAY. It is safe to say that it is a page turner and impossible to put down.Dark, wicked and deeply disturbing at times, I found my self repulsed by the description of the "eye for an eye" moments, yet drawn to them in a sick, demented way. I mean, come on, the book is about revenge, which is my favorite subject! Ms. Taylor has crafted a story so intense that my knuckles are still white from holding my Kindle in a death grip.How many of us wish to seek out and destroy vile monsters that live among us? The ones that, through legal loopholes and fast-talking lawyers, escape the punishment they rightly deserve for their wretched acts on hapless victims. What if one person DID rise up to the challenge, and removed the cancers that lurk in the shadows by becoming judge, jury and executioner? And does one become a monster in their own right while stalking them? Where is the line drawn that separates evil from necessary evil?This book is NOT for the faint at heart. Some of the scenes literally made me cringe inside due to their graphic nature, even when the "prey" was a former "predator" and deserved the swift sword of justice.A thrilling mystery will keep you guessing until the very end and will linger long after you finish the last page.

I don't know what to say other than I was blindsided by this novella by Zoe Dawson. Expecting a feel-good, sweet little Christmas story, Brave left me an emotional mess, crying in my room as I tried to get a grip and come to terms with what I had just read. I haven't done either...and I'm still crying. Brave is not a "Christmas" novel. Rather, it is one about life and love, sacrifice, soul-searing pain and soul-lifting joy, numbing fear and the bravery to face that fear in spite of yourself. The synopsis on this and other sites explains the plot adequately but in no way prepares you for the emotional storm of this magnificent little story. It may be short but it is powerful! Ms Dawson, I got it, I felt it, I lived it through your words. Now, let me wipe my eyes and blow my nose...again...and put the rest of your books on my wishlist.
summary: Be prepared! Have plenty of tissues handy.

Dark fantasy done right. Full of action and adventure, The War of the Moonstone transports readers into a medieval world about to be plunged into war. The Dark Lord has sent an enemy agent to infiltrate the court of the goodly Baron Wesrain. His name is Raugst, and he’s a fascinating character who ends up falling in love with the main character’s true love, the High Priestess Illiana. I normally don’t like love triangles, but this one really worked for me.Our main character, Giorn, goes to war to protect the Moonstone and then gets cut off by the war, unable to return to Niara, while Raugst gains power at home . . . and grows increasingly interested in Niara. Uh-oh! A third of the novel is told from Niara’s point of view, and we get to see the high priestess react and respond to all these various threats, not least of all Raugst. She’s a bold and brave heroine, our light in the growing darkness, and it is her plan that ultimately gives the good guys a chance to win.Giorn is a classic sword and sorcery hero, but this is a gritty novel and when he fights the dark powers they’re actually pretty darned dark. Still, it’s fast and fun and action-packed. But just imagine if J. R. R. Tolkien had shown us what the orcs were “really” up to in their camps and you’ll get the idea. But it makes it all the more meaningful when Giorn chops their heads off!Anyway, I had a great time reading it and can’t wait to read what the author has next.

I have to say that I have just about every book that Evangeline has written from her earliest m/f erotica to her m/m stories (I did write to her mentioning my fantasy of a m/m story with one of them being a Kindred warrior, that would be just HOT). With her Kindred series she has taken her writing talent to an entire new level. First off this book is NOT a stand alone novel. You really must read the first three books in the series to fully appreciate this one.I really wasn't sure at first how the author would be able to handle Xairn's Scourge nature and his extreme need to dominant but I shouldn't have been concerned. There are definitely some very hot and steamy D/s scenes here that are entirely appropriate for this particular book. I think there were definitely a lot more sex scenes than her first three books in this series, but as I said they were needed to address Xairn's growing sexual maturity and inner battle with himself to conquer his extreme Scourge D/s leanings. It seems a lot of authors are starting to put D/s themes in their books and frankly I'm getting rather tired of it but it totally works for this book. (SLIGHT SPOILER) And lets not even mention the primary and secondary shafts. I'm still not sure if that was scary or exciting. Thank God for the Twin Kindred bonding fruit!(END SPOILER)Having said that, the growing love story between Xairn and Lauren was so sweet. I definitely agree with the other five star reviews so far. You do not want to miss this book. It's a definite keeper.(SPOILERS AHEAD READ AT YOUR OWN RISK)I'm also glad Xairn ended up looking like his original Scourge self by the end. I really don't know what was so hot about pale grey skin and red on black eyes but it definitely worked for me! LOL I was a little surprised that Lauren didn't end up pregnant at the end though since the theme of the first three books was all about finding the Chosen One in the Scourge prophecy who would help to replenish the dying Scourge race. At the end of the novel Evangeline does say that she has decided to write two more books in this series though so I am just figuring that means it will happen in one of those books.(END SPOILER)I also have to say that I am so happy that Evangeline has self-published this series. Paying only $2.99 for a full length novel of over 133,000 words is just sweet! As an avid reader who has over 1500 books on her Sony ereader I am really starting to become disgusted with the publishers that are charging the same for an ebook as they do to purchase it in mass market paperback. When this happens I just buy the paperback and when I am done with it I take it to my local used book store and atleast get credit towards another book with the trade-in. As an example, the latest ebook I purchased cost me $5.50 and has only about 35,000 words to it. So thank you so much Evangeline for the self-publishing. I'm hoping eventually more authors that are as well established as you on the ebook front start doing that same thing. And I'm also hoping that by self-publishing the authors are making more money for themselves as well.

(Originally posted on SnarkyMomReads where I received a copy of the story in exchange for the review.)Persuasion Skills (Boardroom Acts) by Laurel Cremant is an 107 page novella priced at $3.99.  At just over 100 pages, it is admittedly a quick read and whereas one would assume that a story in the erotica genre would be smack dab filled with sex, these Boardroom Acts offer much more than bedroom skills - there is a story.  (But don't worry - there IS also some hot sex - oral, light bondage, quick spanking - you're warned!)Jax and Pepper have been long-time friends with one night of benefits.  Both are too frightened of losing their friendship, especially since they are business partners, and so they shy away from their true feelings for each other.  The building of the characters as they figure out how to relate to each other, in AND out of the bedroom, is at times tear producing... but many times is filled with levity.  Pepper is not going to let Jax just roll right over her - she stands up for herself.  Jax asks her to stay with him as if they were a married couple on vacation.  One of my favorite scenes?  When she gets him all hot & bothered, and then announces to him that a real husband would know better than to expect sex from his pissed off wife - as she leaves him to deal with his blue balls by himself.  (And just gotta love her "feminists unite!" fist pumps LOL!!)The best compliment I know to give to the author is to say that this story left me wanting more... and looking forward to the next book in the Boardroom Acts series.

reviewText: Originally posted at: [...]Ex sex is the best sex. Seems like an old adage, but it's true. Or at least it is in the case of Ex Appeal by Cari Quinn.When this title became available, I jumped on it. I only wish I hadn't had to put it aside. I so loved the ride. The descriptions nabbed me from page one. I couldn't put this book down.Ms. Quinn writes hot, no doubt, but this story takes the cake and adds crayons. Yeah, I loved the art angle and the creative use of edible crayons. The love scenes darned near melted my screen, but I wouldn't have it any other way.Although I couldn't completely get a bead on what Ty and Jen looked like, it wasn't an issue. The chemistry between them was so powerful, I found myself rooting for them even when I wasn't sure why they split. If I had any issues, it was the lack of communication between them, but, and this is the key, their failure to talk is realistic. It was like watching two of my friends who I know should be together, butting heads because they can't see the obvious -- they love each other. It worked perfectly.I'm referring this story to all my friends. It's hot, sticky, and a breeze to read. If you want a story that will stay with you, and characters you won't forget, then you need to read Ex Appeal. I give it 4.5 cherries.

I've read a few rockstar romances now, and I do enjoy them, but sometimes they can be a little too similar for my tastes.  It's nice to have something familiar, but I think some of the best stories take a different sort of twist with the things that we're all familiar with, you know?Marooned with the Rock Star is definitely like that!  This is a playful and fun story with a really different take on the rockstar hero.  I loved the sort of realism behind Kurt and his band endeavours.  And... I mean, by realism, I mean it just made sense.  His backstory was a little silly at times, but in a good way.  I think these kinds of things could probably happen to anyone, which is a lot of fun.This is going to sound a little weird, but it kind of reminded me of some of the parts from Fifty Shades in that way.  If you've read those books, you'll probably know what I mean.  Like... it's "serious" but there are some flirty fun parts that are amusing and more playful than anything.  This book is like that, but then with a rockstar, a cute and curvy girl, and a cruise ship.I liked the idea of the cruise ship stuff, too.  I haven't read many cruise ship books, and I've never been on a cruise, so I kind of enjoy reading about people being on them.  It's interesting and neat.  Sort of off topic there, but I just like the cruise ship stuff!The chemistry between Rebecca and Kurt is great, too!  Right from the start, there's some crazy action going on between them (not sexual right away, but pretty crazy), and the whole thing just spirals into something amazing from there.  I loved the romantic comedy aspects of this story a lot and I think Dawn Steele did a great job of portraying some realistic, yet entertaining and funny characters.If you're into rockstar romances and you want to try something a little similar, but different in all the right ways, I'd definitely suggest giving this book a shot.  I can pretty much guarantee you won't be disappointed!

3.75 StarsThe title of this book couldn't have been any better. It fits perfectly, and sooo not what you are expecting. This is the first book I've read by Ms. Makela, and I have to say...WOW! Wow factor #1!Skin Deep has amazing originality, which is such a nice breath of fresh air. Wow Factor #2!The book started off with a bang, jumping right into the action and keeping you wanting to know more. "Your time is running out. While our preference is for you to find a true mate, I'm not above assigning someone." Wow factor #3!I liked the characters, though I would have liked to have seen Angelique, the main character, be a bit stronger in her role. For someone that knows her supernatural ability, she seemed very weak. Almost the damsel in distress role, which I didn't care for much.Connor, on the other hand, strong and hot, Hot, HOT! Heh hmm...He can have my back, anytime. Oh, get your minds out of the gutter!Monica...someone please give me some duct tape!There were times when I thought the book went to fast, and this caused the story not to flow super well for me. I would have liked to have had more tension built up, to really feel what the characters were feeling. This especially goes for the steamy sex scenes. Yes, they were steamy, but I think the sexual tension could have been played up a bit more. I also would have liked a bit more backstory too, to have a better understanding of the whole idea behind the story. This is a very short read though, having read it in just a couple of hours, and is only Book One.Final Thought: As a first time author for me, Sarah Makela has my vote. I loved the whole premise behind this story, the uniqueness of the plot & characters, and the quickness of the read as I don't get much time for reading anymore. I will definitely be reading Book Two. I would also highly recommend Skin Deep to anyone that loves a good, fast paced, paranormal read. Only because I wished for a tad more, (tension and backstory) is it getting only 3.75 Wolf Moons. immortylcafe.com

I've never read anything by Suzanne Lilly before this story, but after enjoying Untellable, I'm planning on rectifying that mistake. She's written a truly amazing story, populated by real characters I truly cared about.Untellable is part of a series set in Honey Creek.  The series appears to be written by many different authors, but I'm so intrigued by, and in love with all the characters, I'm sorely tempted to pick them all up.  If they're half as good as this book, I'll enjoy every word.Aspen is our heroine, a former foster child on her own and hiding out from her father (who is not a nice man).  While he's in jail at the start of this story, it's clear it won't be that way forever.  She's determined to make a new start in a tiny, nowhere town and equally determined to keep from letting anyone close to her again.  But, in Honey Creek, that's not an easy thing to do.  Like any small town, everyone is in everyone else's business!Colton is a hunky fireman who likes Aspen from the moment he meets her.  He's fun, caring and doesn't take no for an answer.  While he's certainly not perfect, he is a perfect hero for Aspen.The plot is mainly about Aspen coming out her shell and finding herself (and the courage to stand up to the man she fears).  She grows as a person, and she learns that it might be scary to fall in love, but it's not always dangerous to do so.The story had me smiling all the way through.  It's sweet, touching, a bit scary and nerve-wracking and ultimately satisfying.  The romance is sweet, and this is a book that could be read and enjoyed by readers from the mid-teens on up.

The Siren is one of my favourite books of the year so it's no surprise that I've been devouring everything else I can find that was written by Tiffany Reisz. She has fast become an automatic buy author and I can't imagine that changing any time soon. The more we learn about the cast of characters in the Original Sinners series the more I love them and the more I want to see of them. It's funny because Tiffany manages to pull me completely out of my comfort zone but she does it in such a gently teasing way that I hardly notice I've left safety until I take a breath and pause for a second. Even then I'm actually surprised to find that something that should shock and horrify me is actually turning me on! Not many authors have the skill to do that but Tiffany does it consistently and with such unbelievable skill.I have been dying to learn more about Kingsley since I first met him in The Siren and oh boy was he worth the wait! Known as the King of Kink Kingsley is a dominant who knows exactly what he wants and how to get it. He makes no apologies for his desires and I'm pretty sure he could convince anyone to do anything with his sexy accent, whip smart sense of humour and gorgeous body. Despite being dominant Kingsley doesn't scare the crap out of me (unlike a certain character from The Siren who I'm not going to mention here!), he is arrogant, domineering and sexy as hell and I'd happily submit to him any day of the week!Charlie is new to the D/s lifestyle, she has always felt something was missing in her previous relationships and has always found the nice guys that she has dated somewhat boring so when Kingsley offers to spend a month training her to become a submissive it's an offer she can't refuse (who could?). I really enjoyed seeing how Kingsley introduced her to BDSM, he takes his time building up her confidence and slowly pushes her limits further every day. It was fascinating following her journey and watching her blossom as she let her deepest desires come to the surface.Submit to Desire may only be a novella but the smut levels are off the charts. One particular scene involving a blindfold and a selection of random household objects, well lets just say I was in need of a cold shower after reading it! My only complaint about the story is that it ended, I could have happily spent days reading about Kingsley and Charlotte. I'm now a complete Kingsley addict and in desperate need of my next fix - in fact I think I'll have to go and read this novella again while I wait for Tiffany's next release! If you haven't already discovered this author's writing then you're missing out on a treat, I'd recommend starting with The Siren but I'm sure you'll soon be moving on to the novellas while you wait for The Angel to release (don't forget to check out the free short stories that are available on Tiffany's website).
