reviewText: After the insanity and angst of the last book, this latest volume returns to the area of the story I find most interesting, and that is the "world building" being done by Bruce and Co. This book ticks all my boxes, blending enough big picture and home life into the story to make the whole effort work.  Bruce's ongoing efforts to collect all the toys in the country really comes to fruition here.  That what he is doing could have been done by the Powers That Be if only they had the guts at the onset is not a point to be overlooked, either.  Great book, great series and I can't wait for the next one.

Little do they know, keeping up and maintaining the relationship is the hardest part and it is a never-ending stage.  It will only end if one lets go.  This book offers a lot of advice on how to make a relationship last.  One of the things highlighted is communication.  The lack of communication will eventually lead to the downfall of a relationship.  I can go on babbling but I suggest you grab a copy of this book.  Very interesting and awesome read.

Just what is happening to them? When they find out the answer, will they be able to accept that what they have will last forever?This fast paced tale of vampire true mates stimulates the senses with frequent hot and steamy sex scenes that include light bondage and anal sex scenes.  The author brings this sensual story to live with vibrant images, details and strong compelling characters that capture the imagination.  The emotions and passions of the characters are conveyed with an intensity that ensures the reader gets caught up in the blossoming relationship between Sabrina and Kyle.  The Las Vegas setting adds just the right amount of glamour and sparkle to this story and the fact that even the vampire wasn’t sure what was happening between the two of them adds a touch of sweet innocence to this very pleasurable and enjoyable short read.I am looking forward to reading the next book to find out how Sabrina and Kyle’s romance is coming along.

Jenna has been friends with Andy and Ryan for over five years.  She watched as Andy rose to local fame in the regional kite surfing contests, even qualifying time and time again at the national level.  Five years ago it seemed they were on the verge of taking their friendship one step further, but the opportunity passed and each of them went on their ways.  Now Jenna is a manager at a watersport company with both Ryan and Andy as employees.  She's never quite lost the intense desire she feels for Andy, and she's struggling to keep things professional between them.  Andy has become a cocky playboy with a stream of conquests.  He pushes Jenna's every button.  He's a no-show for clients, has sex with co-workers during work hours on company property.  Still, Jenna remembers a different Andy, one from five years ago, and longs to bring him back.We've all wanted to tame the player sometime or another in our lives, to be the one that curbs his cheatin ways.  Andy is so darned hot, so irresistible, so naughty in his little-boy way that, personally, I'd be tempted to ignore all the red flags and jump that thang.  Plus there is that whole forbidden manager/employee angle.  Should Jenna go for it? Will she ever notice that her friend Ryan is more than half in love with her? What about the mysterious guy on the motorcycle?  Jenna has been nose to the grindstone at work for too long, and it's clear from page one she needs a relationship.  Not just sex, but a relationship.  But can Andy ever give that to her, given his bed-hopping?The imagery of Green Island and the Great Barrier Reef in Australia really set the scene for this erotic story.  I could feel the heat, the sand and the surf.  It made me long to grab my passport and hop on a plane.  The sex scenes are smoking hot, graphic, with enough slang to make them modern and edgy.  I read the whole book with the author's Aussie accent running through my head, which probably added considerably to the appeal.  If you're in the mood for a gorgeous kite surfer in paradise, this is the book for you.  Voyeurism, self-pleasure, and intercourse, with lots of build-up and tension.

I consider myself a fan suspense novels, and I have high standards after reading so many.I figured this book would be a great way to pass a free afternoon I had. Read it start to finish!What sells this book is the unusual character backstory. Like other reviewers mentioned, it's refreshing to get a survivor suspense story from an unlikely source.When I saw that he was a marine, I was trepidatious. I was afraid I wouldn't really understand any of the references, and that I'd spend most of my time skipping forward through those parts.To my surprise, everything was explained or just simply made sense. It never felt overly technical, and I assure you that I've not had any experience in the military.The story flowed well, descriptions never outstayed their welcome, and the action was on point.Regarding the pacing of the ending, I do see where people might feel that it's rushed. I felt like it was intentional. Once the tides turn and things get dire in the story, it progresses at a rate that seems realistic to real world standards.The ending was well-written and packed a punch. It wasn't a happy ending, but it doesn't have to be in order to be good.

The Ian Fleming Files: Operation Armada (Book 1 of The Ian Fleming Files)I was offered an ARC (advanced reader copy) in return for an accurate review. Without a doubt... a MUST for any Bond fan! The Ian Fleming Files: Operation Armada by Damian Stevenson is fantastic. The book has intelligent detail to history and complete with fun characters throughout. Naval intelligence, Commander Fleming, 1940 and World War 2... what more could you ask for?A very imaginative, absorbing novel. The first `Ian Fleming Files' adventure `Operation Armada' was a great start to the series but with `Parsifal' we get a richer, deeper, more substantial work. The plot kicks in fast and it's a great hook. Along the way there is some delightful character work that further enhances our knowledge of the main character and all the supporting players. I especially like the scenes with his family, his mother and brothers, when he is unable to divulge to them what he does during the war (They think he's a `pen-pusher'). There is a memorable new villain with a mouth full of diamonds and plenty of oddball henchmen with exotic weaponry. Fleming flies a plane, rides a camel, journeys in a submarine, steals a ride on the Trans Siberian Express, shoots a crossbow and even has time to contemplate fatherhood during a night swim to a Nazi stronghold. The Kindle clicks go fast with this one. You won't stop reading till you get to the end. Can't wait for 'Operation Uncle Sam!'

This is the story of Emma, a young woman of 30-ish, who suffers from bi-polar disorder but who manages it with medication.  She is set up with a date by her flatmate and the two of them don't get on.  The evening (or early next morning) ends with a brutal but mutual sex act which results in her pregnancy.  To save the baby from harm, Emma has to give up her lithium which keeps the disorder at bay.  Emma and Simon get together again in an off and on way and I really found I wanted to know what happened.To me, the clever part of this story is that it is a first person narration by Emma and we see her bipolar disorder begin to creep up on her.  Because she is telling us about it, we can see her rationale for her over-excited, hysterical behaviour, all the reasoning behind her fear and despair.  We know where things are heading before she does.  If this were described in the third person we'd only see the results, not the reasoning.  This aspect is extremely well done.  I also found some of the writing very funny - even in desperate situations, Rosen Trevithick can pull a funny out and I found myself highlighting a phrase or two that made me giggle.There's an exciting and ultimately satisfying ending to this story.  Very enjoyable.

reviewText: Whilst running from her abusive ex-husband Paisley has one thought and one thought only, get as far away as possible, start a new life and pray the disgusting piece of human parasite that is her ex never finds her again.But whilst running she ends up facing more than one complication. The first is being temporarily unable to keep moving and secondly there is the very attractive I can tempt you with my eyes into doing anything I want Sterling who is dead set on making sure she gets all the help he can offer .The catch? Sterling is a Psychiatrist and knows just what to say and do with woman in Paisley's situation. But Paisley has sworn no man will ever have power over her again and she does her utmost best to block out any and all physical and mental help Sterling tries to give her, that is until her ex shows up with guns blazing!I truly enjoyed this read, there was the right amount of gripping suspense and angst to keep me turning the pages. And the right balance of fear turning to romance and protectiveness to make my heart melt.The character of Paisley was very interesting, the author let me into the mind of an abused woman and the various decisions she makes. Some yes were very " What was she thinking?" and others where " That's it woman fight!"With the what was she thinking moments the author got me thinking about just why some woman stick around with men who so badly abuse them, and I realized that for us on the outside it would make no sense at all, but for the women who have to suffer these despicable acts of violence there is always something holding them back, fear, lack of love and trust, something from the past no matter there is something.And thus instead of judging we need to try and remember there is a deeper meaning in their actions. Through this character the author truly showed me that abused woman have their own set of issues and for some it's just never that easy to walk away.The character of Sterling was one that certainly made me sit upright and take double notice. He has his own set of issues and much like most Psychiatrists they never think another in their line of work can fix them, but his issues that keeps him from living a normal sexy rich playboy lifestyle had me stop and think for a almost a full minute before realizing it could totally happen and be very real and true, and thus does not make his actions or lack there of too surprising as I am sure it will be for some readers.  Everyone has an issue they hold onto until a situation either forces them to deal with it head on or someone points out that they need to follow their own advise.The backdrop settings were well described, characters were well developed and the author really dug deep with her characters letting me in on every thought and thus I could fully connect with them and really zero in on their emotions.I am taking away a message of fear holds most of us back from taking a chance. Yes the same might happen again but chances are it won't and if you simply let the chance slip simply because of your fear you will never know if you let your one and only chance at happiness go.I highly recommend this read for fans of twists and turns real life situations romance reads. Paisley was a true heroine when it counted and Sterling a real life make my knees go weak hero! Passionate andheart-stoppingly emotional and oh so sexy!Keep them coming Robyn!5/5 Star Review" He's her knight in shining armor but she's the one about to rescue him""Copy provided in exchange for a honest review

This is a fine book for a very specific crowd.If you're a sci-fi techno-junkie, hooked on jargon and technical talk, and you love action, you'll have a terrific time here.  I'm not, and STILL enjoyed reading it.I gave it three points for general audiences...but add a point if you love reading futuristic writing about technical military action.  Even more if you want to promote indie Kindle publications."Information Cloud: Tales of Cinnamon City" is a fast-paced book that shoots from one narrative line to the next in an almost seamless fashion, never dwelling too heavily upon one thread long enough to dominate.  In each short and very readable chapter West manages to build interest up to a level of interest that demands satisfaction--only to delay that satisfaction by switching to the next account.  Yet, since the narration is moving along quite speedily, the constant change does not seem unsettling...in fact, it seems as seamless as, say, watching a house be built by looking at the carpenter, then the plumber, then the electrician, etc.  It's hard not to want to go on.Why did I not give the book a four, or a five?  Because, as rich as the action was, I never knew much about why the incidents in the book were happening, nor was I given any real reason to root for one side verses the other.  For instance, where is Cinnamon City?  Is it even on Earth?  Who where the security forces, and who are the Kamari? And who are these all powerful Lords to whom only a couple of pages are devoted?True, some insight is given to these questions in the Glossary, but--call me old-fashioned--the book needs to tell us these things, not just some pages added at the end (which require a lot of shuffling around on the Kindle, anyway).  Besides, many questions are still not answered, such as when this is taking place?  What is happening in the world around them?  Is there an America, or ANY country?Additionally, there are things that show up in the Glossary that seem to have nothing to do with the book at large, though they might have been interesting had they been included.  For instance, why is "Ice Cricket" created for the Glossary only?  It doesn't occur within the novel.  And until I read the Glossary I was not even aware that Cinnamon City was domed.  That seems a pretty vital point to leave until the Glossary.Additionally, there is not much character building.  A daughter, for instance, who has a lot to do with two central characters and is the motivation for a good deal of their actions late in the book, is not introduced with any description until halfway through the novel.  And the death of a major character's father is handled much the same way...because only a couple of passing remarks are made of his existence his death toward the end of the book has no real weight.A lot of this might not really matter to those who want their books action packed, fast paced, and full of technological innovations.  And it is here that "Information Cloud" actually shines...the mechanizations used by these futuristic armies are intricate, well-described, and most of all exciting.  As each new weapon is wheeled out there remains little doubt about what drives the author: West LOVES his technology, and has thoroughly mapped out the specifications, syntax, and even their shortcomings.  Forget exposition and characterization: these weapons are the real "characters" here.So, again, add a point to my three-star rating if action and weaponry are what you want.  If you like world-building, stick to Mieville, Bacigalupa, and others.  If you like world-DESTRUCTION, however, where each new weapon is better than the last, and each device flies, monitors, kills, maims or explodes a whole lot better than the last, then "Information Cloud" is for you.Peter James West has carved out a niche for himself, and it should please those who are devotees of this genre--for I'm assuming a techno-junkie market is out there.And, what's more, there is good news for those who belong: it's made clear that other books will follow.

This is a solid book on the interesting practice of "hot" yoga. The emphasis in this book is NOT on "positions." The focus is on describing the practice of hot yoga and motivating us to try it out. Hot yoga refers to the temperature of the room. In many traditional cultures, hot rooms (think sweat lodges) are part of a mystic tradition, and the author points out that hot yoga is also considered Power Yoga!The benefits to hot yoga are much like any form of yoga -- a calming meditative state, improved blood circulation, mood, muscle tone, etc. -- but hot yoga goes further. The heat opens pores, loosens muscles, helps improve tissue elasticity, opens airways, and more.In the practice sections of the book, the author is crystal clear about what to do and not do, emphasizing caution with medical conditions. He describes how to set up a home studio or how to select a class and compatible teacher. The entire "practice" section of the book feels like Rosenstein is taking you by the hand and walking you through the process as a friend. He explains that this is YOUR practice, and you must set up a situation and awareness that allows you to incorporate hot yoga into your life successfully.Although the language seems a bit formal, the explanations are thorough and friendly. The author is clearly an expert, and I found that reading this quick book was like talking to a "hot yoga" guru. My advice: If you are thinking about doing hot yoga, this is a must-read before you begin, and if you've already taken the plunge, you'll get great ideas from the history and expert viewpoint.

Open Minds has a dystopian feel to it. Kira lives in Chicago in a world very different from ours. Because of a mutation linked to chemicals in the water supply, people have developed the ability to communicate telepathically. The skill kicks in roughly with the onset of puberty, and the rare child who fails to develop it is destined for life as a zero, the bottom of society. Kira is one such child. By age 16, she still hasn't changed to a reader. She's become something far worse.Kira is a mindjacker. She can control other people's minds.Kira's confusion, anger, and fear draw us into her story. We learn about her new skill as she does. Fortunately, she has Simon, a classmate and fellow jacker who guides her development. Unfortunately, Simon carries an undercurrent of danger, a hint of the underworld. Kira can't tell her family about her new abilities for fear of their safety. Neither does she tell Raf, her best friend, and their relationship fills with lies.Then Kira learns there are far greater dangers when one is a jacker. And in a world that reads minds, a secret is a very difficult thing to keep.Open Minds is the only book in this set I have read, but if the others are anywhere in the ballpark, readers are in for a treat.

Although this is the first book in Truscott's The Perpetual Campaign series, it is the second that I've read. I'd wondered about the meaning of the series name and now think I get it. The primary characters, Clarissa Rogers and Carter Jennings, are political operatives who are constantly (perpetually) working to elect or reelect a candidate, jumping from one campaign to another.What makes this installment different from A Referendum on Conscience (second in the series, but the first I read) is that the candidate in this book, Alex Hogan, is much less deserving of their expertise. This makes for an interesting dynamic, as Clarissa and Carter's loyalty is more to Winston, a mentor who has hired them for this campaign, than to the candidate. The contrast between the two characters (Carter is an archetypal gun-for-hire while Clarissa is more of an idealist who would rather believe in her candidate) fueled contemplation on the good and bad in our political process. Hogan's opponent in the general election, the ultraconservative incumbent, Tara Gunderson Hansen, who it seems to me was not based on, but certainly inspired by, a specific Congresswoman from Minnesota, set up a classic lesser-of-two-evils race.Truscott's characters, the idealistic Clarissa and even Carter Jennings, warts and all, are likeable and the kind of people that a reader can pull for, which bodes well for the series. Political thriller lovers will find this book, and I suspect the entire series, excellent reads. I sure have so far.**Originally written for "Books and Pals" book blog. May have received a free review copy. **

This was a quite satisfactory tale  with a beginning and an end.  This snapshot could be fitted with the other parts without any sense of discontinuity.  On the other hand, it does not commit us to any fixed future.

***The review contains spoilers****The writing style left a lot to be desired.  At times I was confused as to what she was reading, what was real life, or what was in a book.However, the story itself was so unique that confusing writing aside, I could not stop reading.Who of us hasn't dreamed of being our favorite heroine in an erotic story?  How many times have we fantasized about being spanked by Christian Grey or another character just like him?  For Holly, her life had taken a dramatic turn for the worse on the brink of her 10 year high school reunion.  Getting drunk, while depressed, in a room with a bunch of people you haven't seen in ten years is never a good idea and Holly ends up with the goth/witch turned lawyer in her basement invoking some dream spirit.  Instead of invoking some general feelings of goodness, the crazy spell makes her kindle a magic portal into her favorite stories.  Suddenly, she's thrust into the bodies of her favorite characters and living out all of our book boyfriend fantasies.But then something goes horribly wrong as one particular damaged hero figures out a way to enter the real world.  Suddenly, Holly's friend is trapped in the kindle and the dominant, insane hero is running around in his body.Definitely a unique twist on why too many fantasies can be bad for you.  If you can get past the writing style, this is a book that will engross you to the very end.

Great perils have this beauty, that they bring to light the fraternity of strangers. - Victor Hugoafter spending a day at the Belgian seaside, Louise and her younger sister Jennifer head for their remote holiday cottage to spend the summer together. as soon as they arrive, they  each encounter their worst nightmares.the characters' personalities are clearly defined. the differences between the siblings either mask or highlight their similarities and mutual dependency. the strangers' identities and their origins are shrouded in mystery. even the motive for their actions leave much room for the reader to speculate on.the pacing is really fast and the events are deftly sequenced that i finished the 24-page story in 15 minutes or so. instead of reading, it felt like i was watching a short film too.the locale also brings to mind a training camp up in the mountains where i often used to go. it is only a ten-minute drive from civilization but out there, you suddenly feel so isolated. the whole area is surrounded by verdant forest. an empty parking lot is all that remains when the last group of day shift employees leave for home. when dusk falls, the whole camp is transformed. as if on cue, your ears are filled with the discordant symphony generated by unseen nocturnal creatures trying to outdo one another. light posts automatically switch on but between these sentinels lie deep pools of darkness. the cemented pathways leading to the sleeping quarters are bathed in shadows as well. now i wonder how i would regard the place should i get the chance to participate in another training.Vanessa Morgan has certainly written a fast-paced-bad-things-do-happen-to-good-people story. i have to admit that reading The Strangers Outside creeped me out and my imagination went into overdrive. i literally locked the doors, latched the windows, read with all the lights on and made sure that i sat with my back to the wall.i have no fear of the dark or even strangers but now i am reconsidering...
summary: bad things do happen to good people

Little did she know that the hottie who saved her after the accident is the number one Demon to beat.I like the story, I think it's a pretty fun and exciting background for the relationship between Izzy & Shade, it fits them perfectly. Even though they feel an instant connection, their relationship still takes a little time to flourish, Izzy has trust issues and what for what happened in her past, I don't blame her. And Shade, has a shady past (lol pun intended), so he thinks he's undeserving and doesn't want to scare her away by moving too fast or by making any wrong moves.Izzy is too funny and a perfect combination of sweet & sassy, while Shade is a totally delicious demon with a sweet and caring side. They are absolutely perfect for each other. And after the tournament Izzy comes face to face with her troubled past, and I have to say, I was 100% gratified with how she reacted. If I could have given her a high five, I would have lol.It's a must read!P.S. I'm hoping that Charles Latham gets a story of his own; I'd like to see who can handle the God, lol.

reviewText: This follow up to Frat Boy and Toppy really worked for me. This takes place during the events in Sweet Young Thang (although you don't have to read that one first) but it is all about Brad and Sebastian. Surprisingly, there was more of a serious tone to this one, likely since the other TAG boys are not around to offer their unique wisdom and guidance.While there was a hint of the D/s aspects of their relationship in Frat Boy, especially Brad's submissive nature, it is really explored here. What really worked for me was Brad and Sebastian actually having a conversation about what they want and need from each other. Brad feels something has been missing while Sebastian has been occupied with his thesis, and after Sebastian has a hissy over Collin staying the night after the frat house fire, he finally lays it all out. What results is not only a beautiful, honest discussion, but some amazingly hot sex. I really got the feeling from them that this was just who they are and what they need rather than two guys playing a D/s game.I really enjoyed watching them take the relationship to the next level and would happily read more.
summary: Nice follow up with Brad and Sebastian.

reviewText: What a meaty read!  The tone is scholarly and in-depth, so if you're tired of reading books about marketing and advertising that only scrape the surface, you've found your book.  What I found most surprising about this book, given the title, is that it focuses on psychology and the workings of the human brain, and how that affects the success or failure of advertising.  A lot of it is frankly over my head; but it's clear that Dr. Benton is an undisputed expert on this topic.My own book,The Entrepreneur's Guide to Sleaze-Free Selling: The 3-Step Sales Formula For Growing Your Business ... Without Being Pushy, Obnoxious or Rudewould make a nice accompaniment, after you've read this one.  It allows you to incorporate all of Dr. benton's science of advertising into your sales process, and do it in a heart-centered, authentic manner that feels good to both you and your customers.

reviewText: I previously reviewed Eddie de Jong's book "Goal Setting for Success (Personal Development for Beginners.. .."  Not to sound redundant but this book is also written in a friendly, concise manner that allows the reader to quickly learn and utilize the basics of good time management.  This is a great book that, in my professional opinion, would be an asset to even junior high and high school students.As a counselor/therapist, I believe this book would be very helpful in conjunction with the book noted above.  And although this book is listed in the title as #2, I have had many clients over the years that "never found the time" to work on "setting goals".  So for these individuals I would have them read Time Management for a Productive Life first to allow them to set up a time strategy and "lose the excuse" of not having time to establish do-able goals.  I really like that his books are short and to the point-- yet told with a well thought-out flow illustrated with many good examples.  I hope to read more of his books in the very near future.
summary: Time Management a book all should read.

When I finished K. M. Jackson's first book, Through the Lens, I was tickled to start Seduction's Canvas and find a fun little authorial trick had been played, which I discovered when introduced to heroine Samara Leghton. (Nicely played, Ms. Jackson).Samara is the rebellious daughter of a NYC real estate mogul and hard-nosed businessman. But being rich does not spare her from heartbreak and all she wants to do is mourn her brother and pursue her art. She's no stranger to the gossp rags, and papparazzi, and even throwing herself into her painting and planning her first show can't insulate her. Her family, including a matchmaking minded mother, and an erstwhile suitor who seems more intererested in the connections a relationship with Sam can reap for him, couple to leave her frustrated and wondering if romance is even possible. But then her history with bad boys is rekindled when she meets motorcycle man Mark Thorn. And surprise, surprise. He's moved in across the hall. The attraction is instantaneous and smoldering. And no matter how hard Sam tries to keep him at arm's length, Thorn is determined to prove to her he can be the man of her dreams. But her family - and a secret from his past that Thorn is keeping from her that connects them both - will not hear of it. When lust overflows, all bets are off and the chips are going to fall where they may.Jackson's new story is a bit darker than Lens, but no less marvelous a literary feast. I am again in awe of her ability to create such a rich, complex and satisfying tale in a shorter format. The backdrop of New York City is wonderfully rendered, and creates a great picture of a rich girl's Manhattan. As a native, I loved every bit of detail about the city. The wealth of detail about painting, and art was marvelous and a great addition to the immediacy of the story. The secondary characters are varied and interesting, and her parents nicely nuanced. Sam's three selves - as pointed out by Mark, combine to create a complicated woman fighting not just her own desires, but the expectations of parents, and society, and men. Mark Thorn is a tough, rough man with a wide streak of gentleman running through him. Together a combustible cast.And the love story itself is hot, tormented, and the characters tortured by their own desires and the conflicts, both internal and external, that make their relationship such a thorny one. As a reader I was thoroughly invested in this romantic story, and while it is a romance so you know you're guaranteed a happy ending, Jackson kept me on the edge of my seat as I followed this couple through their twisting, heart-wrenching tale. But of course, that level of tension makes the sweet denouement all the sweeter.
summary: A story overflowing with heart and passion.

That these authors' voices are different from Hugh's is fine, given that we're hearing from other characters. Rather than cheapen "the real Wool story", they add to it beautifully.As for those reviewers who are blasting this story for its "political agenda" - shame on you. I see no "agenda" here, only the desire to tell the story of two fascinating characters who find themselves face-to-face with a dark reality. In that, Mr. Davies succeeds remarkably. I recommend this story highly, and am now off to find other works by this author.

I am not a huge fan of the romance genre but I gave this book a chance because it caught my eye as something different.And it is different than other romances I've read. I give the author a lot of credit for trying this approach, too. The title of the book is appropriate, because it's written in a stylized format that provides mostly Glimpses: each section is roughly one page long, no paragaph is more than two sentences, and the sections alternate between the present and the past. This must have been a huge challenge for the author to tackle, because it involves a lot of structural detail that must have taken forever to sort through. And it raises the question: by providing a million glimpses, are we able to get a good view of the whole?For the most part, yes. I found the characters down to earth and believable, which is important to me. I liked them, they didn't seem fake, and that's not something I always get from a romance. Their lives were not glamorous at all: he was a blue collar worker, she is a teacher. They both have issues. They don't always say pretty things. These people live lives I can relate to. That's interesting to me. I was really pulling for Harleigh and her boyfriend Shaun to be able to work things out. These are good things.The problem is, because of the way the book is structured, it becomes a bit repetitive in spots. Further, although I like the situation and the dialogue sounds genuine, because of the paragraph limitations, given the haiku like format, I honestly had no idea what these characters look like. It's more like reading a book in radio rather than video. I can't see them in my mind, because we are never offered that much detail, and I guess I'd like to know more. For example, I want more description about Shaun other than that he wears socks that have holes in them. What does he look like? What features about him does Harleigh find attractive? Also, we read about numerous short situations, but because each section is confined to a page, everything that happens is given equal weight and nothing can stand out more than anything else, especially because the structure dictates we'll be going back to the past in the next section.That said, this is a quick, pleasant read, and the structure allows you to move along at a fast pace. I'm glad I caught a glimpse of Glimpses and I look forward to reading more from Erin J. Munz in the future.

reviewText: When I heard that Shay Savage was writing a follow-up to Surviving Raine, I could not tell you how happy I was! I LOVED that story! Needless to say, I had high expectations when I started Bastian's Storm and this story did not disappoint.Raine and Bastian have been rescued from the Island, but their problems are far from over. Bastian struggles desperately to be the man that Raine deserves. It's a daily battle to not drink and keep from beating the hell out of people. He wants to go back to the Island where life was simpler. His demons are dark and plentiful and Raine has so much love, patient and understanding for him. They are truly in love.When enemies from Bastian's past threatens not only Raine, but someone else that he loves, he is willing to do anything to keep them safe. Even if that includes going back into a death match. But this time.....he may have met his match in Evan Arden.How far is Bastian really willing to go to survive and keep those he loves safe? Who can he really trust when it comes to the game of death?I love how Shay writes the male POV. She does such a great job getting into their heads and making us really believe everything they are thinking and feeling. To be honest I have never read the Evan Arden series, so I did not have a lot to go on when it came to Evan. I was totally on team Bastian! With that said.....and knowing how this story ends, I really want to go read that series now. Evan Arden seems like a very interesting character!This was a story filled with love and suspense <-------- I heart that combination. I really liked that there was never really a conflict between Raine and Bastian. Their love for each other was never in question. That was not needed to keep this story moving. The drama just came from Bastian himself. Trying to figure out what was most important for him, trying to figure out how to deal with his past so he can move on to his future with Raine by his side. Was he able to do that? Was he able to defeat Evan Arden in the death games? Read Bastian's Storm to find out!
summary: Bastian or Evan.....Who's team are you on?

I Know Lucy is a fascinating tale of a teenaged girl thrust into the most horrible of circumstances. Forced into a life of crime in order to survive, Lucy is a strong, resilient, and yet fragile young woman struggling to find a life for herself.I enjoyed the way the author switched up the POVs in this book, first person for Zach and third for Lucy. It worked really well, since Lucy's part of the story are all remembrances of the past while Zach's are present day.Lucy is a wonderfully real character, she seems to leap right off the page. reviewText: This book was unusual for me as my opinion kept changing. One minute I was loving it, the next I wasn't so sure. In summary, I did enjoy the story and it's laugh-out-loud moments but a little more loving would have raised it just a notch.The strengths of the book were the wonderful range of characters - most hugely over the top, especially Cameron's mother - and the humour throughout the story. This is one of those books with some great one-liners. I also adored Cameron's 'stories' about his family.This is the story of two men who are looking for something more in their lives. Henry is an ex-porn star whose reputation seems to follow him everywhere. He is sick of being known for his huge 'endowment' and wants to find a special person to love him for himself. He is a successful business man and philanthropist.Cameron has tried to be independent and make a life away from his crazy family. He didn't want to dependent on their money or connections but at twenty-nine, finds himself in a position where he is wondering where his life is going.An unfortunate first meeting, where Henry insults Cameron based on a misunderstanding of what he thinks of Cameron, results in Cameron disliking Henry. But fate (and their friends) has a way of bring them together. As they keep running into each other, they are attracted and eventually realise they have both may have made a mistake in their first impression of each other.Throw in some fabulous and strange friends, wacky drag-queen uncles, Cameron's outrageous mother ("Her son wasn't the marrying type") and a bratty teenager and there is lots of fun.So where did it not come together for me? I think it was the romance angle. I wanted to see Henry and Cameron spend more time together and it just didn't happen. Because they weren't together, I also failed to see how their love developed. I guess I just wanted more love.
summary: A fun story but I wanted a bit more romance

reviewText: I am so happy I stumbled across this book. I first read the synopsis & my curiousity was peeked from there. 'Only Way Out' is a fast paced book. It tells the story of a young female (Latesha aka Tesh) wanting to be loved. Being that she has low self- esteem, when she meets Trey she's sure he's the one; or is he? Trey wines and dines her, & helps to rebuild her self-esteem quickly. Tesh soons learns what Trey's true motives are toward her. Tesh comes up with a master plan to bring him down & he'll never see it coming. Only Way out is the very first book I've read by the authors Fire and Ice, but best believe it won't be the last. The book kept my attention from the first to the last page. My only disappoinment was that it ended way too soon. If you love drama, more drama, dopeboys & murder, THIS is most definitely a novel you'll enjoy reading. Although it was a very fast read/short story I can't deny the fact that 'Only Way Out' was 5 stars for sure. I'm really looking forward to part 2 & hope the wait won't be long. I'll be on the look-out for more novels from these authors. Loved it!

When I first saw Rachel post the link on Twitter to go sign up to be a part of the blog tour for her debut novel, I knew I had to sign up. And can I just say how incredibly glad I am that I did?!!? I really liked this book. We have a great cast of characters, a well developed plot, and good pacing. Rachel had a good blend of humor, angst, and definitely some elements of surprise.I knew I would love Savannah (Sav) right from the start. She's sassy, feisty, and confident. However, she has also built steel-enforced walls around her heart after losing her parents at a young age and also after being blamed for the suicide of her first love (who happened to break her heart). She has found a way to escape the pain by losing herself in men and indulging in drinking and partying. Her dad's best friend and surrogate father, Mr. Davenport, has offered her a job in L.A. hoping she will change her wild ways and get a fresh beginning. Sav meets Tate Connors almost immediately upon arrival to her new apartment complex. She is instantly attracted to this man who just oozes sex appeal and plans on making him her next conquest. If only a casual hook up could be that easy. Sav discovers that Tate is actually her new co-worker and friend Tanzi's twin brother. Despite the flirting the two of them do on their first official encounter, Sav quickly realizes that Tate is an arrogant jerk and refuses to let him use her. Tate definitely runs hot and cold to start. One minute he's flirtatious and protective of Savannah and the next he acts flippant and is back to his womanizing ways. However, the more time the two spend together, the more they both see the brokenness in the other and want to comfort one another. As much as Sav knows she shouldn't go there, who can resist the Tate Connors Effect?! These two definitely have some serious chemistry going on and the sexual tension is suffocating!Sav's character really does break my heart. Underneath the sassy exterior lies a very vulnerable woman who longs to feel comforted and taken care of. She uses one night stands as an escape, giving her a few hours of feeling needed, of being someone's world. Sav doesn't do relationships and as she starts getting deeper in with Tate, she feels her walls begin to crumble. However, both have been burned in the past and starting over is new and fragile. The slightest misconceptions and miscommunications cause jealousy and distrust to flair up and we see two people who slam their shields up instead of talking things out. Lasting relationships can't be built without trust and their relationship is certainly put to the test on several occasions.Sav is incredibly lucky to have found so many friends after just moving countries. She has a pretty great support system and they definitely add so much more to the story! I love Tanzi. She's fun, outgoing, and she also doesn't take crap from anyone. Being twins, her and Tate have a close relationship- but she definitely calls him out on his crap, which was always fun to watch. She is an awesome friend to Sav and is someone she can rely on and trust. Jack, Tanzi's boyfriend and Tate's best friend, is another great character. He treats Sav like a little sister and tends to serve as a mediator when things with Tate and Tanzi heat up. He is also pretty good at talking Tate down and helping him see sense. Lucas, who is a friend of Jack's,ends up becoming a good friend to Sav and sticks by her, even after incurring Hurricane Tate's wrath and jealousy. Lucas however is interested in Ali, Tate and Tanzi's cousin, which would lead you to believe Tate would let up on the guy a bit. Not so much. Tate has a possessive streak- he knows how Sav plays guys and once he realizes the depth of his feelings for her, he is determined to make her his and won't give up until he does.I love how the prologue of the book and the last chapter really come full circle and tie in together. I won't even lie- reading those last few chapters I felt this knot begin to form in my stomach and I don't think it will be going away until I get my hands on the next book. Thankfully, Rachel does not end on a cliffhanger but it really does get your mind churning as to what is going to happen next. Tate and Sav have some big decisions awaiting them. Will their pasts control their futures? Or will they be able to overcome it and move forward? So much weighs on an already fragile foundation. I only hope that Tate and Sav can come out stronger and little by little continue to strengthen that foundation.This is definitely a must-read. I loved this book, loved the characters, and I cannot wait to see where Rachel takes the series next!
summary: Love, Love, LOVED this book! Beware the Tate Connors Effect!

In the small town of Carrolton, everyone knew everyone's business, and what they don't know they simply make up. And so it was rumored when Michael left town -- he took with him Megan's virginity, and a priceless series of murals painted by her grandfather.The years pass and Michael is now a successful attorney, Megan following in her grandfather's footsteps is an artist, her medium working with gemstones.Fate and the last painting her grandfather completed bring Michael and Megan together once again. It doesn't take long for them to rekindle the love they shared as teenagers.The past becomes very much a part of their future. The reunited sweethearts attempt to rebuild their relationship as they work their way through years of deceit created by family and friends,Megan and Michael's story is designed to touch the reader's heart. From the opening chapter The Artist's Granddaughter unfolds pulling you deeper as secrets are unraveled and lies put to rest.I thought Ms. Bayne would have a hard time topping her last romance Prodical, I was wrong, With The Artist Grandaughter, painting with words, Ms. Bayne created a work of art sure to satisfy the romantic in everyone.Donna L. Bolk/The Romance Review
summary: Another great romance from Robin Bayne

reviewText: This book was one I begged and hope would be written because I fell so in love with Clarie and Jonathan in Mid Life Love and I did not want to let them go. I needed to know how their story ended and of course I needed more of Jonathan. He is completely swoon-worthy and he will forever be one of my favorite book boyfriends. MLL at Last picks up where MLL left off and it starts with a bang. You still have Claire running around trying to get her crap together then you have Jonathan trying to rush her so they can start the rest of their lives together. One thing I love about this entire story is you fall in love with the other characters in the book and they take root in your heart as well. You get to see the fun side of Claire and you are introduced to some very CRAZY new characters in this that give a certain element of fun to say the least.  Whitney's writing is very flawless and flows at ease. I had to keep reminding myself that this is indeed just a story and I will not run into Jonathan Statham on a elevator no matter how much I want that. This is a must read for every person who drowsed during history class. No one will be bored. Mark Ledbetter diligently researched the inchoactive formation of our republic, from early dating lists of presidents, banking and trading, militia conscription, with battles fought,  to well thought out plans of federation.We learn about the East India Company, where forts were located, and why, to elaborating on the American Revolution, the French and Indian War, the Thirty Year War, even to naming generals, admirals and commodities.Without bring overwhelmed, we learn about Acts of Congress, Acts of Parliament, the Constitution, the Declaration of Independence, Declaration of the Rights of Man, Implied Powers, even to, the Inaugural Addresses of Thomas Jefferson and James MadisonLedbetter whets curiosity as he explains the details of founding thoughts and rules formulated, then formalized, by our forefathers. He lays bare the facts about early banking systems. The success, and failures, of free trade, the committing of land speculation and expansion, why, and how, the French and Indians were involved on our early wars and settlements.Mark Ledbetter is a historian. His comprehensive facts and their ramifications nothing short of phenomenal. This Forgotten History, Part 1 should be required reading in our schools.

I received this book from the author in exchange for an honest review.3.5 starsRuby Hill is a short novella featuring a spooky ghost story along with two characters reconnecting after a traumatic death tore them apart. Sometimes I'm just in the mood for a quick read, no long term commitments, no waiting for book two, no cliffhanger ending. I enjoyed the fact that I could read this story in under an hour without stopping.Main characters Corbin and Ashley had a major falling out after Corbin blamed her for his brother's mysterious death in the Ruby Hill asylum. It's one of those old asylums that shut down in the eighties and is now frequented by ghost hunters and kids looking for a thrill. Corbin's brother Cash died there during a ghost hunt with Ashley's paranormal team.Six months later, there have been two murders within the crumbling building. The media is labeling a ghost as the killer, so Ashley's paranormal team agrees to set up equipment and investigate. Corbin is a cop saddled with the job to babysit the paranormal researchers. While exploring the dark asylum, Corbin and Ashley realize they still have feelings for each other. Corbin, a non-believer in the paranormal also learns that there might be more than logic can explain within the creepy walls.It's an interesting plot line. My main complaint is that the story is just too short. I'm dying for more information on the history and the haunting. Basically the murders are solved, along with the motive behind the murders...but it's kind of left hanging. It's nice that Corbin and Ashley found each other again, but I think Ms. Balance could either add to this story or write a sequel that handles the ghost aspect. There's more story to be told at the Ruby Hill asylum.

There are several ways to look at a book that is business based and blunt. This is a blunt book that talks about business of kindle publishing. Now I don't agree with everything the author has in the book but I'm not making 14k a month. Therefore I am not qualified to say what to do or not to do. This book does make you think. It makes you think about the business side of book writing. This book is loaded with good information. It has great links and suggestions on what do do to get sales up. I realize that there are some scathing reviews about ethics in terms of sales. I believe my job as a reviewer is to look at a book in its entirety and the audience that it is intended for. I got a lot from this book. It was an easy read. It is very clear and understanding. It leads you to making 14k a month. I give it 5 stars.

Wow! Normally, I'm not at a loss for words but really, what else is there to say about this book!There was so much going on, and usually, for me, that is not always a good thing. I much prefer a story to focus on just one or, at the most, two relationships. But as with this whole series, I just have to know what's going on with everyone.All of the couples were touched on except Alicia and Marcus but I'm OK with that. There will be another time to get more details on them. We know their babies have come home from the hospital and the couple is working on their suddenly huge family. They certainly didn't need any parts of all the drama that was taking place in their friends' lives and the friends wanted to shield them from a lot of it, so it was very realistic that we did not hear from them.I'm finding it pretty difficult to get in depth with this review for fear of spoiling things. All I can say is it a MUST READ, but the other books in the series should definitely be read first. I like the fact that SK does not do full reviews of characters and events, which too often take up valuable real estate in the story. Having read the other books, you don't want to be reminded of details over and over. You want just enough to refresh your memory and SK does that flawlessly.I am very much looking forward to reading more of the Pattels story. Lorenzo has definitely intrigued me and I simply must know how things play out with Hawk & Raven.I waited so long for this story and I have not even an ounce of disappointment. It was worth every second of the wait!The only thing that would make it better is if we can somehow get this on the big or even small screen. It's like reading the script of an intriguing and sexy crime drama. From MUST READ to MUST SEE TV. Yep, that would make it perfect!

Wow--I knew it would be coming from earlier in the series, and honestly, it initially irked me, but my apologies to Ms. Ritchie, because I was so wrong!!! This book is Daisy and Ryke's story and it was amazing. Despite the longer length, I was so engrossed with not only their story, but this group's tale that I was able to fly through the pages.Ryke seriously deserves his own paragraph in my review because, well he is just WORTHY. He may not have thought so about himself, but I have loved him from the beginning of this series. He is in your face, foul-mouthed, and sexy like no other. Ritchie does such an amazing job with her writing that I feel like I can see him climbing up the face of a mountain, let alone doing other things. Let me just say, I have a new appreciation for cornfields. Despite all that, he was a troubled guy who just really wanted to do the right thing but found it difficult due to his past. I loved how he works through everything and I love how he eventually handles everything with Daisy and her family.Daisy has been somewhat of a wild child throughout this entire series but I had no true idea how troubled she was. This story helped illustrate how Daisy was in someways more mature than her sister Lily. Daisy, due to pressure from her mother, just had to grow up too fast and was in situations that no teenager should be facing. But all of that craziness in the life of Daisy helped me come to grips with the concept of Ryke and Daisy.Aside from their love story, the great part of this book, this series, is that all the characters we have come to love play very active roles in this story. It is not the casual mention of the characters but it is truly a continuation of their stories as well. As you may have guessed, the characters which were less than appealing, ie Ryke and Loren's dad and the Calloway girls' mom, show up as well. All the craziness and drama of their lives and the love they have found despite their situations make this such an entertaining book and one of my favorite series. I cannot wait to read more!!!!
summary: Yet another winner by Ritchie--5 Star Review

Hard Glamour is an excellent read.To me this story seemed like a coming of age story not only for the main character Lane, but, for Dillon as well; with a naughty edge. I would not exactly call it steamy but then again that is all up to your interpretation of the more sexy-time scenes. I loved the character development in this story. The small town girl with no Hollywood know how, landing soon to be most in damned playboy actor, at first this can seem a bit farfetched but during the story it all starts to make sense.  I especially liked how everything that happened seemed random but in truth, most people land jobs and find boyfriends or girlfriends in the most unusual places. If you enjoy drama and romance with a little bit of crazy this book is for you. If you are looking for a fun book to read this weekend I suggest picking up Hard Glamour.I received this book for an honest reviewBook Description from Amazon:A steamy new adult romance set in the gritty world of Hollywood entertainment. Motorcycle riding alpha, bad-boy, Dillon MacAvoy tries hard not to fall for small-town girl Lane Channing in Hard Glamour.A promise to keep...Honoring her mother's last wish, Lane Channing vows to follow her dreams. She takes the 'big risk' and leaves her small Kansas town behind and heads to LA, the city of dreams. She's got a stellar job lined up, an old jeep, and 20 bucks to last her to her first paycheck. Her hopes shatter when she arrives to find her job's been given to someone else. Now she's broke and if she doesn't do something fast will soon be living on the streets. Welcome to cutthroat -- Lane is most certainly not in Kansas anymore.On the cusp of success...Dillon MacAvoy has one goal -- to become a star -- whatever it takes. Even if it means honing his bad-boy can't-be-tamed-and-forever-single image. Besides the image isn't far from the truth. Dillon cares only about his younger brother and his career. He's on the brink of superstardom if he can just decide on the next right script. But for that, he needs a script reader he can trust.In a strange twist of fate...Lane Channing is Dillon's last chance. If Lane lasts the summer without becoming MacAvoy's latest conquest, she's guaranteed a job in entertainment. No problem, as long as she can ignore the heat that pulses through her every time Dillon is in the room. After all, love and commitment with a sweet, hometown girl would only ruin the Dillon MacAvoy brand.

reviewText: Ok, I think this is the last book in the Take A Chance series, and it totally rocked! It went out with a bang, and if you've read any of this series you MUST read this one. The epilogue alone was freaking fantastic, and then you get the story of Mike and Morgan. This couple is something else, I tell ya! Now I've read three out of four of these books, somehow I skipped book two. Either way, I don't think you'd be terribly lost to read these as a standalone, but I think they absolutely rock as a series in order.Mike is the guy we got to know a little bit in the last book, Play Me. He was a bit of a jerk, but in a playful way. Anyhow, you get to know him as the player. Mike is never going to get tied down with a woman. He even has a whole stoplight theory on how to be with a woman, and let me just say it's an eye opener. Right away I was excited to know he was going to get his butt and his heart handed to him in this book.Morgan is a dancer, but not a stripper! Unfortunately this is not a clarification Mike has before he opens his big mouth. Well, Morgan is also a bit of a firecracker, and a little stand-off turns into a drunken night of fun and that leads to... well, marriage.There are so many fun sparring type situations in this book. Mike and Morgan definitely go head to head and its awesome. And then their make up sex, omg, its awesome too! I think they are probably my favorite couple in the series, they were just so much fun. I mean, you see someone, your attracted, you bicker, you make up, you have some drinks, and then wake up the next morning and your married. Awwwesome! And you get some cameos from previous couples, and that's always fun.So this series is really quick. Depending on how fast you read, it's a one or two sitting read, generally. But Diane Alberts really packs it in during those pages. Every book is filled with drama and some super hot sex. And I love how she makes these men so up front about being in love with the heroines. The men are persistent, and it just makes me want to cheer. Vegas is the perfect setting for the whole series, but this book especially. Let me just say one thing, and you'll get it after you read it, but I freaking love it.

I really liked this series closer, the half demon assassin leading man, Creed, was really great - one of his 'super powers' is being likable. The romance was a slow build even though the initial connection from Creed's side is the instinctual 'mine' that's not normally handled anywhere near this well in the majority of paranormal romances. What really makes this work is that while he's hers, Creed treasures his heroine enough to allow her to make the choice as to whether she wants to claim him as hers. The leading lady Nieve, initially seems frail but there is a hidden kernel of strength within her and just as something about Creed wakes her up to the piece of the past she's forgotten, his support allow her to build that strength - in a world where women have very little power.It was fun to see the pair from the first book play a part in the wrap up and we finally get to learn some of Scratch's secrets. Great finish to this post apocalyptic old west-ish paranormal romance.

reviewText: “RomperSuit” offers both brilliant writing and mesmerizing characters whose lives and fates are constantly interconnecting with one another. Charlie has a lot of layers to his personality, but even the minor players are well developed. Between that and the non-stop action I stayed hooked on this one from start to finish. It's very much an escapist book in that once you start reading, you forget about everything else and just immerse yourself in the story. And I really appreciated that the twists kept me from figuring out how things would go until they were going. I hate it when I can see how something will end halfway through, but “RomperSuit” kept me guessing to the very end. Highly recommend.

Amanda Young is one of my "sure thing" authors whose books I pick up when I want to be guaranteed a good read. I've read most of her books, and so far I haven't found anything I didn't like. Her characters are realistic, her love scenes are hot without being purple or cheesy, her narrative is smooth, her dialogue is natural...she's just a great writer.This is a hot little novella (50-odd pages) about a guy that finally decides he's done with women. The same day he decides to act upon his same-sex fantasies, he runs across the younger brother of an old friend. Sparks fly, things get hot, and the rest is history.I admit the "supposedly straight guy turns gay" story is one of my guilty pleasures. I know it's not the most realistic scenario, but it's one for which I'll gladly suspend disbelief. I love the secret glances, the tentative touches, and the "so wrong but feels so good" angst. If I had one complaint about this particular story, however, it would be that the transition was little too quick for my taste. In this case, though, it's obviously more of a word count limitation than intentional rushing. It's difficult to capture the psychology of coming out in 50-something pages, so you have to understand beforehand that a short story like this is going to contain the highlights rather than the full experience. If you want a short, sexy e-book and have a couple of bucks to spare, buy this. Or just make it simple and buy Amanda's entire backlist.

I manage to page through the repeats and finally that chapter ends. AND THEN, it's the end of the book!!!  The author never gets to the upper floors to tell  us about the sleeping/nursery arrangements, which was the floor I was most interested in to begin with. Crazy time.Now, I am well aware that some of these free Kindle books have problems with paging, continuity, etc. and maybe in the future this one will be cleaned up but, until then, stay away from this book.  Even though it was free when I got it, it wasn't worth the aggravation. I am not a happy camper right now.

reviewText: Eternal Hope is a very well written book, filled with action, plot twists, and a some very steamy sexy romance. *Fans self* Eternal Hope has a perfect blend of lovable/hated characters and a steady plot line that will hold you in its grips right through to the end.  I can honestly say I stayed up well into the night reading, sacrificing my sleep (who needs sleep anyway) until I was finished. I really didn't want it to be over. Frankie Rose takes you on an action packed journey with twists even I never saw coming.  Heck even things I thought I had figured out were completely wrong.  And saying that is something, there are not many books that I don't have at least 3/4 of it figured out before I get to the end. Well done, Frankie, well done!So first off we have Farley.  This fiesty little package of womanhood is one gigantic force to be reconned with.  Sure she might not be the best fighter, but she is willing to learn. And yeah she doesn't know that much about herself and what she can do but that won't stop her from trying to protect those she loves at all costs, using whatever ability she has in her possession.  Farley is a girl well worth the time getting to know.  I truly admire her spunk and ability to get out of sticky situations. The best thing about Farley is that she still has compassion and believes that even though someone is "evil" that there might still be a way to save them.  Farley is a girl who knows her mind and sticks to her guns.  She is no wishy washy heroine.  If that is the way it is, then that is the way it will be.  She will do anything in her power to make it happen.Now for the swoonage ladies. Daniel, ah Daniel.  Where oh where did Frankie create this beautiful creature.  Daniel is the perfect blend of alpha male, who still manages to be shy is so many ways.  Sure he can be one sarcastic son of a gun, but when he is with Farley he is a whole different person.  I can admit that in Sovereign Hope I had my doubts about him, but he sure made me a believer! Daniel is yet another complex character that will have you wondering what is really going on.  Though we do get a tiny peek into his head with several of his PoV's it is still rather vague as to what happened between him and a certain messenger.  Daniel will keep you guessing about his past, but never about his feelings for Farley.  The one part, it had me teary.  It was heartwarming to see him doubt her feelings for him.  To hear him talk to her and be so unsure... *sighs* Really it is one of the things that had me in love with him the most.  Daniel is my newest book boyfriend, I am never giving him up, EVER!There are not many authors out there that can take a YA sexy scene and make it either too chaste or too skanky, but Frankie Rose sure can.  Her steamy scenes will have your pulse racing and melting into a pile of goo. Eternal Hope has tons of action for those who love to be well entertained.  This installment to The Hope series was everything I hoped it would be and more.  I am really kicking my butt for letting it sit so long on my kindle without being read. If you love alpha boys who melt your heart and heroines who know what they want and go for it, this is your series.  So, what I am saying is, why have you not bought it yet? Oh and when is part three coming out. Must have it now!

What do you get when you cross a cop and an ex-Army bad boy?Pure sizzle.Under the crisp uniform of RCMP officer Kendra Givens, a vulnerable yet sensual woman guards her carefully structured life. She doesn't need anything adding to a challenging job which exposes her to society's most base and troublesome elements.Jake Symonds, despite his honourable Army career, is known in town as a mischief-maker and all around bad boy. As far as Kendra is concerned, as a local bar owner, he is responsible for a good portion of her nightly strife. If his patrons drank less, surely there'd be less fights, disorderly conduct, and domestic disputes.When she answers a call about a break and enter at his pub, she's irritated and on edge. It has nothing to do with his tight, muscular body or his intense hazel eyes. She'd never consider him worthy of an attraction. So why is her pulse racing?In the Line of Duty is the kind of book you start and finish in one sitting. You have to. There's a lot packed into this short novel and I found myself thinking about the characters long after I inhaled the book. At times achingly sweet and others steamy and ablaze with passion, In the Line of Duty is the perfect book for a veranda, a swing and your favourite summer drink.Donna Alward's books are filled with real characters with compelling stories to tell. Always a page turner and always satisfying.

I have had the pleasure of reading and reviewing all of Ms. Black's Justice Series, the last one called Tracking Shadows just this July. That series, in the genre of UF Fiction, takes place in the year 2096 with Alpha males and Kick ass heroines. This newest release, Matchmakers Mark, is quite a change, which shows another side of our talented Regan Black.The setting for this beautiful love story is Charlestown, South Carolina. Please do not get me wrong, this is no easy boy meets girl, boy falls in love, and they live happily ever after kinda story. Heaven forbid, but it is certainly a light-hearted paranormal romance, filled with mystery down to almost the last page.I quote from the book blurb. "When you're more than just human, searching for your soul mate and eHarmony doesn't ask all the right questions, it's time to call in the expert: Campbell Consulting and the Legendary Matchmaker".Amy Campbell, an English Professor, and her dog Guinness, a greyhound, are visiting her friend Maeve King. They are both working at the local college teaching a class together. Amy, while walking with Guinness, wanders into a beautiful Flower Shoppe owned by Lily Parker. These three women are the heart of the story.We learn that Amy's Aunt Camille is a Matchmaker. A long line of them are in the Campbell family tree, and Amy is next in succession. We learn about Aunt Camille through the letters she writes to Amy during our story.Lily, owner of the flower shop is a Halfling, half elf/half human. She has embraced her human side, as she feels she cannot be of service to her elf family because her magic is not strong. She buries herself in her flowers, and wishes to find true love.Maeve King is a human and best friend to Amy. At the moment we meet these wonderful women, our story unfolds, with such a rich story line, humor, and mystery, it was hard to put this down... and I didn't.Darian Knoll, the Matchmakers Guard, has come to Charleston to give something to Amy from her Aunt, and that's where we begin. Dare has given his life to guarding Aunt Camille. What could this mean?Lily has a mark in her arm. She has always thought it was her mating mark. That is how she would find her true love, they would match. The mark starts to itch, then burn; it starts to move, and grow and what could all this mean?The twists and turns are such a great start to the newest series for Ms. Black. Her world building is elaborate in description and flavor. One could feel the spray of the water; one could certainly be spooked in the graveyard...And yet, the lovers were sensual, strong and so right. Of the three women we met, I tended to favor Lily. She had such a strong sense of what was right, and wanted to harm no one, even at the cost to her own desires. The ensemble Ms. Black brings to the table is wonderful, and from what I see, the next episode with them will be welcome on my TBR Pile. I am so happy this will continue.Review by Gloria LakritzSenior Reviewer and Review Chair for the Paranormal Romance Guild
summary: great New Series for Regan Black

reviewText: Jory Strong's latest installment in her Supernatural Bonds series is erotic and hot. Strong's imaginative voice creates an interesting and unique paranormal world where various shape-shifters live among the humans. Dominant, protective, and truthful, Jubal is a delicious alpha male. Summer, a submissive in search of a Master, is loyal to her friends and does not trust easily. Jubal and Summer's chemistry ignites from their initial meeting. But, Summer's suspicions presents a problem for Jubal's dominant nature. Using dominance and submission along with discipline and punishment, Strong aptly portrays the subtle trust-building dance between Jubal and Summer. Having enjoyed this book so much, I am adding the earlier books in this series to my to-be-read pile while anxiously awaiting the next installment.I received an eBook copy from the publisher for purpose of an honest review for The Jeep Diva. I was not compensated for this review, and all conclusions are my own responsibility.

I finished Lisa Kessler's newest book and start to a new series, Moonlight. Yes, this is a werewolf book with some jaguars. I have notice a trend of these kinds of books, but I actually really liked this book. Let me share my thoughts:First off, the story might feel a little slow at first, but you need to keep in mind this is the start of a new series. It is very important to keep in mind, because Ms. Kessler is building the story. Plus, it's kind of important to know why certain people are getting chased and murder.So, we have Adam Sloan who happens to be a werewolf and he's wonder why there's a jaguar in his territory. Once he stumbles upon Lana Turpin, Adam's life gets turn upside down (that's putting it mildly). Anyways, he sees something special between him and Lana, but can't face the facts that he found his mate.Yep jaguar and wolf, it's bound to get complicated. If that wasn't enough, Lana has Nero Organization chasing after, which endangers Adam's pack.Once the story is establish, it's pretty action pack. We have a mysterious group that seems pretty evil. Then you have a complicated relationship with jaguar and wolf possibly getting together. I mean how do tell your family, "Hey I found my mate, by the way she's a jaguar." Yep, not going to go over to well. So, if you are looking for a new shifter book with wolves and jaguars with evil mystery group, you might want to give Moonlight a try. I can't wait to see what happens next.Copy provided by publisher

reviewText: What a superb historic romance series. I'd been very much looking forward to this next installment in the story of David and Murdo, and the author delivered in a deliciously satisfying way. I love how both Murdo and David are very strong in character, and the evolution of their interpersonal dynamic is a delight to witness. Murdo has more "life experience" and is higher class than David, but never acts superior, snide or dismissive. He does treat David with the care and respect he deserves, while gently, yet insistently, guiding him to accept his feelings regarding his sexuality, and their relationship. LOVE this depiction. Such a breath of fresh air these characterizations are. (I read a lot of historicals, and so many feature one haughty main character and one that is presented as painfully naive.) The sex and intimate scenes between David and Murdo are the perfect blend of passion and tenderness - hot, romantic and also very much important in depicting character development. The plot is interwoven with wonderful secondary characters and threads which are very exciting, and I love reading about the true historic events and descriptions of Edinburgh. I could not put this book down as I just had to know what was going to happen next. More please!!
summary: Superb historic romance, I could not put it down!

reviewText: Emlyn Chand's Courtney Saves Christmas is the tale of one spunky, determined little penguin. On Christmas, Courtney recieves a compass from Santa. It is the perfect gifts for an adventure-loving young penguin. Finding herself impressed and in awe of the lovable Mr. Claus, Courtney is determined to travel to the North Pole in order to give him a thank you hug.Armed with her trusty compass, Courtney learns to navigate the world. She also learns a lot about bravery and her own strength. When she finally arrives at the North Pole, she finds that not only has an entire year passed, but Christmas is in serious trouble. Without giving away too much, let's just say that Courtney's strength and the lessons learned throughout the book are enough to turn her into a hero.This book had me grinning like a little kid, which is truly the sign of an amazing children's book author. When I finished, I literally recapped the entire story for my family. It's uplifting and heartwarming, without being too saachrine.Courtney Saves Christmas belongs on the reading lists of lower grade-school kids everywhere this holiday season.Disclaimer: I was gifted a copy of this book in exchange for a review.
