reviewText: When I was asked to read & review this book, my first impulse was to make sure I was clear about what the term, "dystopia" refers to. (quote) "A dystopia is the opposite of a utopia. It appears in many artistic works, particularly in stories set in the future. They are often characterized by dehumanization, totalitarian governments...or other characteristics associated with a cataclysmic decline in society." (end of quote)- Wikipedia"Electronic Gags" by Kudakwashe Muzira fits the above definition perfectly. It is set in a totalitarian USA governed by a military dictator. The protagonist is a biologist named Freddie, who is a rebel. He is the only person to safely get away from a police raid on a secret rebel meeting. Michael, his best friend, is put on death row. Freddie will try to save his friend and his country.With this plot, you will be reminded of Orwell's 1984. In the real world, you will be reminded of Mandela's fight against apartheid in South Africa, King's struggle for civil rights in the USA, and Ghandi's nonviolent resistance in India, which led to its independence from England.Suffice it to say that the memory of mankind is fragile. Consequently, there will always be a place for books such as this one, which helps mankind to remember past mistakes, and hopefully, avoid repeating them. If this book helps us to do that, then it is a fitting tribute to the memory of Mandela, King and Ghandi. Highly recommended.Reviewed by Thomas Jerome BakerAuthor ofHow to Coach A Debate Team*****Many thanks to the author for providing me with a digital copy of this book in exchange for a fair and unbiased review.*****
summary: Dystopia is the Opposite of Utopia: Memory of Mankind is Fragile

reviewText: This author is a good communicator. And to be a good communicator, you must be a good listener. I have these visions of her stopping, sitting in silence, waiting to allow things in, from others or her own self, for life's truths, muck ups, 'duh' moments and smiles to wash over her and flow out from her fingertips to the page. From the opening sentence of this book, she had me in a verbal headlock and I knew I wasn't getting released until I read every word.I want mid-afternoon pick-me-ups like those! Oh, you know the ones I mean. Ok, now you've got "Afernoon Delight" by the Starland Vocal Band jogging through your mind and it won't leave. Earworm! Earworm!One of my early favorite lines from Harry, imagining what someone else is assuming he's thinking ***SPOILER*** as if "... I need to feel like a special f***ing snowflake" ***SPOILER END*** tells us a lot a out him, about how he thinks, his multifaceted nature. It does all come into play.I was not easily able to determine where things were going or would end up and I love that. One of the few things that I was able to predict was the truth surrounding the first encounter with Logan - I did see that coming before Harry realized it. This was pretty much the only time in regards to the major events and reveals. I almost think this was maybe done on purpose given the role Logan would play in Harry's life. One small thing to give us as readers to tether Logan in Harry's story and make us curious about him, to remain interested. Believe me, there is interest.Now Harry, talk about a fully painted picture of a character. Not a portrait but a full blown landscape. He's confident about work and people, how he can read them. But then, he has real doubts about the same and their feelings towards him. I think this explains his inability to have seen Danny's true feelings about him specifically much earlier on. I was like Harry and I didn't think it was that... deep. The clues were there but I, as the reader, and Harry as the man brushed them aside as something else. That or it was just denial. Perfect example: ***SPOILER*** Danny to Harry when Harry picks him up from Danny's first long appointment with someone, "I'm all f***ed out," and he and Harry sort of cuddle up together. In all honesty, very sweet and yes, honest. ***SPOILER END***First fave mention: ***SPOILER*** Irish whiskey!!! I pretend in my mind that it's Bushmills. ;) ***SPOILER END***I won't talk much of Liam. Yes, he's definitely important, but given the state of their relationship, he and Harry, as the story opens, it's used as a catalyst for many things. It's not necessarily a front burner part of the story, in a sense. The one thing I'll say is that the dominoes of deception kept lining up and I could feel the cascade of lies as being a word away from starting the noisy, if orderly, clickity click of destruction. Luckily, all will get out alive, for the most part.The dom/sub scenes between Harry and Logan are hot, like the ***SPOILER*** metronome scene, holy shiznoly ***SPOILER END***but they are spiced with uncertainty, hesitation and, dare I say, fledgeling connection, dangerously bordering on cautious acceptance. We do get insights and forward momentum in all of them, the few that there are.Must. Use. Phrase. ***SPOILER*** "blah, blah, blahity, blah" ***SPOILER END*** And you know you'll use it, too!! ;)Second fave mention: a way Harry uses to describe his own reaction to something is ***SPOILER*** "When Luke and Laura finally drifted apart on General Hospital, I cried for a week." ***SPOILER END*** HA!I won't spoiler tag this line so that I can show the quality of writing, and it's intriguing, to boot: this is from Harry - Danny's not my sunshine on my rainy day, but his storm cloud crackling provides much better ambiance.Do I need to sigh to really tell you?Just as life keeps us guessing, so too did this story. I really didn't know, couldn't foretell, what would happen (or not) between Harry and all of Danny, Logan and Liam. Well, Liam somewhat. That was pretty serious secrecy, what he did. And getting back to Harry and Danny for a moment, there must be something there between them. Why else the strong reactions? Cut-to-the-quick relief, hurt, hope, fear, desire and doubt. All so strong.You never know who you may find, or who finds you, who you may end up spending your days and nights with. It feels like the author reached inside a part of me and laid out my story in the sense of emotions, connections and experiences that we've probably all encountered at some point. And it was all done within a story about a rentboy service. It feels like you're not reading but rather hearing Harry's complex inner voice first hand - complex like most of ours. That may seem obvious given the first person POV, but it's more than that. The knowledge level of the character the author has created here is off the charts.I wholeheartedly recommend this book to anyone. Anyone. ANYONE.Bonus: after you're done licking your chops clean on this one, go and read the little freebie "Tinsel Is Like Bondage For Trees" , you will salivate all over again. MWAH!
summary: A very clear voice in a complex story

reviewText: This story about aspen  a small  town  broken relationship. Wounded soldier. Being  dump by girl  in an emailComes back home wounded.  Finds the still love each other . Not bad story

Deserted old houses. Is there anything scarier? The settling noises they make, creaks often sounding like painful moans. Imagine you are new to town, needing a place to call home for a few months. An apartment building, surrounded by thigh high grass, catches your attention. No renters, you find out, not for a while. But the rent is cheap. And you need a place to stay. So you stay. And then the horror starts.Utterly frightening, The House on Cooper Lane is an incredibly well-crafted horror story, thick with a palpable tension and indelible moments that will give you chills. Phipps writes like a freight train, grabbing the reader and never letting go, like a dog worrying its favorite toy. The story moves quickly, never bogging down, never letting the reader get comfortable. Spine-tingling chills await around every page.If ever there was a book you wouldn’t want to read at night while alone, it would be The House on Cooper Lane. Brilliantly written, this book is guaranteed to give you nightmares.
summary: Spine-tingling chills await around every page

reviewText: Is justice relative? Can it be compromised?Encryption is a realistic spy story that exposes the crimes of government in the name of national security. A murder mystery filled with espionage wrapped around political and moral issues, Encryption forces readers to examine foreign policy and national security with a more critical eye... and in doing so, readers may find they do not care for what they see.The plot is strong, the characters full and the concepts important. Overall, Encryption is well written, with only a few pesky errors. I didn't agree with the politics at all times, nor is that a requirement for my enjoyment of the novel. The novel did seem to take shots at the American government, sometimes perhaps unnecessarily, all the while involving a plot that portrays British government action as cold, immoral and, at times, outright devious, all in the name of the so-called "greater good."An excellent tale set in a more realistic, less fantastical world, Encryption is sure to please fans of spy thrillers and political thrillers. It is both entertaining and thought-provoking, well worth the read.
summary: An Intricate Spy Tale Immersed in Governement Corruption

reviewText: There is deep emotions here developed in this story which I really love a lot. Funny, romantic, and many more. You should definitely get this book it is amazingly beautiful.

The glamour of the Kennedy presidency is still remembered...while I do not remember this period myself...those of the older generation spoke glowingly of Camelot.  In this brief overview of Jackie Kennedy's life, you come away with an appreciation of that moment in time.  Finally the melding of technology with an eBook helped enhance the story by presenting clips of film from the past.  While this would  not be the definitive book for information on all things Jackie,  the overall presentation and succinct writing has the reader coming away with a satisfied feeling of having been given a glimpse into Jackie Kennedy's life.

I found that odd and couldn't' get past it, also I can usually disregard bad punctuation but the speech mark positioning was killing me.I also found story base very similar to many other books, nothing original.Apart from that it was a very easy , quick read.

This electrifying thriller starts with a bang and keeps going. When Mark's wife Kelly finds a condom in their marital bed she concludes he's been cheating on her and kills him. After calling an ambulance she panics and goes on the run. Consumed by her curiosity to find out who her husband was having an affair with, Kelly embarks on an investigation that turns the notion that her husband was simply cheating on her on its head.Although the main story was not predictable, I did guess the ending when I was 25 % into the book. Still it was a great read and Bianca Sloane remains one of my favourite Indie thriller authors.

Needless to say Gareth comes out and him and David become lovers and then Edge, Gareth best friend, who hates gays ends up coming out of the closet as well. Personally I liked the story I just think it could have done without Edge being thrown into the mix. To me they didn't seem to mesh well and I'm not a big fan of ménage's as it is anyways, but despite not being a fan of ménage's I just didn't feel Edge's character. I would recommend that you at least give this book a try because you may like it and like I said it does have strong characters in Gareth and David and has a pretty good storyline.

The only thing that I really missed when I moved into my beautiful town home was the ability to have my own vegetable and herb gardens. When I lived in a regular house I had several gardens and I really enjoyed growing (and eating) my own produce. I am not a very talented gardener when it comes to indoor plants and every attempt that I have ever made to even keep house plants has resulted in utter failure. Thanks to this book I now feel as though I have acquired enough knowledge to successfully grow an indoor garden. This book explains the importance of lighting and fertilization, as well as how to achieve it indoors. It explains what kinds of bulbs produce effects that most closely imitate the sun as well as how to use the different types of fertilizers. I can’t wait to get started on my own indoor garden!

I finished this book over 30 minutes ago and had to give myself a breather because WTF, Lori??!!  What a whirlwind of a book this was.  I was so up & down with Jacqueline (Jaq), I thought I was becoming bipolar.  Jaq doesn't make the best of decisions (saying so mildly) and she has the best of a friend in Shelley (no enabler there). After struggling through a series of Ms Bartal's books with a main character who can't make up her mind from book to book, (gave up at book 3) I thought I was reading a different author entirely when I began "Won't You Be My Neighbor?"Apart from wanting to tell the male character how to actually "Woo" a lady, I was kept involved the whole book through. The author of this book contacted me, asking for an honest review of her book.  Since it was available for free download, I decided to see how my daughter liked it.Kid's Point of View:My daughter was most emphatically NOT in a story mood when I started to read it to her.  In fact, the resident five-year-old was deep in a computer battle playing her favorite online game, but I started to read it aloud.  By the second page, she was standing by my chair asking me to start over.  And within minutes, she was curled up in my lap, listening to the story of Katy and her dragon friend.She was absolutely delighted and at the end asked me if there was another Katy book for the Kindle.  There was and we had to download it immediately.Mom's Point of View:This is a fun, sweet tale.  There was nothing scary about it.  My daughter did get a little worried when the dragon left Katy, but just for a moment.  She found the book funny and it kept her interest.  This is also great if you have a child who is afraid of swimming lessons.  My daughter just started them again and was a little worried.  The story hit home.  The rhyme is a little forced in parts, but overall well done.  As for Kindle formatting, the text and pictures were on different pages, which bothered me a little.  I would have liked for my daughter to have been able to view the illustrations as we read the text, not after each section.All in all, a cute book that my daughter enjoyed!

This book contains several short stories about Arabian Knights (not Nights!) that are very similar to fables and folk tales that we read as kids, however the characters differ, and the societal rules quite are quite different. However, the moralistic leanings of the stories are very similar to fables. Generosity, humbleness, fairness, and the like are all represented here by the Knight's tales. I think my favorite part of the stories was the way the language read. A line for example "Al Numan pondered Hanthala's words for a while as his conflicted emotions chased one another across his face". Colorful use of words and tempo, but no understanding is lost whatsoever. I think you will sincerely enjoy the Knight's tales, and frankly, you can't beat the download price!

reviewText: Author and blogger Nonnie Jules has taken some of her most enlightening and encouraging posts and put them into this wonderful little book, Sugarcoatin' Is For Candy & Pacifyin' is for Kids!.I began following Nonnie shortly after she began her blog and yet I have managed to miss a few of these posts that she has chosen to share with us.  Her writing and her speaking are from the heart.  Nonnie reminds us that we must be Candle Lighters and help others whenever we can.  How wonderful it will be to reach a successful pinnacle in your life and find that many of those you have helped without expecting anything in return are standing right next to you basking in the spotlight.  We are reminded over and over again that success does not come from walking on someone's toes but by helping others along your way.  I truly believe that this is an inspiration for all of us whether or not we are readers, writers, parents, or grandparents.Nonnie is the author of The Good Mommies Guide to Raising (Almost) Perfect Daughters and Daydream's Daughter Nightmare's Friend (both excellent reads).  She also talks the talk and walks the walk.  Recently she founded the very successful Rave Reviews Book Club and 4 Wills Publishing.I encourage everyone to check out this book as well as her other books.

reviewText: Ethan Parker is a sort of loner. When he comes to hear a girl crying night after night next door, he finally does the right thing. They form a friendship and bond that is really sweet. The Private Affairs of Lady Jane Fielding is a high-emotion, steamy novella. After an unfortunate accident, Lord Jacob Fielding and Lady Jane Fielding are deemed unable to have any more children, which causes issues when their lack of a son brings Jacob’s vile brother Arthur on the scene, expecting to be named heir.I’ve read one novel from Viveka Portman before this one, The Wicked Confessions of Lady Cecelia Stanton and although I enjoyed the story, I thought the formatting was too overly-edited and choppy. In The Private Affairs of Lady Jane Fielding, the formatting was much better and easier to follow.The book is told from Jane’s perspective and she was refreshingly honest and I found her easier to like than I had expected. Her husband Jacob’s emotions needed to be covered in order for the plot to make sense but we get a great insight to Jacob just from Jane’s telling because of her obvious love and care for his feelings.The characterisation was great. Portman really makes it easy to hate Arthur as he is very irritating and his actions infuriating. He was selfish and throughout, I was hoping for him to get his comeuppance. Matthew was the opposite, a lot more sincere and likeable and the author developed the main characters a lot more than I had anticipated given the length of the book.The way the plot plays out probably leads The Private Affairs of Lady Jane Fielding down a slightly sordid route yet some of their choices felt easy to understand. I loved the tone and the way Jane recounted the story. The Private Affairs of Lady Jane Fielding was fascinating, a little erotic and easy to enjoy.4.5/5.*Book gifted for honest review.

You can set it in there the other way and thenyou only have to open the magnetic latch to charge it, but then the automatic on/off feature will not work because it is set in there the wrong directionfor that. reviewText: Every so often an author comes along whose work I'm not familiar with. This is the first I've read from Ms. Froese and it about blew my socks off. Drawn in from the get go by the intriguing black and white cover and beautiful writing style, the lifelike characters keep the reader's attention glued to the pages.With settings so real you are almost walking the streets and smelling the coffee, the mystery surrounding Anne's late aunt just serve to pull you in further.This book is most definitely a keeper and I look forward to reading more of Ms. Froese's work.

Frankie is very independent and sure she will never marry.  Then she meets Seth and falls in love, but he is already in love with Violet a girl Frankie feels she can not compete with.  But fortunately Seth realizes beauty when it is only on the surface is worthless. A girl who is beautiful inside and out is a priceless find.  He wants to marry Frankie whatever her reasons for thinking herself unworthy.

TWINS? SERIOUSLY? TWINS?  OMG!  Is there anything better in a book than the main character having a twin brother?  I think not!  Jared and Rocky.  Jared and James own their own construction company.  With their hard party ways make the Weldon twins almost lose their business.  Who is their biggest competition?  Roxeanne (Rocky) McKenna.Now I don't do spoilers in my review, but out of all the 3 first books, this is the most intriguing of them all.  The twists, turns and terror are just awesome.  When you think you know who the bad guy is, bam, you get tossed into another idea of who it might be.  Clearly Saints has done her research on this book!IRA from the 80's Ireland and threats to the present are too good to put down.  Add in the steamy sex scenes and you have the perfect romance/thriller book around!

reviewText: It is 1889 and Christmas for the members of Thursday Night Murder Games Club. this was one crazy ride from page one! I loved that max doesn't know anything and you, as the reader, get to learn everything with him. A wonderful read! I can't wait for the next book!!

reviewText: This brief book features a practical introduction to understanding Alzheimer's disease. If you are looking for a book that explains how dementia affects the brain without all the confusing medical jargon, this concise guide provides an admirable outline. In addition to providing valuable tips on care-giving, this book also offers advice on how families can better recognize and cope with the effects of this disease as their loved one undergoes cognitive and behavioral changes. Recommended.

...this isn't the conclusion!  The story was exciting, with twists and unexpected turns. I read the first book,Aiden's Game (A Tale of Three Hearts).  Daisy's Choice further developed the characters of Daisy and Aiden.  I think Daisy is very immature and selfish, but she grows up a bit.  Aiden is a likeable character despite his controlling tendencies.  Pete...he's always gonna be the underdog.  I couldn't help but feel bad for him, even after the test results!  Overall, the writing was great, it draws you in and holds your attention.  What initially appears to be lust at first sight turns someting more meaningful. It makes you believe in second chances. It ends the way I hoped, but there is no conclusion.  We are left wondering what Aiden will do with the results.  There MUST be another story.  We also need to find out what will happen with Pete!

When will I learn to check if these books are not complete?  I was disappointed once again to find no conclusion to the plot.  I enjoyed the descriptions of the concert venue and places Yayoi  went in New Zealand. I would have liked to see the characters developed more fully--Bill seemed to show little depth. A wonderful heartwarming believable story. The cover is excellent it gives the hint of a hero. A women with strong will but smart enough to know when to make a move. The story encourages everyone but especially women to know, you don't have to endure life you can enjoy it.

There are a lot of grammar errors and misspellings, but if you can overlook that, the story is very interesting.  It keeps me up until the wee hours of the night.  The author needs to find a better editor.

I love Erik and Kelli's story. This is a perfect addition to the series and fills in some of Erik's past that we haven't found out yet. As always Scott, I love reading your books and your style of writing.

I read the premise of Xenofreak Nation and thought, "huh, that's interesting." What I didn't expect was to be drawn, almost instantaneously, into a well-developed world that is believably what we could be in the near future. The characters are dense, multifaceted, all individuals who make you feel as though they could each have their own books written about them. And the centerpiece of this cast is a keystone. Sheltered, but neither stupid nor spineless, Bryn is the backbone of the story. Her growth, her understanding of the world around her, that the people in it are all people, her acceptance of her own mutilation are masterfully done.But although the plot is fantastic, the characters engaging, the premise original, the most subtle and crucial bit that makes this book a true 5-star is Conway's writing. She gives hints, she shows, she alludes to, then delivers later with explanations. But she doesn't bog you down, just offers moments of clarification and certainty amid an environment where so much is guarded and uncertain. Her writing made me think about her book, her characters and her world when I couldn't read, and helped me re-immerse immediately each time I picked it back up. Conway delivers little bits that are subtle, but stayed with me.A true 5-star read, highly recommended. I look forward to great things from Melissa Conway.

I am enjoying this series.  The girls are feisty and crazy at times in their foolish behaviour but always likeable and the men so deliciously sweet and so not as macho as they think.  Erin and Marcelo are a great couple and fun to follow.  There are some flaws in the plot perhaps but the thing that overrides this is the enjoyment we get from the flow of the story.  This is an enjoyable book and sometimes that is more than enough.  I am going through a mini crisis and reading this series is keeping me entertained very easily and so I repeat sometimes this is enough.  Just started on Natalia in the third book, this is a long mini crisis!
It was most certainly a very  interesting version of vampiric folklore and I will definitely buy the next book that already looks promising

I AM IN SHOCK!!! Without giving any spoilers I have to say that true fans will LOVE this book but there are sooooo many awful things that happen that it will hurt! BIG HURT! But true to form it is extremely well written and awesome. If you are wondering if you should start reading this series WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR! But read every other book first and be prepared for big shocks in this one. I can't wait for the next one! Thank you Sara. I was gifted this book but I have bought every other one by the author.

I don't know why I buy these short ones, I like something I can read for at least a day, not 20 minutes.  I guess I'm not paying attention.  Lots of adjectives describing just about everything, a good plot though.  Pretty good read, inventive if I do say so myself.

Heeeee this was fantabulous! I mean really - Red Riding Hood (a kickbutt chick with blades) and the Woodsman (who obviously carries an axe), in a post-apocalyptic world, battling zombies? Who wouldn't want to read this? And if you are familiar with Tara's work you know that she rocks the smexy times and can make anybody laugh. Seriously the only bad thing about this book was it is a novella and I wanted MORE! Sadly, it appears that her WIP is not a book starring the intriguing Belle, although I have been told it should come "someday".  *sigh*As with all Tara Quan books this was a sassy, funny, quirky (and each one has a different quirk), seriously sexy and sensual good book.I have not read - although I do have - the first book in this "series" Tower in the Woods and it wasn't until I was more than three-quarters through the book that I realized that a character from the first book was in this book so it obviously works well as a stand-alone. I still plan on reading Tower in the Woods as it is currently the only book of hers I haven't read and that needs to be remedied. In my humble opinion, there should not be a Tara Quan book that is unread as you are missing out on some good, smexy, fun times with intrigue or a mystery or hey, a zombie or 200, tossed in just to make it cooler.I received a copy of this book from the author in exchange for an honest review.

I was lucky enough to have read each of these books in ebook format before the collection became available. Now that it is I can't wait to order my printed copies of this trilogy. Each book tells the story of the Golden Queen of the Ahwahnee and how she leads her people in their battle to protect the world of man from the evil that threatens it. The stories are written from the perspective of the native people in them which draws you into their lives, their tales and their hardships. Beautifully written stories for both young and mature readers who have interested in native legends or paranormal. You won't be disappointed.

Jazz, the assistant was a much more interesting character; helpful, attentive, cheerful, open.The relationship between Maxie and Jean-Louis was not warm. They didn't even really seem to get along; disinterested.  One minute she was backing away from his vampire teeth and the next minute they were lovers - it seemed just that quick.  Huh?The vampires, particularly Pen, did not seem to like Maxie and treated her with impatience - no reasonable explanation why (and odd since they needed and wanted her skills - and they hired her).  Pen, for being as old and experienced in human nature as she should have been, was not very helpful or kind or understanding; that being said, Maxie continually acted childish and ill-tempered, then would beg them not to fire her (doesn't sound like leadership or management material).You would think after all that, that I would not want to read the next book, and I honestly don't know if I do, or will, and yet... I think the author has real potential; she gives good descriptions, and I do like the way she handles the 'blood-drinking vampire' part of the story - very low-key and easy to accept.  I want to like her story.  If the second book is as slow in getting to the meat of the story, I won't read the 3rd for sure.  But I am considering giving this series one more try...

As an Anglo-Franco the first thing that engaged me in this book was just how American it is. The characters' names, the distances they drive, the names of places and the cultural references all work together to hold the reader authentically in the action. It's one of those books where you know the make of the gun and the type of car that a character is using. Perhaps these are technical points but to me it makes it real. More important really is the broad philosophical theme that directs the course of the story. The enemy is not religion per se, but fundamentalism. When tracts or texts allow for violence to enforce any concept, civilisation has to take note and stand up. The scenario is disturbingly plausible. Fundamentalists seek to seize power by armed rebellion against the state. I will not say any more than that because you will want to read it for yourself. The writer adopts an all seeing viewpoint, allowing many characters and threads to intersect, tangle, unravel and conflict. The result is a powerful story which you always feel could be happening outside your window. Characters are drawn from the well of life, politics and ambition. Everyone knows characters like these or has seen them in history. This is the second book in the author's "Revelation Trilogy". I'm looking forward to the third book "The Revelation Effect" which is out now - and keeping my eye on CNN - just in case.

reviewText: This YA romance has all the makings of a good plot, but lacks in that the author utilizes telling more than showing the drama that transpires.  Also it is difficult to realize that when he seeks his father in a room of blue fog, that he is entering a time travel essence and so one doesn't really realize that until half-way through his meeting with the teen-age maiden Agoura and her tribe and woolly mammoths are brought into the story.  Then you realize that they are in a prehistoric age.  And so it is with the rest of the plot: in each subplot the reader is well into it before realizing he is in another time zone.  We never learn what anyone looks like as there is little development of character.  I would like to see the author rewrite this story, working on character development and by some artistic trick revealing each new time zone in the beginning of such sub-plot plus showing action of the scenes more than just describing them.Although it is a novella, it would be a more presentable book if it had the usual recitations relative to fiction, copyright, etc. and chapters.  The lack of chapters might have been the reason it was sort of confusing on the time episodes.  However, for the YA genre, it will be enjoyable.The author provided me with a free e-book so that I could do an honest review.

"Rise of Chaos" is an apocalyptic horror novel with a good dose of suspense, violence, and excitement. A new drug is formulated in Florida by "underground chemists" looking to create a substance that results in the high of marijuana but is not illegal. They succeed in creating a legal drug that mimics the effects of marijuana, but the high is killer--literally. The side effects of the drugs involve a painful death and then reanimation of the user into a mindless, flesh-craving creature that the characters of the novel call a "feeder."The feeders quickly destroy most of Florida's population, leaving only pockets of desperate survivors. Mason, the hero of the novel, is traveling through Cocoa Beach when he runs into Pualani, a beautiful Hawaiian girl; she connects him with her friends, who are hiding out in a townhouse and plotting their next move. After meeting up with a few more survivors and engaging in some fast-paced battle scenes against the feeders, the group decides it must get to Camp Freedom--a group of militaristic survivors off the coast of Florida. From there, the group's bond is sealed; no one will be left behind, and they form an unusual family.The action in "Rise of Chaos" does not stop, and should be very appealing to fans of war novels and horror novels. From a group of pirates who kidnaps women to the League of Islam that has infiltrated and started to conquer the United States, the author maintains the pace and sense of imminent danger throughout the book, which is divided into five "episodes." Mason is a strong and capable hero, and Pualani, equally strong, is a feisty foil as his love interest.  The supporting cast of characters also adds variety and interest to the plot.The author has also deftly created his apocalyptic atmosphere--small and horrific details like bits of blood and brain floating on the tide, or a minefield of buried feeders, evokes not only a feeling of fear and anxiety, but a Florida that you can almost see and smell, full of palpable terror and decay. The villains are heartless and determined to destroy America, and there's no ultimate promise in the book that they won't--other than the determination and optimism of the survivors, who can believe in the future and hope for something better even amidst carnage.While this book was a satisfying read, there were parts that left me wanting more--for instance, I would have cared more about the characters had they been more fully developed, with more backstory about their lives before the disaster struck (with the exclusion of Kalen and Cap'n Tony; their backstory was horrific and certainly made me care about them). I also think the novel would have been more chilling if there had been more description of how certain landmarks of Miami and Florida had been destroyed or desecrated by the feeders. All in all, though, "Rise of Chaos" is an entertaining entry into the zombie-apocalypse genre; it would be a good pick for fans of the movie "28 Days" or the television or graphic novel series "The Walking Dead."
summary: Suspenseful Apocalypse Tale, Heavy on Horror and Bravery

Annie Prudhomme is working as a waitress at the Main Street Diner in her hometown of Marietta. She didn't want to come back here, but she didn't have a choice. Her marriage fell apart when her ex-husband, Davis, was convicted of running a Ponzi scheme on the elderly. Now he is in jail and everything she has is gone except for her family ranch in Montana. One of the first people she meets since her return is her first love, Carson Scott. He lost his wife in an auto accident and is now a widower with a young son, Evan. She broke Carson's heart when she left. Now she is back and he wants her but can he forgive her? Will they get a another chance? Will Evan get the mommy he wants? Katherine Garbera has written an emotional story that explores how we need to forgive our mistakes and should take a chance on love. Annie may be feisty but she is afraid to commit. Conner is a realist who knows that he cares for Annie but will never let his actions hurt his son.  How these two find themselves is a uplifting and romantic story that grabs your heart. I did a minireview of this book on amazon long time ago, but for some reason it dissappeared, so I am reposting the extended version which I did for Wave's reviews site.Have you ever read a book which you kept coming back to no matter how many books you have read after, and wanted to read and reread and savor every word and reread again? Have you ever read a book where you wonder how the writer could transport you to another time so flawlessly and make you want to get to know the characters in person because they felt so amazingly real? I am sure we all have such books which we can gush about endlessly, and this is one of those books for me.This is a historical fiction novel with the touch of m/m romance of the kind which I personally do not see nearly enough in the genre, and of the kind which I crave the most. I have read historicals which, as far as I am concerned, really should not classify as such since the settings were badly researched and/or the characters were contemporary-minded (just placed elsewhere in time). Recently, however, I have read several historicals in a row where the settings were well-researched and the characters felt for me...well, let's just say I felt as if I was reading about aliens from space, so unrelatable the characters felt in the best possible way. And this prompted another reread of this book, where I could not help but hold my breath so badly I wanted my beloved characters to succeed against all odds, survive, and find all the things they are looking for in life.These characters did not feel as if they have contemporary mentality and were just dressed in Roman costumes. Quite the contrary, in fact. One of the most likeable characters in this story wants to buy his mother ten slaves when he becomes a successful soldier, and no, there is absolutely no chance I could like somebody from my own time wanting to do that.  But this author seems to remember that there are at least some character traits that a lot of people could relate to no matter which time we live in, and good guys in this book, while not running to free their slaves or do other anachronistic things, seem to have those traits in abundance -- traits like honor, patriotism, courage, and willingness to help their comrades on the battle field.This is a story which, as blurb tells us, takes place in Rome and one of its provinces. As I said above, this is first and foremost historical fiction about the life in the army of Rome at the time of its glory as much if not more than a m/m romance. The love story between Valerius and Dardanus is definitely there, but it takes a back seat to the rest of the story. This is also a coming of age story for Dardanus, who comes to the home of General Cassius Valerian because his father wants Valerius to take Dardanus under his wing as his ward and maybe later heir.All of the characters in this book are very well fleshed out, and it was a joy to read about Valerius very reluctantly deciding to be Dardanus' sponsor for the summer when he starts his military training and slowly, oh so very slowly, coming to realization that he may actually be attracted to young man. Dardanus was so lovely, a twenty-year-old who dreamt about being a soldier and who is blossoming into a real soldier who fights for Rome, and whose admiration of Valerian turns into love. His friends Iocundus, Ellerius, Iallis and couple others were delightful characters as well.We get treated to very detailed descriptions of Roman army training and battles, but for me it was never boring; in fact, it was so very vivid that I found the pictures the writer painted with words. I was so engrossed, it truly felt as if I was there among the soldiers and was observing the battle field.My only niggle with the book was the fate of the villain and the villain itself. The villain felt to me more pitiful than villainous, although I totally understand how soldiers of Rome would have felt very differently and had no pity. At the same time, while my little contemporary heart liked how the villain was dealt with, and I do get the explanation of how it would have made sense, it did feel to me a little anachronistic.Please be warned, there is one m/f sex scene on page, which, while completely making sense in historical context, may turn some readers off.Highly recommended.
summary: One of my all time favorite historical novels, period

If you're looking for a great resource of money-making ideas to build a legit business, this a an excellent resource to start with. And if one of your top goals is to break free from your 9-5 job, the plethora of low-cost business ideas this book provides will give you both the inspiration and practical advice that any potential entrepreneur could use.What I like most about this book is the author's quick-fire, no-fluff approach in presenting each business idea. After a quick look into what you'd expect from a legitimate, low-cost business, the author explains the benefits of pursuing that business as well as the downside. The author also provides a look into the typical earnings that you might expect to make if successful, and what kind of start up equipment, skills, and knowledge you might need to make it work successfully.The book definitely caters to those who are looking for business ideas that require little start up time and low costs to get off the ground. Most, if not all of these businesses can also be built low cost if you can control your spending and bootstrap your way to success. The ideas presented within are also great as side-gigs even if you don't want to quit your job anytime soon.In short, if you're an aspiring entrepreneur, freedom-seeker, or someone just looking to make a little extra money on the side, this is a great resource to begin with. Choosing what business to go into is extremely important, especially when resources are limited. So having a guide like this will help you to make an informed, thus better decision; which invariably is the mark of a successful businessman or businesswoman.
summary: Good Resource For Choosing a Profitable, Low-Cost Business

reviewText: I gave this 4.25 stars.... Main reason being that I now love Audrey!  In Beautiful Broken Rules, she left kind of a sour taste in our mouths.  We thought she was a psycho... Little did we know her story!Their tragic past with secrets that could have brought them together instead of tearing them apart, feelings that never faded through everything, and their states of being unsure of being together, make this story one that is hard to put down.You will fall in love with Audrey.  Feel sorry for her.  Long for her to and Jace to work things out.  I found myself begging her to just tell him everything... beg for him to be hers.Jace was so heartbroken back in high school... Now you see him as a loving and guarded man.  His feelings for Audrey run deep.  I found myself wanting him to run to her and tell her to forget about the past... force her to try to start new...But we know it isn't that simple... It would make for a boring book.  When tragedy strikes, things really get interesting and heartbreaking.

This was N. Michaels debut book and altogether it was a pretty good one. There was some very hot sex scenes in it and I had a hard time putting it down once I started reading it. There was quite a few grammar errors in it that made it a little difficult to read at some points but other than that it was really good.Katherine Slav grew up spoiled and not having to work for anything. Her father was a very well known neurosurgeon and wanted his daughter to fall in his footsteps and become one also. Katherine was a party girl who loved to go places and shop a lot. She had everything she wanted. That is until her father told her that if she didn't go on to be a neurosurgeon then she would be cut off of all funds. Katherine decided to try to do things on her own so she packed up and moved out. She didn't have much money so she knew she had to find a job quickly if she was going to make it. Fortunately for her her cousin Julia knew the perfect one.Katherine became the assistant to the head CEO of a major company. On her first day she met him Eric Miller. Katherine was expecting a older guy with grey hair but when she met Mr. Miller she knew it was going to be hard working for this sexy man. When they were close to each other they could feel the electricity between them. Eric liked what he saw also but he had a strict rule about dating employees. It was a big no no.Katherine was invited to Miami for a week to help Eric with work. There were two rooms in the suite so they shared it but can that actually keep them apart? Eric has a really bitchy screw buddy Eliza Montgomery who is obviously by his side all the time so she can get noticed and make a name for her self. She is a nasty individual who will do anything to stand in Katherine and Eric's way of being happy. When she shows up in Miami she makes it known to Katherine that Eric will always be hers. That she will be an easy lay and he will come crawling back to her. Will Eric let his rule slip and let things develop with Katherine or will Eliza stand in the way?I really did like this story but I should warn you that it ends with a lot of questions to be answered and book two is not out yet. I can't wait to read more about Katherine and Eric. There is definitely more to this story but I didn't want to give to much away. The ending will shock you.

Jamie O'Connell needs Iona if he is going to have a chance of defeating his enemy.  Jamie is finding that Iona helps make his wolf stronger which gives him a better chance of winning against his enemy.  What he didn't count on was that he might need Iona to make him stronger but he is finding out that he just needs her period and he will do whatever he has to so that he doesn't lose her.Iona has been dead to the world for fifteen years.  Now that she is awake she is finding out that the world as she knows it has changed quite a bit.  Iona had a dark reputation and because of the reputation she is now known as the Blood Queen.  Being asleep for so long she is hungry and she is finding out that the blood of one man is the only thing that will satisfy her, and Jamie really isn't a man, he is a werewolf.Jamie is hiding things from Iona that just might mean she has traded one curse for another.  Jamie and Iona are going to have to find a way to defeat Jamie's enemy and find a way for the two of them to find a happiness that is fast becoming more important than anything else in their world.This another great story in this series.  The story is fast paced and the reader will not want to put this one down until the very last page.  The characters are wonderfully written and full of a depth that makes them come alive for the reader.  The plot is engaging and very well written.

reviewText: I like this one just for the title - cute and fun, just like the story!This series is pretty easy reading including this book which has a gay-for-you theme. Gabe befriends Nick. Gabe supposedly has a finely turned gaydar and recognises that Nick is gay although Nick doesn't think so himself.Nick has always been a bit obsessed with his best friend John, something even his mother picks up on, but he denies his feelings are actually attraction. He continues to deny he can be attracted to men and may be gay, even when he and Gabe start a sexual relationship - it's just guys mucking around together, isn't it?I liked the way Gabe was careful with Nick, letting him lead the way but I also like the way Nick was so into everything and accepting. He didn't have doubts that being physical with Gabe was something that he wanted. It was very cute the way they are relaxed and joking during sex, making it a fun experience. "Yeah, it's different for me, too."..(..).."Y'know, with you having a dick and all." Although these are new experiences for Nick, it is also very new for Gabe as his experience of sex with Nick is like nothing he has experienced before.A bit frustrating as Nick continues to deny his feelings but they get their in the end.

It seems that you either like this work, or you don't.  Personally, Fred Stoller's "My Seinfeld Years" is an enjoyable excursion into another's ups and downs in the entertainment field.  Told with just a touch of tongue-in-cheek, this is a personal foray into some of Stoller's moments as he has endeavored to "break into the business" over the years.  He isn't afraid to reveal his own insecurities, his own frustrations, or to make fun of himself in any situation.  All of that makes this an enjoyable journey into Stoller's life.  "My Seinfeld Years" ends a bit abruptly; so, it was sad that the book ended just as it was getting going!  I would have enjoyed more!It was surprising to learn how many other shows and movies Stoller has been in.  Never the Bride, not quite even a Bride's maid - still he remains a marvelous addition to any cast.  Stoller is "that guy!"  You know; you've seen him everywhere (in shows like "Everybody Loves Raymond," " Friends," and "Murphy Brown" just to name a few ) with his certain blank look like:  "what's happening?"  If you are a follower of TV comedy standup during the 80's and 90's,  you will recognize Stoller.  Perhaps you will recognize him from his role in the "hit,"  "Dumb and Dumber," as he gets "punched out!"  Stoller finally got his big break -- a shot a degree of stability for which he'd always dreamed -- as a staff writer on one of the biggest television shows in history: "Seinfeld."  For the "Seinfeld" fans, it is interesting to read how a script for "Seinfeld" comes together, with each of the four actors having a story line requiring approval by each of them before you could move forward with the script idea.  While Fred was working as a writer during his "Seinfeld Year," it was fascinating to get a brief look behind the television screen; it was also interesting to follow his discussion of scripts which you remember seeing on the show, which includes one developed by Stoller himself.This is a great read for any Seinfeld fan.  It is an enjoyable piece of comic autobiography, making for an enjoyable afternoon read, which is over far too quickly.  For the price of $1.99 for the Kindle addition, what do you what, muffin tops only?
summary: For $1.99: "What Do You Want, Muffin Tops Only?"

Overall:  5 starsPlot/Storyline:  5 starsWhat would you do if you read obituaries for you and your spouse in the newspaper? If you're Peter Talbott, you would go to your own funeral, of course. Little did Peter know that that act of satisfying his curiosity would lead to a terrifying cross country chase with people trying to kill him everywhere he went.The Undertaker, like most good suspense thrillers, hooked me on page one. And that was where the character known as the Undertaker was introduced to the reader in one of the most chilling opening scenes that I've read in a while.I've read a number of action thrillers that were first rate until they ended with a disappointing climax--it was either too easy to see where the story was going, or the climax was too convenient or too contrived. But I enjoyed the climax of The Undertaker. It caught me almost completely off guard, and it was a satisfying end to the build-up of the story. Granted, the revealing of one character's true identity was somewhat improbable, but this was fiction, after all, and it did make for a great story.One of my favorite big-name authors is Nelson DeMille, who is a master at ramping up the tension to gut-wrenching levels. In my opinion, William F. Brown is very nearly in the same league with DeMille for writing taut, suspenseful scenes.Character Development:  5 starsThe story was narrated in the first person by Peter Talbott, a software engineer who had recently lost his beloved wife and soul mate Terri to cancer. Talbott was a smart, likeable character. Still in mourning for his deceased wife, he was trying to get on with his life, but with little success. Everything changed, however, when he met Sandy Kasmarek, a sassy lady whose no-good, cheating husband had been murdered. Although the two had absolutely nothing in common, the chemistry was there, and with Peter's dry wit and sarcasm and Sandy's tough cynicism, it was fun watching the sparks fly as an unlikely romance blossomed amid the chaos and carnage of the pair's desperate flight from the people who wanted them dead.Peter and Sandy were the good guys. There were plenty of bad guys--frighteningly evil and absolutely ruthless--but it wasn't always obvious which side of the law some characters were on until the dramatic climax.In my mind, I kept visualizing younger versions of Harrison Ford and Holly Hunter playing Peter and Sandy. And yes, The Undertaker would make a great movie.Writing style:  5 starsThe Undertaker was a near-perfect combination of suspenseful action and colorful, often witty dialogue. The descriptions of the various locations and people encountered by the on-the-run Peter and Sandy were vivid and realistic.I noticed a number of punctuation and spelling errors in the version submitted for review, but they weren't frequent enough to distract from the writing.The Undertaker is a novel with 6,333 Kindle locations. Lending and text-to-speech are enabled.
summary: A lot like a Nelson DeMille thriller... and that's good!

reviewText: Bravo to Bailey Bradford for bringing the "hidden issues" in this world out into the light. She writes this story with sensitivity and honesty.John is an average gay man, goes to work, comes home and tries to cope with his bouts of severe and debilitating depression. With medicine and therapy, he thinks he's doing a great job of overcoming his illness. He no longer hits the bars, no longer has the indiscriminate sex. He hasn't dated in two years.Then he meets Benji, who confuses the heck out of him with his hot and cold attitude, and lack of normal boundaries. He's drawn to Benji, but what does Benji want? John wants more than just sex, but is it so wrong to take what Benji's offered so far?John starts to realize what he thought was coping wasn't living; he was just going through the motions. That he's isolated himself and maybe it's time to go out and get back to living life.The characters in this story are very real people. John gives a very good look into the life of someone who is dealing with a mental illness and how it affects all aspects of their lives.This is a serial novel done in parts, so next for me is part two.Reviewed by Laurie Pfor TheRomanceReviews.com

reviewText: This short story is part of my RARE Event reading challenge. The author's writing style hooks the reader into the story so easily that I didn't even realized it was ending till I keep trying to turn the page on my Kindle and it said 100%. I was so deep into the story that I didn't want it to end.Whispers in the Dark is the perfect reading after a hard day at work or school when the only thing you want to do is to get lost in a story but one that wouldn't keep you up all night. I really recommend it.
summary: Perfect read after a long day

Young couples, Baley and Shane, got more than they bargained for when they bought their new home. The home isn't just big and beautiful, it also comes with a secret hidden tower! Baley stumbled upon the tower's entrance by accident and then Shane followed her in. Right that minute, an instant sensual spark ignited between them. They couldn't stop touching each other and they couldn't seem to get enough action. While hitting the sack is not new to them, the intensity is. Is there something magical or mystical with the tower? Baley and Shane intends to find out.Sandra Ross outdid herself with Naughty In The Tower. The author never lets you down when it comes to kinky- hot scenes (pun intended). The allure of the mysterious tower room will draw the readers to turn the page faster. It will make you scratch your head wondering what kind of history the tower has.Naughty in the Tower is a light read . Don't expect a long novella story with this book. I consider that as a good thing since I never really liked reading for more than 4 hours. While this book is a bit short, it does cover all the grounds of a naughty erotica. You won't lack for action here. Every page is filled with detailed scenes that will make your senses tingle in a very good way!I would suggest this book to those looking for mystery and plenty of action! It's a must- read on your day- off! It's loaded with sensual scenes without being too heavy on the info and details.

Contained in this book are short illustrated chapters on many. many colors of horses. Did you know that a grey horse must have at least one parent that is grey and a grey foal is never born grey?!A cremello has pink skin, blue eyes and cream colored coat with white mane and tail.Brindle is a rare color pattern in horses but does occur. If you have never seen a Leopard Appaloosa, there's one in here!Did you know that 'splashed white' horses are commonly deaf?At the end of the book there is a basic horse diagram.SO if you are wanting to learn about all the different horse colors then this book is definitely one to get BUT if you are looking for more details on breeds, horse characteristics etc then you probably do not want this one.

Unrequited Love, Victim, Survivor, Fearful.... Those are just a few of the terms that are associated with Brooke Bennet. Famous singer of duo group Nocturne until she was kidnapped by a psychopath who stole her sense of security and passion for life and music. Five years later, in The Waiting Game, Cameron Dexter comes to Brooke's rescue once again on the day that Spinks, her kidnapper, is released from prison. He convinces her to go into hiding with him until Spinks can be locked up for good. But Brooke is tired of being the things that make her weak. She wants to fight and the only way to do that is to draw Spinks out and make his move sooner rather than later.Sexy bodyguard, Cam, goes out of his mind trying to protect Brooke, the woman he loves, as well as capturing Spinks. Brooke is jumping out of her skin to feel safe again and to get Cam to see her as more than just a job.With the stakes so high, time seeming so short and never-ending all at once, who will come out on top? The smart and savvy psycho? Or Brooke and Cam, the edgy duo?Giving this book 4  stars, Eve Devon delivers a book that will put you on the edge of your seat, dragging you in with her believable and worthy characters. Her writing throws off the most graphic images that puts you right there within the story.(I received an ARC for my honest review and this is my honest to goodness, straight from the heart review!)www.caretocommentanne.blogspot.com

First, the guy on the cover got me.  I got the books for that reason.  Then I started reading.  I LOVED each story.  There are 3 brothers, all different but coming from the same family.  Reid the oldest, a stuffed shirt lawyer falls for the wild child Jenny.  Of course, she brings him around and you just love them both.  Then brother Matt, issues of his own but when he meets Janet he starts to see life in a different light.  The youngest brother, Grant, race car driver, dare devil, risk his life at every turn until a near fatal crash.  Then he meets Carrie and she changes him and his life.  I LOVED each story.  The story was about these characters, there was no villain, etc. just the story between two people and how they came together.  It was a delicious read.  I couldn't wait to get to the next brother.  I thought the stories were just right, long enough.  I am just a reader, I don't have a clue how to write a book or edit one.  I just look for what entertains me and leaves me feeling good when it is over.  Usually, I will think about the characters for days afterwards wondering what their lives are like.  As a reader, I highly recommend these books.  I loved them.-

A trail of paranormal bread crumbs led me gently into a refreshingly different, often chilling, twist on the afterlife--or "between," at any rate. A great read if you're in the mood for something mysterious that isn't a mystery, romantic that isn't a romance, and chilling that isn't horror. Can't really say more about the plot without spoilers (yeah, it's that kind of book :>)). I loved the relationship between Lucy and her best friend. The pets were a nice addition, too. Can't say much about the other major (paranormal) characters (again, without spoilers), other than to say they were developed and complex. The town, its inhabitants, and other minor and minor-ish characters were also richly drawn--as were the trips to the medieval past--all making the story feel authentic.

This is the next book in the series about Devine Designs.  Elizabeth and Logan are now engaged and moving forward on their plans for designing Haven.  When we meet everyone again, they are staying at a small hotel.  Logan and Elizabeth, Ariel and Garrett, Nancy and Jason, Helen and Benjamin, Barbara, and Craig.  Everyone is a couple except Barbara and Craig.  Barbara is hurting from her divorce and, of course, Craig is a Dom.  When Barbara says some mean things, Craig takes her to task.  Barbara is outraged, but the few spanks that Craig gives her starts her thinking.  Over the weekend, Barbara and Craig get to know one another better and finally, Barbara goes to Craig for her spanking.  But, she also feels that she needs a daddy, so they start doing a little age-play.I really liked this book.  First of all, it is a continuation of what happened in the first book.  We find out about how Elizabeth and Logan’s relationship is moving along.  We also learn a little about Ariel and Garrett.  I think the next book will be focused on this couple.  We also have some explanations.  Barbara is asking questions and the other submissives are explaining why their relationships are the way they are.  They explain that they gave their dominants the power to discipline them and that they can always take it back.  It was very enlightening.  I give this 5 stars!

Things can get very heated when in a locked room, especially when you have a devious guy like Garreth around. Garreth knows how he feels and is tired of hiding it but he knows that nothing can come of this unless Jenna is willing to take a leap of faith for him.Both characters have such great chemistry; they fight, they love, and they fight so more...to say they have a firey relationship is putting it lightly. reviewText: This book is so good! As soon as I started, it was so hard to put down! In the beginning, when Anna and Jake were first reunited, it seemed like from what happened between them there, Anna would just easily give in to Jake. The resistance she ended up showing made it so much more entertaining to follow. I loved Jake! Protective, charming, understanding, etc. It would be impossible for me not to fall for him. I always love books where the characters have disturbed pasts that they've kept hidden. Uncovering those secrets kept my eyes glued to the pages. There were so many scenes that I couldn't resist reading multiple times; the scenes involving alcohol, the battles between Jake and his brother, and of course, the steamy scenes! So good! The only negative I found would be that at times, I lost track of who was saying what, so I would have to retrace my steps to try and figure it out. Overall, it was great, though! I wanted to reach the end to see what happened, but I wasn't ready for it to be over!

The Barker's Dozen - Reminiscences of an Early Police Dog by English author Robert Warr is a delightful series of twelve stories from Victorian England as recounted by Snuffles, a Springer spaniel belonging to Scotland Yard Inspector Thompson. With illustrations in the vein of Strand artist Sidney Paget for Sherlock Holmes, this reader soon felt like she was caught up in a 19th century detective novel.Using deductive abilities in the style of Sherlock Holmes, Inspector Thompson, aided more than just a little by his staunch aide-de-camp, Snuffles, solves crimes that confound the local constabulary.  The stories are told from Snuffles point of view, who assists his master by consulting with other animals literally on the `scene of the crime.'  From an assortment of cats, a fox, a swan, and nefarious others, Snuffles brings to light clues that would no doubt go unnoticed by his less linguistically-gifted master.  Not lacking for opinions, Snuffles regales his audience with dry witticisms such as describing a cat as having `all the moral fiber of wet bread,' and designating an alleged murder involving a magpie as `murder most fowl.'The Barker's Dozen - Reminiscences of an Early Police Dog is in the venue of a stroll through a fictional detective novel and a visual treat.  Sherlock Holmes fans...and animal lovers...take note.
summary: A fun read and a  visual treat

reviewText: This book is not an easy, breezy contemporary romance. It's a well written story of one young lady's triumph over years of hidden abuses and the soldier who rescued her, believed her, and saved her from her horrible situation and how they fell in love. The story takes place over several years and deals with some hard issues like rape, self mutilation/cutting, unwanted pregnancy, and parental abuse. It is not for the faint of heart, but it also deals with therapy, healing and finding yourself as an individual, independent adult. I gave it half a star off for some editing problems and minor formatting issues. Otherwise, I recommend this book, and will be looking for the companion novel about 'the Good Sister'.Heat factor hot.

Better than Perfect, is one of the most endearing romance reads I've read in a long while.I loved the way the MC grew in maturity and became her own person, as the read progressed.Starting as a bit of a lost soul, with the death of her parents in a horrible accident, Karlie finds herself drifting through life, without much purpose, or knowing her place and what she wants to do with her life. Awful tragic events then lead her to her becoming the guardian to two adolescent twin boys, who don't have anyone else. And although its not what she ever envisaged happening to her, she is drawn to the role and takes on the responsibility, fighting all those around her who are opposed to the arrangement. And along the way she is given the chance to find herself and to fall in love.What I loved the most about this read, was the authentic characters and the way the plot unfolded in unexpected ways, never tied up neatly in a bow, which for me, made the read more realistic and believable, and had me clutching to each and every word.So if you want to be bound up in the lives, and loves, of great characters and if you are a true romantic, and love a book to snuggle up with in some cosy corner, then Better than Perfect is definitely the read for you.Highly recommended

reviewText: Again, another action-packed thriller from Russell Blake. I'm beginning to really like El Rey and hope there'll be more stories about him. In “The Card Counter” by James Kipling, Devon Walker has his hands full dealing with his ex-wife and trying to be a better father to his children.  A Homicide Detective, he is also investigating several recent murders.  As the body count rises and a pattern emerges, he soon realizes that they have a serial killer on their hands.  Can the killer be stopped - before all of his targets are dead?The Card Counter is a page-turning murder mystery.  The plot is fast and flows smoothly, with lots of suspense as you become invested in the well-developed characters and storyline.  Believable and realistic dialog by the characters help propel the story to its conclusion.There are a few spelling / grammar issues – but nothing that distracted me from the story.All-in-all, a VERY good read and I highly recommend this book to everyone that likes a good murder mystery!
summary: A nice murder mystery - I could not put this book down!

Six Naughty Nights was filled with lots of fun & sexy naughtiness!The sex & role playing between Toby & Esther was off-the-charts explosive; all thanks to the Naughty Nights game provided by their good friend, Faith. But, seriously grab a fan or cold drink when reading. That's just my fair warning to readers :)I really enjoyed this read along with the characters. Toby was such a sexy guy *sigh* and he was 10 times that in the bedroom especially when his dominant side came out to play ;)But aside from the that, I really liked his character: handsome, sensitive, sweet, and caring. Of course, he also had no hesitation stepping into the father role. I always love a man who can man up.As for Esther, I liked her as well...for the most part at least. To be honest, I had kind of a love/hate relationship with her. I got quite put off with her character due to her decisions which I thought were quite selfish. However, being in her shoes and from her reasoning, I could understand why she made the choices she did.The story also flowed smoothly and I thought that the pacing was just perfect. It didn't drag for me and it had a nice pace throughout.Overall, Serenity Woods has penned a very enjoyable & entertaining story. The story and characters pulled me in immediately from the first opening scene of the earthquake until the very last beautiful scene in Faith's living room. Although I've had to stop at numerous times in the story due to life's demands, I never forgot the story or lost sight of it. Every time picking up the story from where I left off, I connected immediately with the story again and it felt like I had never put it down.So, yes, Six Naughty Nights was a winner in my book. It was a fun contemporary romance packed with great characters, scorching hot sex scenes and a feel good factor that left me smiling & satisfied in the end.*Disclaimer: I received an ARC from the author in exchange for an honest review.

I absolutely hate to use the cliche, "I couldn't put it down", but honestly it was applicable with this book. Desley, the heroine, was very real to me. When we first meet her, she is not a woman with superhuman emotional strength which is what helped me to relate to her. But she was stubborn, which also made me relate to her. I was surprised by how much I enjoyed the budding romance between her and Fergus, and on top of it all, the murder mystery kept me on edge till the very end.  I can't wait to start Ms. Tyley's next book!

"An Emotional Affair" actually had me rather hot under the collar for much of the book. While I didn't agree with either Mark or Cheryl becoming emotionally involved with other people, I was mostly mad at Cheryl for how she treated Mark. The man definitely developed quite a bit of patience where she was concerned, because if I were him I'd have probably left her a long time ago. She was all the time screaming at him, and man, wtf was up with the violence?! Where does the girl get off thinking she can just get way with hitting him like that? Even I, a woman, have to say that after being punched in the face, Mark would have been well within his rights to slap her back. More lies, backstabbing, and manipulation going on in this book, and if a story can get me as worked up as this one did, it's definitely a good one!

The story is interesting and moves with lots of drama and action, but I could not see the connections between characters and chapters and I could not tell most of them apart ... except for the woman. There was only one woman, which I find rather annoying in an adventure story. None of the characters were clearly described or introduced, and I could not tell many of them apart, especially when they just showed up in chapters that moved from one part of the earth to another with no clear description except for the chapter heads. To add to the confusion, some of the characters were called by two different names at times, with no explanation why. It took me a few chapters to figure that out. Ordinarily I wouldn't have bothered, but the author might want to know she needs to do some work on her character formation to make her stories more powerful.

This was one of those books that I really didn't want to put down. I found the concept of human brainwaves on a radio frequency to be quite entertaining. The characters were wickedly evil and each twisted in their own perverse way. The series is divided into 8 books, but they are not stand alone books. You would need to read them all from the beginning to have a grasp of the craziness that is going on in Asylum. If you are a fan of American Horror Story you should like this book. Although some of the experiments and treatments that were going on in the institution were totally crazy and unbelievable I found the book to be creepily fun and a real page turner. The author gave us enough background into the character's lives and past to be interested in them. I did not find the editing deficiencies to be distracting from this good fun read. Although I got the book for free I would not hesitate to buy it for a reasonable amount and would definitely pay for a sequel. I would like to find out someday what becomes of "nurse Perry"!!!!

It is very entertaining to see to what lengths Tony goes to build up his nerve to ask Nikki out.  The love affair is something to write home about.  These two people who have denied themselves the pleasures of the flesh for so long are not wasting any time.  While reading these scenes, I could not help but wonder who would have the heart attack first... the characters or myself.  Turn your fans on and cool down before reading these scenes.  Either that or keep plenty of ice on hand.

This is a problem that many of us have, but don't know we suffer from it. Not until we move to a new place or do spring cleaning do we realize how stuck with our possessions we are. Dr. Andrew M. Goodman delivers here a novel book that every single family can benefit from reading and applying to our lives. I think this is a great first step in making even grander changes in our lives for the better.Un-Clutter is exactly what the doctor ordered! You don't have to be a hoarder or a pack rat to benefit from removing the clutter from your life. Personally, I started small using some of the simpler tips in the book and became more confident to make drastic changes. I'm happier for the better. Not only is my home better off, but my mental state is new and fresh. I think my memory has improved, my mood has lightened, and I finally know the exact location of all of my belongings. Un-clutter! 66 Routes to a Freer Life was one of my best book decisions.
summary: One of my best book decisions

reviewText: This was a really great book. Avery was about 14 years old when her mother just disappeared. Her mother was just so many great things. To Avery, she was happiness, light, and most of her happy memories all rolled into one. When Taylah disappeared the family was just torn apart. Avery's father was always a workaholic but he became more withdrawn after that day and her brother Liam became so angry and bitter. He tried to forget it all by drinking heavily, doing drugs, and having sex with women. Avery has survived by dancing all the time. She wants to be a ballet dancer and so she puts all of her time into that. She's in a relationship with a man (Jacob) that doesn't love her and really doesn't treat her well. He is only with her so he can get her fathers company and money. Nate is a professional motorcross rider. He's married and has a little girl. His marriage hasn't been happy in a very long time, if it was ever happy at all. He's miserable but he's scared that if he leaves his wife then she will take his daughter away from him. She keeps putting her daughter in dangerous situations but only cares about using her to control Nate. This is a story about an affair but there is so much more to it than that. I'm not saying an affair is right because it so isn't. But sometimes things happen because some people can't stay away from one another. They can only find happiness with one person and they try to find some happiness in it.Avery is a woman that had a mother disappear and it tore her apart and her family. She's just trying to survive and get through her life. Nate is stuck in a marriage that he is miserable in with a woman that doesn't care about anyone but he loves his daughter enough to stay.This book is definitely worth reading. I would love to find out more about Liam, Kelly, and maybe Keanu. They would definitely be great books to read.
summary: Sometimes Closure Helps But Sometimes It Destroys

I have to admit, i didn't like the first book.What prompted me to buy the 2nd I can only blame on the lovely cover and the intriguing excerpts.In the first book Claire realizes that her husband/love of her life has impregnated her best friend. Claire divorces him moves to Sanfran with her twin teenagers to a job she hates and ends up working under (not directly) a young, model-hot, billionaire who pursues her like a crazy madman. There's the typical push pull between the two and the issue of her being older than him. they work out their issues with cartoonish sex and a grovel scene at the end. it was meh but then I read that there's a sequel with the ex returning. . . uh oh. . . must read about the ex!I have to admit that I Love a book where an ex realizes the error of their ways and tries to come back. This book has that but delivers in an unsatisfactory way.The second book has the same problems of the first book but it somehow got worse! Claire is still obsessively upset about her ex-husband and ex-best friend. I know that what they did was terrible but it was over 5 years ago and she has a new billionaire man who has sex with her 80 times a day! Why are they even a blip in her radar? She should be instead be focusing on:1. Why her fiance is spoiling her daughters rotten and turning them into greedy super brats. In one scene one of her daughters cheekily asks him why he's only sending 300 dollars a week, like it's a pittance. Is that supposed to be funny? They sound like opportunistic future gold-diggers.2. Why he is having her followed by security guards. They report to him her every move.3. Her unlimited funds megawedding that had to be pulled off in 3 months "or else",4. Why he's intercepting and destroying her mail5. Why he's trying to sabotage her new design career by throwing temper tantrums every time she works late. He's a billionaire, he of all people should know how much you have to work to be successful.6. Why she and Jonathan never get caught having sex in public places! They have sex all the time EVERYWHERE. Hey! I have to eat at some of these places! Have some courtesy or hire someone to follow you to wipe down all areas with Lysol.The Ex coming back into the picture was also a big let down. I want at least the illusion that she has a difficult choice between the two. Instead the author went the easy route and just villainized the ex making Jonathan the clear choice.The book was a disappointment but the cover, i will reiterate, is lovely.
